title: Combat & Loadouts: Foundation
topic: Weapons, gadgets, classes, damage and ballistics

text:
WARDOGS has no fixed class selection at spawn. Each life, a player spends cash at a vendor to build a custom loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles, starting from $10,000 [1]. Experience is earned on role tracks that gate which items can be bought. The Season 1 changelog named Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [2]; the Update 0.2.0 patch notes (posted 14 Oct 2026) instead list Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot and Driver tracks plus a "WARDOG Progression Track" [11]. The notes do not say what happened to the "Career" label (see Open Questions).

The developer's stance on realism is a middle line: the store page says "tactical gunplay" in About This Game and, under the Early Access current-state answer, "Realistic gunplay balanced for gameplay rather than simulation" (live capture 2026-10-08) [1], the February 2026 FAQ calls the game "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game" with "Grounded Gunplay" as an Early Access feature [6], and a May 2026 post lists "real-world ballistics" among its pillars [7]. No official weapon list, damage value or ballistic parameter has been published. The official Steam text for the 9 Sep Season 1 changelog [2], the 30 Sep update 0.1.2 [3] and the 2 Oct balance hotfix [4] is the Season 1 baseline.

Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, released 15 Oct 2026 [12]; notes posted 14 Oct [11]) is the first official source to publish combat numbers: calibre base-damage reductions (.308 -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 cal -16%), Level 3 armor and helmet damage reduction lowered 55% to 50%, Level 4 lowered 65% to 60%, suppression rebuilt with Level 3 and Level 4 helmets reducing it by 68% and 80%, a battery-powered Infrared Range Finder (about 80 s per battery), a new Molotov, four new weapons (TCX-SPR, PP-19 Bizon, Evo-3 Ultra, M14), parachute and Medical Bag changes [11]. Numbers are owned by damage-ballistics-and-balance, gadgets-armor-and-equipment, weapons-catalogue and price-tables-season-1. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot, so nothing later is known here.

Document confidence is Medium: the structural model, role tracks, repricing and the 0.2.0 balance changes are official, but absolute per-weapon damage is still unpublished and pre-0.2.0 weapon details rest on beta-era press and player-reported guides (see weapons-catalogue).

text:
- Loadouts are bought with cash each life from a vendor; players start with $10,000 and cash persists between matches (Steam page, checked 2026-10-08) [1].
- There is no spawn-time class pick. Six role tracks (Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot) were named in the official changelog of 9 Sep 2026 [2]; the 0.2.0 notes (14 Oct 2026) name Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot, Driver and a "WARDOG Progression Track" [11].
- Official gunplay wording on the store page: "tactical gunplay" (About This Game) and "Realistic gunplay balanced for gameplay rather than simulation" (Early Access current state) (live capture 2026-10-08) [1]; "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game" and "Grounded Gunplay" (18 Feb 2026) [6]; "real-world ballistics" (21 May 2026) [7].
- Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep 2026, live for the 10 Sep launch) slowed role XP between levels 10 and 20, moved many unlocks and repriced hammers, scopes, the FOB and vehicles; the developer says each season gets a different XP curve and item order [2].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) made revive validity server authoritative, scaled buildable-destruction rewards by build progress, barred throwables from enclosed vehicle seats and fixed a Havoc bug that raised damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire [3].
- Balance hotfix (2 Oct 2026): IR Rangefinders were disabled in the vendor until Season 02, when they will need batteries, and the CIWS now destroys a Havoc in about 6 s instead of 12 s [4].
- Update 0.2.0 (notes 14 Oct 2026, live 15 Oct): Level 3 armor and helmets 55% to 50% damage reduction, Level 4 65% to 60%; Level 3 and Level 4 helmets reduce suppression by 68% and 80%; the Infrared Range Finder runs on batteries (about 80 s of active use); a Molotov is added; the Medical Bag durability rises 100 to 150 [11][12].
- Calibre base-damage cuts in 0.2.0: .308 Winchester -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 Cal -16% (percentages only; absolute damage per weapon is still unpublished) [11].
- No official absolute damage, headshot or bullet-drop table exists; the beta-era claim that drop and travel time are modelled is press-reported only [9].

text:
Covers infantry combat, weapon categories, gadgets and equipment, the role/progression system as it relates to loadouts, the documented damage/ballistics model, and how loadout purchasing ties to the in-match economy. Game version: Early Access Season 02, Update 0.2.0 (15 Oct 2026), with Season 1 (0.1.2 and the 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes) kept as dated history. Official posts after 2026-10-15 are not in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

Excluded: vehicle combat detail (see vehicles-outposts-foundation), mode rules (gameplay-modes-foundation), full economy mechanics (economy-foundation) and per-weapon, per-item and per-price tables, which live in the depth documents listed under Related Documents.

text:
- **Loadout**: the set of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles bought for one life [1].
- **Role track**: a per-role XP progression that gates item purchases. Season 1 names: Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [2]. Update 0.2.0 notes headings: Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot, Driver [11].
- **WARDOG Progression Track**: an official 0.2.0 heading for general unlocks (for example Level 3 Helmet & Armor at level 70, Sport Parachute at level 34) [11]; the guide term "WARDOG Level" is player-reported [10].
- **Rebuy Last Loadout**: vendor button that, since 0.2.0, pre-populates the equipment vendor UI with the last loadout so items can be added or removed before purchase [11].

text:
- Each player starts with $10,000 and buys a custom loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles each life; cash persists between matches (Steam page, 2026-10-08) [1].
- The store page's Early Access current-state answer lists "Realistic gunplay balanced for gameplay rather than simulation" (live capture 2026-10-08) [1].
- The store page's Mature Content Description says "Wardogs contains killing with weapons and melee combat", so melee combat exists; no melee weapon roster or stats are published (live capture 2026-10-08) [1].
- Teamwork earns cash, including reviving squadmates, transporting friendlies to the zone and controlling the objective [1].
- The store page describes "tactical gunplay and combined arms combat with building and destruction mechanics", sniping with a ghillie suit, rocket launchers that destroy apartment blocks and buildable forward operating bases [1].
- Role tracks named in the official Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep 2026): Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot [2]. The changelog also shows items moving between tracks (Heavy Tank from Career 35 to Driver 35; Music Tape H from Pilot 28 to Driver 23) [2].
- Update 0.2.0 notes (14 Oct 2026) describe Assault as "the role for attacking enemy bases"; C4 and the Remote Detonator move into it and a Molotov Cocktail (level 13) joins it [11].
- Season 1 changelog (title "Pre-Load Live & Season 1 Changelog", posted 9 Sep 2026 UTC) states that "each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" [2].
- Update 0.1.2 is dated 30 Sep 2026 [3]. On 2 Oct 2026 two separate official posts appeared: a hotfix notice for 08:00 UTC about "minor security and stability issues" [5] and the balance hotfix on IR Rangefinders and the CIWS [4].
- Season 02 / Update 0.2.0 went live on 15 Oct 2026 ("We have now released Update 0.2.0. Servers are back online") [12]. The 0.1.2 post had said it would bring "new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [3][8]; the notes confirm new weapons, a Molotov, helmet and Range Finder changes, vehicles, buildables and a rain weather preset [11].
- Weapons added in 0.2.0: TCX-SPR (7.62x39mm assault rifle), PP-19 Bizon (9x19mm SMG), Evo-3 Ultra (.308 Win LMG), M14 (.308 Win marksman rifle) [11]. Prices and levels are in weapons-catalogue and price-tables-season-1.
- The 0.2.0 notes do not address death-cost rules or a progression wipe.

text:
## Loadout selection and economy

Loadouts are purchased at a vendor each life [1]. The Season 1 posts do not describe the death cost; those details are player-reported (see death-penalty-and-rebuy) [10]. The 0.2.0 notes confirm a "Rebuy Last Loadout" button and remove the old placeholder UI [11]; they do not state any death cost, and do not mention a progression wipe. A guide dated 17 Sep 2026 reports that a level requirement only unlocks the option to buy, after which a one-time unlock payment is needed and the item then has a normal per-life vendor price [10] (player-reported). The official changelog does list vendor prices separately from track prices, which is consistent with that two-price model: for example Large Hammer has a vendor price ($1,600 to $2,400) and a Support track price ($25,000 to $75,000) [2].

Official equipment-space change: 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables take up more loadout space since the Season 1 changelog [2]. Per-item unlock costs from guides (medical gear, sidearms, parachute) are in gadgets-armor-and-equipment and weapons-catalogue rather than repeated here.

## Weapon categories and notable weapons

Official text names very few weapons: the Deagle (Career 90 to 85), the PP-19 50-round drum magazine (Medic 33 to 29), 762x54mm AP and 556mm AP ammo, and Recon 6-10x MRAD and MOA scopes [2]. Rocket launchers appear on the store page [1]. Everything else is beta-era press or player-reported [9][10].

A beta press table grouped the vendor into assault rifles, SMGs, shotguns, LMGs, marksman rifles, sniper rifles, a compound bow, sidearms and launchers (RPG-7, MAAWS, 9K333 Verba surface-to-air), recorded 33 weapons with 37 expected at launch, and said prices were not confirmed as final [9]. Those values predate the Season 1 repricing [2] and are stale; the full roster with prices and levels is in weapons-catalogue (confidence Low there).

## Roles and progression

Official: the Season 1 changelog names six tracks, Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot, and lists unlock moves under Career, Medic, Support and Driver [2]. The beta press mapping of kills to four tracks (assault rifles and sidearms, SMGs, shotguns/LMGs/launchers, marksman/sniper/bow) used the guide name "Assault" and predates launch [9]; whether Career is a rename of that track is not stated officially (see progression-and-role-tracks). Guides add that Driver and Pilot are levelled by vehicles [10] (player-reported).

Season 1 changes (changelog posted 9 Sep 2026) [2]:

- Role-track XP requirements rose sharply in the middle band: level 6 from 8,750 to 9,250, level 10 from 25,000 to 35,000, level 15 from 54,750 to 110,000, level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000, level 25 from 192,000 to 325,000; levels below 6 unchanged, and the curve flattens from level 35 onward (level 50 is 1,000,000). The developer says median players at 20 to 25 hours will be around level 20.
- Career unlock moves: Deagle 90 to 85, Artillery Tank 55 to 90, Sports Parachute 36 to 35, Large Backpack 56 to 55, 762x54mm AP 83 to 82, 556mm AP 85 to 83. Medic: PP-19 50-round drum 33 to 29. Support: Large Hammer 7 to 8. Driver: Heavy Tank now Driver 35, plus nine other vehicle level moves.
- Recon scopes repriced: 6-10x MRAD $25,000 to $40,000; 6-10x MOA $30,000 to $45,000.
- Support track prices: Medium Hammer unlock $10,000 to $25,000; Large Hammer unlock $25,000 to $75,000. Vendor prices: Large Hammer $1,600 to $2,400; Forward Operating Base $2,500 to $7,500.
- Air vehicle player-kill XP lowered from 300 to 250.

Update 0.2.0 (notes 14 Oct 2026) reversed the Season 1 slowdown: for example level 10 35,000 to 25,000, level 20 250,000 to 111,500, level 50 1,500,000 to 1,150,000 [11]. The "from" figures in the 0.2.0 notes differ from some Season 1 figures quoted above (for example level 15 110,000 matches, level 25 365,000 differs from 325,000, level 50 1,500,000 differs from 1,000,000); this document does not reconcile them (see progression-and-role-tracks). Reaching level 20 is stated to take less than half the Season 1 playtime [11]. Most attachments moved to earlier levels or new tracks [11].

Full ladders and price lists are in progression-unlock-tables and price-tables-season-1.

## Damage and ballistics

Official 0.2.0 combat-balance changes (notes 14 Oct 2026, live 15 Oct) [11]; full detail in damage-ballistics-and-balance:

- Calibre base damage: .308 Winchester -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 Cal -16%, applying to infantry and vehicle weapons alike.
- Assault rifle body shots do slightly less damage; LMG body damage now matches assault rifles; sniper hit-location damage was increased to offset the base reduction; DMR headshots and upper-body hits are slightly weaker.
- Armor and helmets: Level 3 damage reduction 55% to 50%; Level 4 65% to 60%. Scout Rifle headshots one-shot a target with no helmet and need two on a Level 1 helmet.
- Suppression was rebuilt around per-weapon falloff curves; Level 3 helmets reduce suppression by 68% and Level 4 by 80%.
- 12 gauge slug and compound bow damage against armor now scale with armor tier.

The notes give percentages, not absolute damage per shot, so no per-weapon damage table exists officially. Before 0.2.0 no official values existed at all. The earlier official statements are positional: "tactical gunplay" and "Realistic gunplay balanced for gameplay rather than simulation" on the store page (live capture 2026-10-08) [1], "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game" and "Grounded Gunplay" [6], and "real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" in a May 2026 post whose substance is in a video not captured as text [7]. Press from the closed beta reports that real bullet drop and travel time are modelled and that weapon weights differ (for example AMR 50 12.5 kg, LMGs 7.5 kg) [9]; this is not confirmed by the developer.

Official Season 1 combat-relevant fixes: update 0.1.2 fixed a Havoc bug causing increased damage from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire and fixed buildable "crit spots" reappearing in the same place or jumping to the far side of a structure, so they now favour a spot reachable from where the player stands [3]. The 2 Oct hotfix halved the CIWS kill time on a Havoc (about 12 s to about 6 s), which the developer calls correcting an overcorrection in the previous patch [4]. See damage-ballistics-and-balance for the full record.

## Gadgets and utility

Update 0.2.0 adds a Molotov (thrown incendiary; impact damage plus burn damage over time; throw overarm or underarm; burns destructible foliage; weaker in rain), makes the Infrared Range Finder battery-powered (about 80 s of active use per battery; drains faster if toggled on and off quickly), gives the Level 4 Helmet muffled audio, muffled proximity chat, restricted field of view and sprint fog-over, raises Medical Bag durability from 100 to 150, and changes parachute opening behaviour and prices (Basic $100 to $500, Sport $1,000 to $700) [11]. 30mm cannon ammo now takes a 2x2 slot and backpack stacks are capped at 50 [11]. Explosives and placeables can no longer be used from enclosed vehicle seats [11]. Details are in gadgets-armor-and-equipment.

Officially named in Season 1: ghillie suit, rocket launchers and forward operating bases [1]; grenades, smoke and C4 as throwables, parachutes, backpacks, flares, hammers and IR Rangefinders [2][3][4]. Player-reported: first aid kit, defibrillator, adrenaline pen and an Emergency Resuscitator [10]; see gadgets-armor-and-equipment. The 2 Oct post title says "IR Goggles" while its body says "IR Rangefinders"; whether these are one item is not stated [4]. The 0.2.0 notes use "Infrared Range Finder" [11].

title: Damage, Ballistics & Balance Changes
topic: Damage model, ballistics, hit registration, and the balance-change history

text:
The developer still has not published a damage table, ballistic table or hit-registration description for WARDOGS. What changed with Update 0.2.0 (patch notes 14 Oct 2026, release 15 Oct 2026) is that the "Combat Balance" section of the notes states relative damage changes and some armour and suppression percentages for the first time [15][17]. These are percentages and rules, not absolute per-shot damage.

The 0.2.0 damage rework cuts base damage by calibre (.308 Win -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 Cal -16%, applied to every weapon using the round, including vehicle weapons), evens out and slightly lowers assault-rifle torso damage, aligns LMG body damage with assault rifles, adjusts DMR hit-location values, raises sniper-rifle hit-location damage, lowers Level 3 and Level 4 armour and helmet damage reduction (55% to 50%, 65% to 60%), and rebuilds suppression around shared falloff curves per weapon, with Level 3 and 4 helmets reducing suppression by 68% and 80% [15].

Season 1 material (the 10 Sep 2026 changelog through the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix) is kept as dated history. Document confidence is Medium: the Season 02 changes are Primary and itemised, but no absolute damage values exist, the realism and hit-registration sections rest on marketing-register text, and the ballistics claim rests on one beta-era press report. No official post after 15 Oct 2026 appears in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

text:
## Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) combat balance

All rows are official, from the Season 02 patch notes posted 2026-10-14 and live from 2026-10-15 [15][17]. The notes give relative changes; absolute damage is not stated. Where the notes give a Season 1 value it is shown as "Season 1 (0.1.2) -> Season 02 (0.2.0)".

The developer's stated reasoning: high-calibre rounds such as .308 and 7.62x54mmR were built for sniper rifles, where slow fire rate and small magazines balance big damage per shot, but in assault rifles, DMRs and LMGs they did "close to sniper damage at a much faster fire rate". The update "brings them closer to the other weapons in their archetype"; the FAL keeps the highest damage per shot among assault rifles but sits closer to the TCX-SPR and M4 [15].

### Calibre base damage reductions

The notes say these affect every weapon that uses the round, "including infantry & vehicle weapons" [15].

| Calibre | Base damage change |
|---------|--------------------|
| .308 Winchester | -25% |
| 7.62x54mmR | -20% |
| 7.62x39mm | -19% |
| .50 Cal | -16% |

Vehicle weapons named as affected: Little Bird AH-6M Minigun, Z20 Lakota Minigun, Humvee Minigun [15]. Which individual infantry weapons use each round is in weapons-catalogue.

### Archetype hit-location changes

| Archetype or item | Season 02 (0.2.0) change |
|-------------------|--------------------------|
| DMRs | Hit-location damage adjusted for the new calibre values; headshots and upper-body hits slightly weaker, so DMRs sit between assault rifles and snipers [15] |
| Assault rifles | Upper, middle and lower torso damage made more even; body shots do slightly less damage [15] |
| LMGs | Body damage now matches assault rifles; LMGs are meant to win through sustained fire and magazine size [15] |
| Sniper rifles | Hit-location damage increased to offset the base damage reduction [15] |
| Scout Rifle | Headshots now one-shot targets with no helmet; a Level 1 helmet takes two headshots [15] |
| Heavy and Artillery top machine turrets | Previously used the helicopter cannon's hit-location values; now use the assault-rifle and LMG values, so they do less damage to infantry depending on hit location [15] |

### Armour and helmets

| Item | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| Level 3 armour and helmets, damage reduction | 55% | 50% [15] |
| Level 4 armour and helmets, damage reduction | 65% | 60% [15] |
| Level 3 helmet, suppression reduction | not stated | 68% [15] |
| Level 4 helmet, suppression reduction | not stated | 80% [15] |
| Level 4 helmet, other effects | none stated | Muffled audio, muffled proximity chat, restricted field of view, fogs over when sprinting [15] |

The preview post of 9 Oct 2026 used "Heavy and Super Heavy" helmet names; the final notes use Level 3 and Level 4 [15][16]. Vendor prices of these items are in price-tables-season-1; item detail is in gadgets-armor-and-equipment.

### Slugs and bow versus armour

- 12 gauge slugs: damage against armour now scales with armour tier instead of one flat reduction [15].
- Compound Bow: arrow trajectory has a shorter drop-off; slightly more effective against lower-tier armour than Season 1; bow damage against armour scales with armour tier [15].

### Suppression rebuild

The notes say suppression "was inconsistent and often unnoticeable" and has been rebuilt around shared falloff curves per weapon [15].

- Near-miss suppression from small and medium calibres is considerably stronger.
- Rate of fire is accounted for, so fast-firing small and medium weapons (such as SMGs and pistols) do not suppress disproportionately.
- Suppression screen shake is reduced to offset the stronger effects.
- Level 3 helmets reduce suppression by 68%; Level 4 helmets by 80%.

No numeric suppression strengths or falloff curves are published [15].

### Recoil and per-weapon adjustments

| Weapon | Change in 0.2.0 |
|--------|-----------------|
| MP5 | Recoil pattern updated to be more horizontal, "as it was too easy to use" [15] |
| Super-45 | Damage fall-off increased beyond 50 m (its effective range), pushing it into close quarters [15] |
| DMRs | New recoil pass across all DMRs to match their power curve [15] |
| MGL-40 | Muzzle velocity -25%; stronger damage fall-off at the 40mm outer radius; much more inaccuracy and sway, slower ADS speed and a reload penalty when used on the Little Bird bench [15] |
| Mosin | New PU 91/30 (3.5x) scope; no access to other optics until future customisation features [15] |

Prices and unlock levels for these weapons are in weapons-catalogue.

### Related 0.2.0 items touching combat

- Molotov: a thrown incendiary dealing impact damage plus damage over time to anyone standing in the flames; rain reduces molotov fire [15]. Detail in gadgets-armor-and-equipment.
- Infrared Range Finder: runs on batteries, about 80 s of active use, draining faster if toggled quickly [15].
- Medical Bag durability 100 -> 150 [15].
- Parachutes: take longer to open, do not open below about 10 m, and opening below roughly 50 m while falling fast means fall damage [15].
- Vanguard CIWS: reduced damage to the Spawn Vehicle (2.25x longer to kill it); CIWS cannon damage against structures retuned to shred light cover and struggle against heavy fortifications [15].
- Helicopter cockpit glass now works both ways, so shooting out through it damages the vehicle like incoming fire [15].
- Some weapon inspects are silent, which the developer says is known [15].

## What the developer has said about realism versus tuning

| Date (UTC) | Official post | Statement (quoted or closely paraphrased) | Source class |
|------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------|
| 2026-10-08 (capture) | Steam store page, "What is the current state of the Early Access version?" [1] | "Realistic gunplay balanced for gameplay rather than simulation"; About This Game: "tactical gunplay and combined arms combat" | Official (store page, Primary) |
| 2026-02-18 | "WARDOGS - Top Questions" [4] | "MILSIM? ARCADE? WARDOGS is a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game. Aiming to balance gameplay depth and accessibility. Every decision matters. From moment-to-moment gunfights to Progression Unlocks." Setting described as "grounded militaristic gameplay"; Early Access feature list includes "Grounded Gunplay & Vehicles". Custom "WAR DYNAMICS FRAMEWORK" on UE5; the post says the team is "heavily conscious of performance & input latency" | Official |
| 2026-03-03 | "Answering Your Questions" [5] | Video Q&A (100 players and 3 teams, monetisation, console release). The saved text has no combat content, so nothing on damage or ballistics can be cited from it | Official |
| 2026-05-21 | "Tactical Depth & Teamplay" [2] | "Real-world ballistics, audio and flight models"; "every bullet fired, every loadout built, and every second-to-second choice has real consequences for your account balance" | Official (marketing register) |
| 2026-06-06 | "Gameplay Trailer" [12] | "Play it slow, tactical and methodical, OR embrace the hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game"; the game was shown in pre-alpha | Official |
| 2026-06-16 | "Addressing Feedback" [3] | "Every player's line between arcade and realistic is different. We've drawn ours. This isn't just about Killcam." Approach applies "throughout Early Access & Beyond" | Official |

Assessment: the developer's stated position is a deliberate middle between milsim and arcade, with the line left to the developer (High confidence that this is the stated position; evidence [1][3][4]). Where the line sits for any specific mechanic (damage falloff, recoil, time-to-kill) is not stated in text (Low confidence on any such inference; no evidence either way).

The 16 Jun 2026 post names "Killcam" explicitly, which implies a killcam feature was a feedback topic. The post text does not say whether a killcam exists in the Early Access build or how it was changed [3]. This is recorded in Open Questions.

## Bullet drop and bullet travel as documented

- Official sources: none. No saved Steam post and not the store page mention bullet drop, bullet velocity, travel time, gravity, zeroing or range tables [1][2][3][4][6][7][8][9]. The only official hook is the phrase "Real-world ballistics" [2].
- Press (beta era): the foundation document cites an allthings.how beta write-up reporting that real bullet drop and travel time are modelled and that carried weights differ (for example AMR 50 12.5 kg, LMGs 7.5 kg) [13]. This is press, drawn from closed-beta play, and is not confirmed by the developer. It is consistent with, but does not prove, the "real-world ballistics" claim [2].
- Related fix: the Season 1 changelog lists "Fixed a DPI issue affecting tank aiming"; that concerns input scaling on vehicle weapons, not ballistic behaviour [6].
- Related change: "Vehicle turrets now have a maximum operator rotation speed" (Season 1 changelog) [6].

## Damage model and hit registration as documented

| Topic | What is officially documented | Source |
|-------|-------------------------------|--------|
| Weapon damage values, headshot multipliers, falloff | Still no absolute values. 0.2.0 gives relative base-damage changes by calibre, qualitative hit-location changes by archetype, and the Super-45 falloff beyond 50 m and MGL-40 outer-radius falloff changes (Season 02 section) | [1][2][3][4][6][8][9][15] |
| Armor ratings, plate or vest damage reduction | From 0.2.0: Level 3 armour and helmets 55% to 50%, Level 4 65% to 60% damage reduction. Not published for other tiers (a Level 1 helmet exists; its reduction is not stated). Season 1 changelog gave no armour stats | [6][15] |
| Ammo types | AP ("762x54mm AP", "556mm AP") and, from 0.2.0, flesh-damage (HP) ammo (5.45x39mm, 9x19mm, 5.56mm, .308 Win) exist as unlocks; their damage effect is not described | [6][15] |
| Hit registration or netcode for hit validation | Revive validity checks are "fully server authoritative" (0.1.2). Hit validation itself is not described. The team states performance and input latency are priorities | [4][8] |
| Buildable damage | "Crit spots" on buildables were fixed to stop reappearing in the same place or jumping to the far side of a structure; they "now favour a spot you can reach from where you're standing". Destruction rewards "scale with their build progress" | [8] |
| Vehicle and air damage | Havoc bug "causing increased damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire" fixed (0.1.2); CIWS kill time on a Havoc about 12 s down to about 6 s (hotfix) | [8][9] |
| Melee | Melee combat exists (store-page Mature Content Description: "killing with weapons and melee combat"); no damage or balance detail is published | [1] |
| Killcam | Named in a devlog title context only | [3] |

## Chronological list of balance changes in each official patch post

Source posts: Season 1 changelog posted 2026-09-09 22:46 UTC (published as the launch-day pre-load) [6]; Launch Stability Hotfix #1 of 2026-09-10 [10]; Patch 0.11 post of 2026-09-12 (deployed 14 Sep) [7]; Update 0.1.2 of 2026-09-30 [8]; Security & Stability Hotfix notice of 2026-10-02 [14]; IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix of 2026-10-02 [9].

### 1. Season 1 changelog (9 to 10 Sep 2026) [6]

Developer-filed "Gameplay and vehicles":

- Z20 Lakota balance pass, plus a fix for sluggish pitch.
- Helicopter input damping now applies to every input device.
- Vehicle turrets now have a maximum operator rotation speed.
- 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables now take up more room in the loadout.
- Fixed a DPI issue affecting tank aiming.
- Z20 Lakota chase-camera rotation rattle reduced by 6 dB.

Developer-filed "Balance changes" (italic rationale in the post): levels roughly 10 to 20 slowed, the curve flattened from 35 onward, "our median players, at 20 to 25 hours, will be around level 20", and "the top 5%" who want the "big ticket items" will have to grind. Artillery moves to Career 90 and Heavy Tank to Driver 35; Driver "rejigged to give a satisfying escalation through attack vehicles"; Forward Operating Base and Large Hammer vendor prices raised "to make them more of a choice".

"XP Bands": "Previously our balancing was designed specifically for weekend long beta tests. Now they will be in-line with where we believe they should be. Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders." Values are in the Baseline table below.

"XP Events": player kill using an air vehicle 300 to 250 XP; supply crate item sold under $75 25 XP to 1 XP.

"Economy Changes": 14 vendor and role-track price changes and a rescaled supply-crate purchase curve (Baseline table). "Season 1.0 Unlocks" lists Career, Medic, Support and Driver level moves (Baseline table). No weapon damage, recoil or range change appears in this post.

### 2. Launch Stability Hotfix #1 (10 Sep 2026) [10]

Client hotfix for server joins, kicks and login queue. No balance or damage content.

### 3. Patch 0.11 (announced 12 Sep, deployed 14 Sep 2026) [7]

Server browser, community-server discoverability, Asian capacity, and an economy-abuse policy. No weapon, damage or unlock changes. The only balance-adjacent items are "Various cash exploits have been fixed", a temporary "5% End of Match cash bonus" on community servers "for the next week", and the abuse sanctions (timed ban plus cash and XP reset for exploits; permanent ban for exploit tutorials and XP-farming servers). The post says Season 2 content is not affected by the quality-of-life queue.

### 4. Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026, maintenance at 08:00 UTC) [8]

Balance- or combat-relevant items only:

- Revive action validity checks now fully server authoritative.
- Vehicle fly-through exploit fixed; rewards capped.
- Buildable-destruction rewards now scale with build progress, so destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward.
- Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone awards reduced rewards.
- Throwables (grenades, smoke, C4) can no longer be used from enclosed vehicle seats.
- Adaptive crosshair now hides while aiming down sights.
- Buildable crit spots no longer reappear in the same place, get pushed into corners, or jump to the far side; they favour a spot reachable from the player's position.
- Havoc bug fixed that "caus[ed] increased damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire".

The post states that Season 02 will include "balance reworks" [8]. No numeric weapon values are given.

### 5. Security & Stability Hotfix notice (2 Oct 2026) [14]

Scheduled 08:00 UTC, about one hour downtime, for minor security and stability issues. No balance content.

### 6. IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix (2 Oct 2026, 15:39 UTC) [9]

- IR Rangefinders will be disabled in the vendor, once servers restart across regions within 12 hours, "until Season 02, where they will require batteries to use". Reason given: "we agree with player sentiment and they cross the line into being too overpowered."
- The CIWS "now destroys the havoc in around 6 seconds as opposed to 12". "We acknowledge we overcorrected this in the previous patch."
- "No new client download or server downtime is required."

text:
- The documented balance record is thin and mostly progression tuning; do not read it as a weapon-balance history [6].
- The 21 May 2026 "real-world ballistics" claim is pre-launch marketing; its video content was not captured [2].
- Season 1 tables are history; the 0.2.0 values are current only as of 15 Oct 2026 and may change per hotfix or at the next season [6][15].
- The 0.2.0 notes give percentages and rules but no absolute damage; do not derive per-shot damage from them without the Season 1 base values, which the developer never published.
- The Season 1 changelog mixes price rises and cuts (for example Z20 Lakota and URAL fall to $35,000 while the Large Hammer rises). The values are recorded as posted, and the Support Large Hammer price ($25,000 to $75,000) and the vendor Large Hammer price ($1,600 to $2,400) are both listed without the post saying how they relate [6].
- Press coverage of the same posts (for example the Gfinity and BisectHosting reproductions cited by the foundation) may omit lines; this document uses the saved official text.
- Posts are marketing and ops text, written by the developer; no independent test of any statement has been done.

text:
This document covers the non-weapon loadout items in WARDOGS: armor and helmets, backpacks, parachutes, ammo types, sidearms, optics, medical gadgets, throwables and IR gear. Season 1 (patch 0.1.2 plus the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix) is kept as dated history; the current state is Update 0.2.0 (Season 02), whose official patch notes were posted 14 Oct 2026 [9] and which the developer announced as released on 15 Oct 2026 [10].

Update 0.2.0 is the first official source to publish item-level numbers: Level 3 armor and helmet damage reduction lowered 55% to 50%, Level 4 lowered 65% to 60%, Level 3 and Level 4 helmets reducing suppression by 68% and 80%, a Level 4 Helmet with muffled audio, muffled proximity chat, restricted field of view and sprint fog-over, a battery-powered Infrared Range Finder (about 80 s per battery), a new Molotov Cocktail, Medical Bag durability 100 to 150, a parachute rework and a 30mm-ammo 2x2 slot with a 50-item backpack stack cap [9]. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot, so later hotfixes are neither confirmed nor ruled out.

Confidence is Medium: the 0.2.0 changes are Primary-sourced, but the underlying item catalogue (for example sidearm base prices and medical-gadget details) still rests on player-reported guides and a beta-era press table.

- Update 0.2.0 (notes 14 Oct 2026): Level 3 Armor and Helmet damage reduction 55% to 50%; Level 4 65% to 60% [9]. Ballistics context is in damage-ballistics-and-balance.
- Level 3 helmets reduce suppression by 68% and Level 4 helmets by 80% (0.2.0) [9].
- Level 4 Helmet drawbacks (0.2.0): muffled audio, muffled proximity chat, restricted field of view, fogs over when sprinting [9].
- The Infrared Range Finder now runs on batteries: about 80 s of active use per battery, draining faster if toggled on and off quickly (0.2.0) [9]. Its vendor price rose $1,200 to $3,200 [9]. It had been disabled in the vendor by the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix [3]; the 0.2.0 notes do not say whether it is purchasable at launch.
- New Molotov Cocktail (Assault level 13, $25k unlock, $340 vendor price): impact damage plus burn damage over time, throw overarm or underarm, burns destructible foliage, weaker in rain (0.2.0) [9].
- Medical Bag durability 100 to 150; unlock moved Medic level 24 to 14 and $75k to $50k; vendor price $2,000 to $1,800 (0.2.0) [9].
- Parachutes (0.2.0): longer to open, will not open below about 10 m, and opening below roughly 50 m while falling fast means fall damage; Basic Parachute $100 to $500, Sport Parachute $1,000 to $700 [9].
- Explosives and placeables can no longer be used from enclosed vehicle seats (0.2.0), extending the 0.1.2 throwables rule [2][9].

All items below apply to Update 0.2.0 (notes 14 Oct 2026, release 15 Oct 2026) unless dated otherwise [9][10].

- Armor and helmets: Level 3 damage reduction 50% and Level 4 damage reduction 60% [9]. Against a Level 1 helmet a Scout Rifle needs two headshots; with no helmet one headshot kills [9].
- Helmet suppression resistance: Level 3 reduces suppression by 68%, Level 4 by 80% [9].
- Level 4 Helmet: muffled audio, restricted field of view, fogs over when sprinting; the Combat Balance section also lists muffled proximity chat [9].

- Molotov Cocktail: Assault track level 13, $25k to unlock, $340 vendor price [9].

- Sport Parachute unlock level 35 to 34 (WARDOG track) [9].
- 30mm cannon ammo takes a 2x2 inventory slot instead of 1x1; backpack stacks are capped at 50; vehicle storage stacks stay at 200 [9].
- Explosives and placeables are barred from enclosed vehicle seats [9]. Barbed wire no longer gives cash or XP on kills [9].
- Halligan Bar now breaches both doors and gates; uses raised 5 to 7; vendor price $1,100 to $885 [9].
- Rain reduces Molotov fire and affects spotting range [9].
- The Steam store page lists gear and a ghillie suit as loadout content, with no item table (live capture 2026-10-08) [6].

## Armor and helmets

Season 1 had no official armor values; a guide described a Level 2 Helmet as protection against sniper fire and body armor as protecting the torso only (player-reported) [5]. Update 0.2.0 is the first official source: Level 3 damage reduction 55% to 50% and Level 4 65% to 60% (armor and helmets), Level 3 and Level 4 helmets with increased suppression resistance (68% and 80% reductions), and a Level 4 Helmet with muffled audio, muffled proximity chat, restricted field of view and sprint fog-over [9]. The notes frame the helmet changes as letting these items better fulfil their protective role in more ways than damage reduction [9]. The Level 3 Helmet & Armor unlock moved to level 70 [9]. Also in 0.2.0: Scout Rifle headshots one-shot no-helmet targets and need two against a Level 1 helmet; 12 gauge slug and compound bow damage against armor scale with armor tier [9]. Level 2 values are not stated. Absolute damage numbers are not published; see damage-ballistics-and-balance.

## Tactical vests and backpacks

Player-reported (Season 1): Small Tac Vest opens Quick Slots 5 and 6 with minor reload and equip speed bonuses; Medium opens 5 to 8 with larger bonuses; Large opens all slots [5]. The 0.2.0 notes do not mention vests. Backpack changes in 0.2.0: Ruck, Gunner (+ Sling) and Arsenal (+ 2 Slings) prices fell (see table); backpack stacks are capped at 50; 30mm cannon ammo takes a 2x2 slot; vehicle storage stacks stay at 200 [9]. Season 1: Large Backpack was a Career unlock at level 55 [1]; the notes do not restate its level.

## Parachutes

Update 0.2.0 [9]: parachutes take longer to fully open and will not open at all below about 10 m; opening below roughly 50 m while falling fast means fall damage; Basic Parachute $100 to $500; Sport Parachute $1,000 to $700; Sport Parachute unlock level 35 to 34. The notes add a warning to trust a pilot before boarding their aircraft. Season 1: Sports Parachute Career 35 [1]; Basic Parachute $100, single use, lighter than the Sport Parachute (player-reported) [5]. Official text says "Sports Parachute" (Season 1) and "Sport Parachute" (0.2.0) [1][9].

## Ammo types

0.2.0 unlock-level changes in the WARDOG track [9]: 12g Rifled Slug 41 to 36, 7.62x39mm AP 63 to 60, .308 Win Flesh Damage (HP) 65 to 63, 5.45x39mm HP 16 to 6, 9x19mm HP 6 to 10, 5.56mm HP 10 to 13, 5.56mm AP 83 to 84, 5.45x39mm AP 93 to 90. Season 1: 762x54mm AP (Career 82) and 556mm AP (Career 83) [1]; beta press: ammo billed per caliber, roughly $10 to $250 a box [7]. Calibre base-damage reductions (.308 -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 Cal -16%) are in damage-ballistics-and-balance [9]. A per-caliber ammo price table is not published in the notes.

## Sidearms

0.2.0 [9]: Judge level 18 to 1 and $15k to $5k; GGX 17 level 1 to 18 and $5k to $15k; Deagle level 85 to 65 and vendor price $900 to $750; GGX 18 level 70 to 85, unlock $50k to $125k, vendor price $800 to $1,000. Season 1: Deagle at Career 85 [1]; beta list prices are in the Season 1 table and may be stale [7].

## Optics and attachments

0.2.0 adds optics, muzzle devices, magazines and bipods alongside the four new weapons [9]. New attachments and vendor prices [9]: Compact P-1 Red Dot ($480; WARDOG level 21, $12.5k), PU 91/30 Scope for the Mosin ($780; Recon level 10, $12.5k), Leatherwood ART II for the M14 ($950), Evolys Bipod for the Evo-3 Ultra ($1,450), M14 Bipod ($1,480), Cross Rifle Muzzle Brake ($780), Clutch Lok Muzzle Brake ($1,100) and SRD762TI-QD Suppressor ($1,350) for the TCX-SPR, SL7i-BL Suppressor for the Evo-3 Ultra ($1,400), .30 Cal SS Phosphate Muzzle Brake ($950) and .30 Cal Steel Black Flash Hider ($730) for the M14. New magazines: PP-19 Bizon 53 RND $200, TCX-SPR 28 RND $50, Evolys 50 RND Box $110, M14 10, 20 and 30 RND $60, $110 and $180 [9]. The Mosin loses access to other optics [9]. The notes say most attachments moved to earlier levels or new tracks; the full lists are in progression-unlock-tables and price-tables-season-1 [9]. Season 1: Recon 6-10x MRAD and MOA scope prices rose 60% and 50% [1]; a compact red dot and a 6x Precision Rifle Scope were mentioned by a guide without prices (player-reported) [5].

## Medical gadgets and throwables

Update 0.2.0 [9]: Medical Bag durability 100 to 150 (a single bag goes further before replacement), unlock Medic 14 and $50k, price $1,800; Defibrillator unlock Medic 22 and $110k; First Aid Kit level 10; Adrenaline Pen level 16; M18 Smoke Grenade: Black level 23; Field Resuscitator price $425. The guide's "Emergency Resuscitator" and the notes' "Field Resuscitator" may be the same item; this is not stated. Molotov Cocktail is a thrown incendiary that splashes fire on impact, deals impact damage plus damage over time to anyone standing in the flames, can be thrown overarm or underarm, burns destructible foliage and is reduced by rain; Assault level 13, $25k unlock, $340 [9]. C4 and the Remote Detonator moved into the Assault track (level 4), and IED/C4 now give assault XP [9]. Explosives and placeables are barred from enclosed vehicle seats [9]; the 0.1.2 rule covered grenades, smoke and C4 [2]. Barbed wire gives no cash or XP on kills [9]. Season 1 player-reported prices are in the baseline table [5].

## IR gear

Update 0.2.0 [9]: the Infrared Range Finder runs on batteries, about 80 s of active use per battery, draining faster if quickly toggled on and off; vendor price $1,200 to $3,200. The plain Range Finder is a separate priced item ($400 to $1,450; Recon unlock $15k to $25k) [9]. The 2 Oct 2026 hotfix had disabled IR Rangefinders in the vendor, calling them "too overpowered" and promising batteries [3]. Whether the item is purchasable at the 0.2.0 launch, its unlock level and battery cost are not stated. A boosting-seller blog describes IR gear as thermal goggles or binoculars that ease spotting (player-reported, conflict of interest) [8].

text:
This is the WARDOGS firearm and launcher roster revised for Season 02 (Update 0.2.0, released 15 Oct 2026) [13][15]. The official Season 02 patch notes (posted 14 Oct 2026) add four weapons, a new attachment set, and itemised vendor price changes and unlock changes for many existing weapons [13]. These are the first official per-weapon prices and unlock levels in the record. The Season 1 values are kept below as dated history ("Season 1 (0.1.2): X -> Season 02 (0.2.0): Y").

The four new weapons are the TCX-SPR (7.62x39mm assault rifle, $3,200), the PP-19 Bizon (9x19mm SMG, $1,000), the Evo-3 Ultra (.308 Win LMG, $7,250) and the M14 (.308 Win marksman rifle, $7,400) [13]. The preview post of 9 Oct 2026 called the first "TCX Spear" and the M14 a "DMR"; this document uses the final-notes names [13][14].

Confidence stays Low. Every Season 02 change is Primary (patch notes), but the underlying Season 1 roster for weapons the notes do not mention (M4 and M500 prices, categories, ammo) rests on guides dated 12 to 17 September 2026 that partly disagree, one from a hosting seller. The rubric rates a document by its weakest evidence. No official post after 15 Oct 2026 appears in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

## Season 02 per-weapon balance changes

All from the 0.2.0 notes [13]; numeric damage effects are covered in damage-ballistics-and-balance.

- Calibre base damage: .308 Win -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 Cal -16%, for every weapon using the round, including vehicle weapons. By the guide calibre column and the notes' calibres for new weapons, this covers FAL, Evo-3 Ultra, M14, BMR-308 and MK22 (.308); PKM, SVD, Mosin and SV98 (7.62x54mm); SKS and TCX-SPR (7.62x39mm); AMR 50 (.50) [8][13]. The weapon-to-calibre mapping is the KB's inference from those columns.
- MP5: recoil pattern made more horizontal, "as it was too easy to use".
- Super-45: damage fall-off increased beyond 50 m, its effective range, pushing it into a close-quarters role.
- DMRs: a new recoil pass across all DMRs.
- MGL-40: muzzle velocity -25%; stronger damage fall-off in the 40mm outer radius; more inaccuracy and sway, slower ADS speed and a reload penalty when used on the Little Bird bench.
- Mosin: new PU 91/30 (3.5x) scope; no access to other optics until future customisation features.
- Scout Rifle: headshots one-shot targets with no helmet; a Level 1 helmet takes two headshots.
- Compound Bow: shorter arrow drop-off, slightly more effective against lower-tier armour, and armour damage scales with armour tier.
- 12 gauge slugs: damage against armour scales with armour tier.
- Heavy and Artillery turrets: hit-location values now the same as assault rifles and LMGs.

title: Cash Rewards & Costs
topic: How cash and XP are earned per action, logistics streaks, destroyed rewards, spotting, exploit fixes and build supply costs

text:
Until Season 02 the studio published no per-action cash amounts; the Season 1 and 0.1.2 posts described reward changes only qualitatively [1][3]. The Season 02 Patch Notes (posted 14 Oct 2026, released as Update 0.2.0 on 15 Oct 2026) change that: their "Cash & XP Reward Changes" section prints dollar and XP values for new action rewards, logistics deliveries and streaks, vehicle, buildable and supply-crate destruction, drill tower capture and spotting, and lists seven exploit fixes [14][15]. The notes also give new build supply costs [14].

The Hot Zone still pays double cash and cash persists between matches [4][5]. In Season 02 only, the Lonestar faction gets a cash and XP win bonus and teamplay multipliers, and a losing team 40 points behind gets a 20% vendor discount [14]. The notes contain an in-post update: the logistics streak values were revised after first posting to include the zone multiplier, and this document uses the updated values [14].

Confidence is High: every number comes from the official Season 02 Patch Notes or earlier official posts. Two player-reported guides are kept only as labelled background. Several points the notes do not state stay in Open Questions, among them the Lonestar multiplier values, the death-penalty rules and any progression wipe.

- Logistics: base rewards were lowered and new delivery streaks add per-delivery bonuses, for example crates +$100 / +50 XP each up to 10 (updated values) [14].
- Vehicle destroyed rewards are now per variant: Humvee default $600 but Humvee [Minigun] $5,000; armed variants give 1.5x the XP of the default [14].
- Spotting rewards are about 30% lower than Season 1 and scale with the value of the target; a spotted target destroyed by an enemy faction now pays 25% of the reward, down from 50% [14].
- Build supply costs changed: Door 22 to 80, Gate 85 to 200, L81 Mortar 150 to 600, Talon 9K-SAM 1,000 to 650, Hot Zone Magnet 2,250 to 2,750 [14].
- Exploit fixes: supply-crate selling has diminishing returns per buyer, selling to an enemy gives no cash or XP, FOB Supplied Assist is split between assisting players [14].
- Still unpublished: Hot Zone multiplier scope, Lonestar bonus values, whether cash converts to Gold Bars automatically at Season 02 start [4][14].

text:
- **Teamplay action**: an action that the developer says rewards cash, such as reviving, transporting or spotting [4].
- **Hot Zone**: a shifting sub-zone of the Control Zone where players count double towards presence and earn double cash [4].
- **Build supply cost**: the supplies a buildable consumes; in 0.2.0 the destroyed-buildable cash reward matches this cost [14].
- **Delivery streak**: a bonus added for each consecutive delivery in a row, up to a cap, introduced in 0.2.0 [14].
- **End-of-match bonus**: a cash bonus at match end, referenced by the 5% community-server promotion (Patch 0.11) [2].
- **Economy abuse**: cash or XP exploits, tutorialising them, XP farming or real money trading as defined in the developer policy [1][2].

text:
- Teamplay actions award cash; the official examples are reviving squadmates, transporting friendlies to the zone and controlling the objective (Steam page, 2026-10-08) [5].
- The Hot Zone yields double cash and players count double towards zone presence (Steam news, 18 Feb 2026) [4].
- Cash persists between matches and can be spent or exchanged for Gold Bars, the endgame cosmetic currency (18 Feb 2026) [4]. In-game cash and Gold Bars will never be sold for real money (11 Aug 2026) [6].
- Update 0.2.0 is live (15 Oct 2026, servers back online) and contains the reward values in the Detail section [14][15].
- Wager Vendor: announced as a way to "bet your own cash on your own performance"; it is not available at Season 02 launch and "will open later in Season 2" [14].

title: Cash Rewards & Costs
topic: How cash and XP are earned per action, logistics streaks, destroyed rewards, spotting, exploit fixes and build supply costs

text:
## Earning actions: what was published, by source

| Source class | Actions listed | Amount |
|--------------|----------------|--------|
| Official (Steam news, 18 Feb 2026) | Revives, transport, kills, spotting, "and MORE" [4] | Not published at the time |
| Official (Steam page) | Reviving squadmates, transporting friendlies to the zone, controlling the objective [5] | Not published |
| Official (0.1.2 notes, 30 Sep 2026) | Revive actions, vehicle fly-through, destroying buildables, depositing pallets into a FOB [1] | Not published |
| Official (0.2.0 notes, 14 Oct 2026) | New action rewards, logistics, destroyed rewards, drill tower capture, spotting [14] | Published; tables below |
| Player-reported (allthings.how) | Kills, assists, revives, heals, spotting, resupplying, repairing vehicles, FOB building, hauling supplies, driving or flying teammates, tips, holding the Control Zone, destroying enemy vehicles [11] | Not published |

The player-reported guide's own dollar figures are limited to the $10,000 starting balance [11]. A second guide gives item costs only (for example Galil unlock $35,000), which are costs, not income (player-reported) [12].

## Hot Zone double cash

Official: the Hot Zone is a shifting sub-zone inside the Control Zone, players inside count double for presence and it "yields DOUBLE CASH" [4]. The Steam page repeats "chase the 'Hot Zone' to earn double the cash" [5]. Player-reported: standard cash applies in the Control Zone outside the Hot Zone, with no payout figures given [13]. The 0.2.0 notes do not restate the Hot Zone multiplier; the updated streak values include a "zone multiplier" for deliveries dropped in the Control Zone without giving its size [14]. Whether the multiplier applies to every action is not stated (see Open Questions).

## New and changed action rewards (0.2.0)

All rows: Season 02 Patch Notes, 14 Oct 2026, live 15 Oct 2026 [14]. Season 1 (0.1.2) values are shown where the notes print an old value.

| Action | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|--------|------------------|-------------------|
| Kill with an assault-archetype weapon (bonus) | $1,500 | $2,000 |
| FOB hacking, hacker | $2,500 / 250 XP (the notes say the hacker "still gets" this) | $2,500 / 250 XP |
| FOB hacking, teammates in the FOB radius | not paid | $1,000 / 250 XP |
| Door breached with the Halligan Bar | not paid | $100, once per door; Halligan Bar uses 5 to 7 |
| Friendly FOB door closed | not paid | $75 |
| Destroying a FOB | not stated | Bonus up to +$7,500 / +250 XP by supplies held (maxed at 25,000 supplies) |
| Capturing a hostile drill tower | $750 / 250 XP | $1,500 / 300 XP |
| Barbed wire kills | Contributed cash and XP | No longer contribute cash or XP |

### Role reward reassignment (0.2.0)

Role XP now flows differently [14]:

- Destroying a buildable gives assault XP instead of support.
- Artillery gives driver XP instead of support.
- IED and C4 give assault XP instead of support.
- Repair XP goes to the driver or pilot track depending on the vehicle repaired, instead of a flat support amount.

Track unlocks themselves are in progression-unlock-tables.

## Logistics (0.2.0)

The notes state that base logistics rewards are lower and that delivery streaks add a bonus for every consecutive run, so logistics players are rewarded for return trips [14].

### Delivery streaks (new)

Values below are the updated figures. The notes say the originally posted values were "base design values without a zone multiplier" and were later replaced by "the actual values players will receive when dropped in the Control Zone". The original numbers are not preserved in the post [14].

| Streak | Bonus per delivery in a row | Cap |
|--------|-----------------------------|-----|
| Crates | +$100 / +50 XP | 10 |
| Pallets | +$250 / +100 XP | 10 |
| Players | +$25 / +5 XP | 25 |
| Return trips | +$50 / +25 XP | 10 |

### Base logistics values

| Action | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|--------|------------------|-------------------|
| Player delivered | $150, 50 XP | $100, 25 XP |
| Player delivered (ground vehicle) | $500 | $350 |
| Return trip (ground vehicle) | $250, 100 XP | $150, 50 XP |
| Deploy supply crate, small | $500, 250 XP | $250, 200 XP |
| Deploy supply crate, large | $1,000, 500 XP | $500, 400 XP |
| Deploy supply crate, small (air vehicle) XP | 200 XP | 150 XP |
| Deploy supply crate, large (air vehicle) XP | 400 XP | 300 XP |
| Deploy supply pallet | $2,500, 500 XP | $1,250, 400 XP |
| Deploy supply pallet XP from a ground vehicle | 750 XP | 500 XP |

Source: [14]. The Season 1 values are the "old" figures printed in the notes.

## Vehicle destroyed (0.2.0)

Every variant now has its own reward; armed variants give 1.5x the XP of the default variant, and Attack Vehicle rewards rise with their kill count [14]. Old to new where the notes print both.

| Vehicle | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|---------|------------------|-------------------|
| Kodiak | $1,250 | $500 default, $600 Pickup, $3,400 [M249] |
| Wolf-110 | new | $450; [M2 Browning] $3,900 |
| Humvee | $1,500 | $600 default, $4,250 [M249], $5,000 [Minigun] |
| Ural | $2,500 | $1,000 default, $3,600 Defender, $4,750 Defender [M249] |
| Bobcat | $250 | $100 |
| Dune Buggy | $750 | $300 |
| MH-6 | $3,125 | $1,250 |
| Little Bird AH-6M [Miniguns] | not stated | $6,000 |
| Little Bird AH-6R [Rockets] | not stated | $9,400 |
| Z20 Lakota | $3,700 | $1,500; [Miniguns] $7,500 |
| Havoc | $18,000 | $14,000 |
| L2A6 | $14,000 | $11,000 |
| SPH-2 | $14,000 | $8,000 |
| Flakpanzer Gepard | new | $7,000 |
| T-72B3 | new | $8,000 |

Source for every row: [14].

## Buildable destroyed (0.2.0)

Cash now matches each buildable's build supply cost and XP is roughly 25% of the cash reward [14]. Destroying a buildable also now pays based on how built it is (see exploit fixes) [14].

| Buildable | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------|
| L81 Mortar | $300 | $650 |
| Stingray | $300 | $650 |
| Hot Zone Magnet | $4,500 | $2,750 |
| Vanguard CIWS | $3,000 | $1,200 |
| Talon 9K-SAM | $2,000 | $650 |
| Repair / Refuel Station | $400 | $200 |
| Door | $500 | $100 |
| Gate | $170 | $200 |
| MG Nest | new | $650 |
| Large Shelter | new | $250 |
| Wood Base | new | $15 |

Source: [14]. Note that the L81 Mortar and Stingray rewards ($650) differ from their build supply costs (600 and 650) listed below, so "matches" is the notes' general statement rather than a per-item identity [14].

## Supply crate destroyed (0.2.0)

| Crate | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|-------|------------------|-------------------|
| Small | $500 | $300 |
| Large | $1,000 | $600 |
| Small Armored | $500 | $1,000 |
| Large Armored | $1,000 | $1,600 |
| Supply Pallets | $1,000 | $800 |

Source: [14]. Destroying an empty enemy crate now rewards half cash and half XP, and deploy and destroy rewards scale with the value of the supplies inside [14].

## Spotting (0.2.0)

The notes say spotting rewards are "around 30% lower than Season 1" because spotting was the lowest-risk, highest-paying way to earn, and they now scale with the value of each vehicle variant, buildable and crate. A spotted target destroyed by an enemy faction now pays 25% of the reward, down from 50% [14]. Spotting range is affected by rain (new rain weather preset) [14]. No absolute spotting dollar amount is published.

## Build supply costs (0.2.0)

The notes call these "build supply costs" and say the pass aims to make structures "a considered investment rather than something you spam" [14]. Season 1 to Season 02:

| Buildable | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|-----------|------------------|-------------------|
| Wood Base | new | 15 |
| Bremmer wall | 15 | 32 |
| Door | 22 | 80 |
| Gate | 85 | 200 |
| Large Shelter | new | 250 |
| Air raid shelter, bunker, crow's nest | 100 | 200 |
| L81 Mortar | 150 | 600 |
| Stingray | 150 | 650 |
| MG Nest | new | 650 |
| Talon 9K-SAM | 1,000 | 650 |
| Vanguard CIWS | 1,500 | 1,200 |
| Hot Zone Magnet | 2,250 | 2,750 |

Source: [14]. Build speed (medium hammer contributes less per swing, critical spots give a smaller bonus, large hammer unchanged), drill rig, Talon and Mortar changes are owned by fob-and-base-building.

## Exploit fixes (0.2.0)

All from the notes' "Exploit Fixes" section [14]:

- Spotting added and removed rewards scale with build progress, to stop farming spots on unfinished buildables.
- Destroying a buildable pays based on how built it is.
- Selling from a supply crate has diminishing returns per buyer; after enough sales you break even with no profit or XP.
- Selling an item from a supply crate to an enemy player (for example after they switch teams) gives no cash or XP.
- Destroying an empty enemy crate rewards half cash and half XP.
- Supply crate deploy and destroy rewards scale with the value of the supplies inside.
- FOB Supplied Assist is split between the number of assisting players, so a whole team can no longer each receive the full kickback.

Related 0.2.0 anti-abuse changes outside the reward tables: team-switching restrictions (once a team is more than 10 points ahead), and a victim-driven Team-Kill Punish / Forgive vote; see control-zone-and-match-flow [14].

## Season 02 faction experiment and discounts

The notes announce a "social experiment" for Season 2: a Lonestar cash and XP win bonus and Lonestar teamplay action cash and XP multipliers, "Season 2 only", with no values stated. A new vendor discount gives the losing team 20% off when at least 40 points behind second place, relevant to all teams. Community server hosts seen exploiting the faction bonus "will be punished" [14]. Server-seeding players earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins, amounts not stated [14].

## 0.1.2 reward changes (history)

| Change (30 Sep 2026) | Official wording | Value |
|----------------------|------------------|-------|
| Revive validity | Checks "now fully server authoritative" [1] | n/a |
| Vehicle fly-through | "rewards are now capped" [1] | Cap not stated |
| Destroying buildables | Rewards "scale with their build progress"; a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward [1] | Not stated; superseded by 0.2.0 buildable values |
| FOB pallet deposit outside zone | "now awards reduced rewards" [1] | Not stated |

Press coverage (BisectHosting) repeated these points and stated no values (press) [10].

## Exploit and abuse policy

| Offence | Official consequence | Date |
|---------|----------------------|------|
| Abusing cash exploits and bugs | Timed ban scaled to prior bans; cash and XP reset to 0 [2] | 14 Sep 2026 |
| Creating content that tutorialises exploits | Treated as advertising cheats; permanent ban [2] | 14 Sep 2026 |
| XP farming (joining farming servers more than a few minutes) | Permanent ban [2] | 14 Sep 2026 |
| Repeatable unintended exploits, real money trading | Cash and progression reset; risk of permanent ban without warning; first-offence leniency ended [1] | 30 Sep 2026 |

The developer states that testing an exploit "once or twice" is acceptable, but repeating it is abuse [2]. The 0.2.0 notes do not restate this policy.

## Season 1 economy changes versus beta

The Season 1.0 changelog (10 Sep 2026) states the previous balance "was designed specifically for weekend long beta tests" and that each season will have a different XP curve and item order [3]. It changed prices and XP, not documented per-action cash. Item prices are in price-tables-season-1.

## Income per hour

No sourced income-per-hour figure exists. The only quantified pacing statement in the notes is XP-based: reaching level 20 "now takes less than half the playtime it did in Season 1" [14].

| Player kill using an air vehicle: 300 XP to 250 XP | Season 1.0, 10 Sep 2026 | [3] |
| Supply crate item sold under $75: 25 XP to 1 XP | Season 1.0, 10 Sep 2026 | [3] |

| Level 20 XP requirement 250,000 to 111,500 | 0.2.0 (Season 1.0 had changed 111,500 to 250,000) | [3][14] |

title: Death Penalty, Loadout Loss & Re-buy
topic: What dying costs, loadout loss, re-buy, insurance-like mechanics, negative balances

text:
The official Steam text fixes the frame of the death penalty but not its size. Every player starts with $10,000, buys a custom loadout "each life", and cash persists from match to match [1]. Bulkhead's own launch-era posts say that "every decision affects YOUR account balance" and that players can min/max their "return on investment every life" [2][3]. No official post, patch note or Q&A in the saved Steam news feed states what is lost on death, what a Re-buy Loadout costs, whether a refund or insurance exists, or what happens at zero cash (checked 2026-10-08) [1][2][3][4][5][6][7].

The detail that does exist is player-reported: an unrevived death forfeits the kit bought for that life, the next kit is paid from the same balance, and a "Re-buy Loadout" vendor option rebuilds the previous kit [9][10]. A vehicle guide says a destroyed vehicle must be paid for again at its spawn price [11]. Season 02 (Update 0.2.0, notes 14 Oct, live 15 Oct 2026) confirmed one related change: the "Rebuy Last Loadout" button now fills the equipment vendor UI visually with the last loadout, which the player can add to or remove items from before purchase, and the old placeholder rebuy UI was removed [13][14][15]. That is an interface change; the notes state no death penalty, re-buy price, refund or zero-cash rule, and that silence is not evidence either way [14]. The Season 1 / 0.1.2 text is kept as dated history.

Confidence is Low: the answer to the core question (what dying costs) still rests entirely on player-reported guides dated before Season 02, and none gives a re-buy price.

text:
## Official text: what it does and does not say

| Question | Official answer | Source |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Is a loadout bought per life? | Yes: "Each life, you purchase a custom loadout" | [1] |
| Does cash persist between matches? | Yes | [1][2] |
| Is there an exact loss on death? | Not stated, including in the Season 02 notes | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][14] |
| Is there a Rebuy Last Loadout feature? | Yes: confirmed by the 0.2.0 notes as a button that pre-fills the vendor with the last loadout (editable); no price stated | [14] |
| Is there a Re-buy price or cost difference? | Not stated | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][14] |
| Insurance, refunds, grace for low cash? | Not mentioned | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][14] |
| Negative balance or zero-cash floor? | Not mentioned | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][14] |
| Can cash be spent on anything besides loadouts? | Yes: exchangeable for Gold Bars (cosmetics) | [2] |
| Is there a per-round or seasonal reset? | The Patch 0.11 and 0.1.2 posts say bans reset cash and XP to 0 but state no routine reset; the Season 02 notes do not mention a wipe (silence is not evidence either way) | [6][7][14] |

The only official text that touches the penalty is framing: stakes are "high" and "every decision" affects the balance [1][3]. A 7 Apr 2026 post adds that a metagame (a Black Market and Vault, and a skills and challenge system) is being built during Early Access, with no economic detail [8].

## Player-reported mechanics

All items in this section are player-reported, dated before Season 02 (12 to 17 Sep 2026), and not confirmed officially. The 0.2.0 interface change to Rebuy Last Loadout [14] may have altered how the "Re-buy Loadout" option described below looks and works.

| Claim | Source and date | Notes |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Unrevived death: "that kit is gone and the next one comes out of the same wallet" | allthings.how, updated 12 Sep 2026 [9] | No dollar figure given |
| Being revived "keeps the loadout you already paid for" | [9] | Consistent with the revive-as-income framing |
| "Re-buy Loadout" rebuilds the previous kit at the vendor | KeenGamer, 17 Sep 2026 [10] | No price stated; whether it costs more than a manual purchase is unknown |
| A helicopter crash "takes your loadout, their loadout, and everyone else in the cabin" | [9] | Wording for pilot and passengers; not tested |
| Repeated deaths can drain reserves | [10] | Qualitative only |
| Destroyed or abandoned vehicle: pay the spawn price again | GameBrief, 17 Sep 2026, figures for the 14 Sep 2026 patch [11] | Repair at a Repair Station with Mechanical Supplies avoids repaying [11] |
| Basic Parachute $100, described as inexpensive insurance against losing a loadout in a damaged aircraft | [10] | Not an actual insurance mechanic |
| Emergency Resuscitator free, usable once per life | [10] | Not tested |
| Defibrillator $1,600 when bought for a loadout | [10] | Also in combat-loadouts-foundation |

## Low and zero cash

No source describes what the game does when the balance cannot cover a loadout, whether a minimal free kit exists, or whether the balance can go negative. The allthings.how guide notes only that there is "no per-round reset to bail you out" and advises checking the balance before each rebuy [9]. The KeenGamer guide advises not building a loadout so expensive that "several deaths destroy your cash reserves" [10]. Neither describes a floor (player-reported). Two other facts bear indirectly: Bulkhead resets cash and XP to 0 as an anti-exploit penalty, which implies zero is a valid state [6][7], and the Emergency Resuscitator is reported free [10].

## Vehicle loss costs

Vehicles are bought per life at a spawn price (player-reported) [11]. Official Season 1 changelog prices for vehicle-class items are in the baseline table [5]; Season 02 re-priced many vehicles (for example L2A6 $14,000 to $22,000 and Havoc $18,000 to $28,000 in vendor prices, and new vehicles such as the T-72B3 at $16,000), held in price-tables-season-1 [14]. The changelog does not say whether each figure is a one-time unlock payment or the recurring per-life price, so the repayment cost after a loss cannot be derived from official text alone (see Open Questions).

text:
WARDOGS runs a persistent cash economy. Every player starts with $10,000, team-play actions earn cash, cash carries from match to match, and each life the player buys a loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1][5]. Bulkhead states that in-game cash and Gold Bars "must be earned through play" and will never be sold for real money [6][10]. Cash can also be exchanged for Gold Bars, the "endgame currency" for cosmetic unlocks in the Gold Market [5]. The UK Steam price is £36.99 (Standard), with a £45.99 Supporter Edition and a £11.99 Supporter Pack DLC that is cosmetic only [1][10].

Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) went live on 15 Oct 2026 [20]. Its official patch notes (posted 14 Oct) rebalance the economy broadly: new per-action cash and XP rewards, lower base logistics pay with new delivery streaks, around 30% lower spotting rewards, a full vendor price pass, a faster role-track XP curve for levels 10 to 50, and a build-cost pass [19]. They also add a Rebuy Last Loadout interface change, a Gold Market camo rotation with the Gold Market itself listed as a WARDOG-track unlock, Lonestar faction bonuses, a losing-team vendor discount, and a Wager Vendor that is not available at launch [19]. This KB holds the numbers in the depth documents (price-tables-season-1 and cash-rewards-and-costs); this foundation summarises them.

Two areas are still not settled by official text. The patch notes do not mention a death-penalty rule or a Season 02 progression wipe or automatic cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion; their silence is not evidence either way [19]. The wipe claim remains press and player-reported, traced to a 7 Apr 2026 devlog video that is not in any Steam post [17]. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot, so later hotfixes are neither confirmed nor ruled out.

Document confidence is Medium: the loop, Season 02 changes, prices and monetisation are official, but the death penalty and seasonal wipe are unverified, so the document cannot be rated higher while they stay open.

All facts below are for Early Access, as of Update 0.2.0 (official posts through 2026-10-15; snapshot 2026-10-30) unless dated otherwise.

- Starting balance is $10,000 on the Steam page (checked 2026-10-08); the Season 02 notes do not state a starting balance [1][19].
- Every teamplay action rewards cash, the Hot Zone yields double cash, and cash persists between matches [1][5].
- Each life, the player buys a custom loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1][5].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars, used for cosmetic unlocks in the Gold Market (18 Feb 2026 FAQ; not restated in later posts) [5].
- Bulkhead states: no monetization during Early Access apart from the optional Supporter Edition; cash and Gold Bars must be earned through play; camos cannot be bought directly [6][10].
- Steam lists Standard at £36.99, Supporter Edition at £45.99 and the Supporter Pack DLC at £11.99; the DLC contains cosmetics only (see editions-pricing-platforms) [1][10].
- The Steam page says the team plans lower Early Access pricing and may raise it nearer full release; Early Access is expected to last around 1 to 2 years [1].
- The latest official version in the snapshot is Update 0.2.0, released 15 Oct 2026 after a maintenance window of 08:00 to 09:30 UTC [19][20]. Before it, Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep) [2] and two 2 Oct posts, a security and stability hotfix notice and an IR Rangefinder and CIWS balance hotfix, applied [8][9]. The 2026-10-30 snapshot holds no official post after 15 Oct.
- Season 02 reward, price and build-cost changes are summarised in Detail and held in price-tables-season-1 and cash-rewards-and-costs [19].
- The Gold Market is listed as a WARDOG-track unlock at level 35 for $150k, and eight Gold Market camos are listed for Season 02 (Black & Gold AK removed) [19].
- Rebuy Last Loadout now pre-fills the equipment vendor with the previous loadout, editable before purchase [19].
- Lonestar has Season 02-only cash and XP win bonuses and teamplay multipliers; any team 40 or more points behind second place gets a 20% vendor discount [19].
- The Wager Vendor is not available at launch and will open later in Season 02 [19].
