text:
## Season 02 economy changes at a glance

The Season 02 patch notes (14 Oct 2026, live as Update 0.2.0 on 15 Oct) change the economy in these areas; this document summarises and the depth documents hold the figures [19][20]:

| Area | What 0.2.0 changed | Detail document |
|------|--------------------|-----------------|
| Action rewards | New assault-weapon kill bonus ($1,500 to $2,000), FOB hacking teammate reward, Halligan door-breach reward, FOB destruction bonus | cash-rewards-and-costs |
| Logistics | Lower base pay plus delivery streaks (values revised in-post to include the zone multiplier) | cash-rewards-and-costs |
| Spotting and destroyed rewards | Spotting rewards around 30% lower than Season 1; per-variant vehicle-destroyed rewards; buildable rewards match build supply cost | cash-rewards-and-costs |
| Exploit fixes | Diminishing returns on selling from a supply crate; no reward for selling to an enemy player; FOB Supplied Assist split between assisting players | cash-rewards-and-costs |
| Vendor prices | New weapons, attachments, magazines, gear and vehicles; many increases and decreases | price-tables-season-1 |
| Role-track XP | Level 20 total XP 250,000 to 111,500 ("55% quicker") | progression-unlock-tables |
| Build costs | Full pass on build supply costs and speed; drill rig, Talon and Mortar rebalanced | fob-and-base-building |
| Faction and discounts | Lonestar bonuses; 20% losing-team vendor discount; server-seeding rewards and vendor discount (no values stated) | this document |
| Gold Market | Camo rotation; Gold Market listed as a level 35 WARDOG unlock | season-reset-and-currencies |
| Loadout | Rebuy Last Loadout interface change | death-penalty-and-rebuy |
| Wager Vendor | Not available at launch; opens later in Season 2 | this document |

The 0.2.0 notes do not state any change to the $10,000 starting balance, a Season 02 progression wipe, a Gold Bar conversion or a death-penalty rule [19].

## Faction bonuses, discounts and the Wager Vendor

Faction balance experiment (Season 02 only): the notes list a Lonestar cash and XP win bonus and Lonestar teamplay-action cash and XP multipliers, with no values stated; the notes also say community server hosts seen exploiting the faction bonus will be punished [19]. The preview post of 9 Oct 2026 lists the same items and frames them as a "social experiment" about the blue team's win rate [18]. A new vendor discount applies to the losing team: 20% off if they are at least 40 points behind second place, for all teams [19]. Players who join and populate empty servers earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins, with no values stated [19].

Wager Vendor: the notes say it lets a player bet their own cash on their own performance, with a live wager tracker above the minimap, and that it "is not available at Season 2 launch" and "will open later in Season 2"; it is "not a permanent addition" and is intended to come and go within a season [19]. The preview adds that players choose objectives, set how many deaths they will spend, and set a stake, with longer odds for stacked objectives, and that it may be pulled if exploitable [18]. Whether it has opened is unknown: the snapshot holds no official post after 15 Oct.

## Earning cash

Season 1 (to Update 0.1.2): official sources confirmed which actions pay (revives, transport, kills, spotting, "and MORE") and that the Hot Zone yields double cash [5], but published no per-action dollar amounts. The only official reward figure was a one-week 5% community-server end-of-match cash bonus from 14 Sep 2026 [3]. Season 02 (Update 0.2.0): the 14 Oct patch notes publish per-action amounts for the first time (for example assault kill bonus $1,500 to $2,000, Deploy Supply Pallet $2,500 to $1,250) [19]; they are held in cash-rewards-and-costs. Update 0.1.2 made revive checks server authoritative, capped vehicle fly-through rewards, scaled buildable-destruction rewards with build progress (a placed schematic no longer pays in full) and reduced pallet-deposit rewards outside a FOB zone, with no values stated [2]. Community guides add income sources and no amounts (player-reported) [15]. See cash-rewards-and-costs.

## Spending cash

Cash buys the per-life loadout [1]. Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) revised the vendor price list again, for example Basic Parachute $100 to $500, L2A6 $14,000 to $22,000 and new vehicles such as the T-72B3 at $16,000; the full Season 02 list is in price-tables-season-1 [19]. As dated history, the Season 1 launch changelog (post of 9 Sep 2026, Season 1.0 live 10 Sep) listed these official price changes [4]; some of these items were re-priced or re-gated in 0.2.0 (for example the Little Bird with miniguns now unlocks at level 8 for $125k) [19]:

| Item | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| Forward Operating Base (vendor) | $2,500 | $7,500 |
| Large Hammer (vendor) | $1,600 | $2,400 |
| Support Medium Hammer | $10,000 | $25,000 |
| Support Large Hammer | $25,000 | $75,000 |
| Career Artillery Tank | $400,000 | $500,000 |
| Pilot Little Bird with miniguns | $25,000 | $50,000 |
| Pilot Z20 Lakota | $50,000 | $35,000 |
| Driver URAL | $50,000 | $35,000 |
| Driver Dune Buggy | $35,000 | $25,000 |
| Driver Kodiak Flatbed | $15,000 | $35,000 |

The same list also moves scope, small supply crate and Music Tape H prices and rescales the supply-crate purchase curve from 25 to 250 down to 1 to 200 [4]. The Kodiak Flatbed is an official increase, and its unlock level moved from 2 to 10 [4]; the full table is in price-tables-season-1. The changelog does not say whether a price is a one-time unlock payment or a per-life price.

Per-spawn vehicle prices (for example $500 for a Bobcat, about $8,000 for the SPH-2, about $18,000 for the Havoc) are community measurements, not an official table (player-reported) [16].

## Death penalty

Official pages say a loadout is bought each life and that outcomes feed the balance [1][12], but no official post, including the Season 02 patch notes, states the loss on death, any re-buy price, refund or zero-cash rule (all saved official posts checked, 2026-10-30) [19]. Update 0.2.0 did change the Rebuy Last Loadout interface: the old placeholder UI was removed and the vendor is pre-filled with the last loadout, which can be edited before purchase [19]. Community guides report that a downed player who is not revived loses the kit bought for that life, the next kit is paid from the same balance, and a helicopter crash can destroy pilot and passenger loadouts (player-reported) [15][16]. See death-penalty-and-rebuy.

## Currencies, persistence and seasons

Cash persists between matches and can be exchanged for Gold Bars [5]. Each season will have "a different XP curve with different item orders" [4]. Official: bans for cash exploits reset an offender's cash and XP to 0 [3]. Season 02 gold-related facts: the notes list eight Gold Market skins (Black & Gold Little Bird as a Season 2 exclusive; Chocolate Chip, Two-Tone Desert and Digital Wood families), remove the Black & Gold AK camo, and list "Gold Market (LVL 35, $150k)" among WARDOG-track additional unlocks [19]. Not in any official post, including the Season 02 notes (which do not mention it): that every player's cash and XP reset at season end and that leftover cash converts automatically to Gold Bars. This is relayed by press and a seller from a 7 Apr 2026 devlog video, not by the Steam post of that date, which only announces the planned Metagame (Black Market, Vault, skills and challenges) [11][17] (press and player-reported). The conversion rate is unpublished. See season-reset-and-currencies.

## Monetization

| Product | Price (Steam, 2026-10-08) |
|---------|---------------------------|
| WARDOGS | £36.99 [1] |
| Supporter Edition | £45.99 [1] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC) | £11.99 [1][10] |

The Supporter Pack holds three Starter Weapon camos (Valkyra A-91, Lonestar Bushmaster, Manticore KH-2002), a Littlebird "Taxi" camo, a hideable scoreboard supporter icon and two bobbleheads; no gameplay item is listed [10][6]. The launch press release quoted $39.99 USD for Early Access [12]; the 11 Aug post refers to "stair stepped pricing" without figures [6]. Regional prices are in editions-pricing-platforms.

text:
This document holds the vendor prices the studio has published for WARDOGS, in two dated layers. Layer one is the Season 1 baseline: the "Economy Changes" section of the Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep 2026, live 10 Sep), which gives 15 repriced items with old and new values [1]. Layer two is the "Vendor Price Changes" section of the Season 02 Patch Notes (posted 14 Oct 2026, released as Update 0.2.0 on 15 Oct 2026), which publishes prices for 28 new items, 32 price increases, 14 price decreases and 8 headline attachment decreases, each change with old and new values [7][8]. Store prices come from the Steam store data snapshot [5][6].

Important limit: both lists cover only what the studio chose to print. Prices of items not named in either list are not published in any official source found, so this is a complete list of published prices and changes, not a complete shop catalogue. No official post after 15 Oct 2026 is present in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

Confidence is High because every value is quoted from an official Steam post or the Steam store data; no player-reported figures are used.

text:
This document covers seasons and currencies as of Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, live 15 October 2026), keeping the 2026-10-08 pre-Season-02 baseline as dated history. Official Steam posts confirm that cash persists from match to match, that cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars, that Gold Bars are the "endgame currency" for cosmetic unlocks in a "Gold Market", that Gold Bars and cash will never be sold for real money, and that each season gets its own XP curve and item order [2][3][4]. The Season 02 patch notes (14 Oct 2026) add Gold Market content: eight new weapon and vehicle skins, the removal of the Black & Gold AK camo, and a "Gold Market (LVL 35, $150k)" entry among WARDOG-track unlocks [14]. They also publish a new, faster role-track XP curve for levels 10 to 50, a Season 02 curve change in line with the "different XP curve each season" statement [4][14].

The explicit rule that a season end resets cash and XP, auto-converts leftover cash to Gold Bars, and keeps Gold Bars and cosmetics permanently is NOT in any Steam post in the local snapshot, and the Season 02 patch notes and release post do not mention a wipe, a reset or a Gold Bar conversion [14][15]. That silence is not evidence either way. The claim is attributed to a 7 April 2026 BULKHEAD devlog and is relayed by Vice, KeenGamer and Timesaver.gg [10][11][12]. The conversion rate is unpublished everywhere. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

Confidence is Medium: the currency model and the Season 02 Gold Market changes are official, but the wipe mechanics are second-hand and unconfirmed.

- Official: "Cash earned persists in your account from match to match", and cash can be exchanged "for GOLD BARS - the endgame currency used to obtain cosmetic unlocks in the GOLD MARKET" (Steam post, 18 Feb 2026) [2].
- Official: BULKHEAD "will NEVER monetize in-game cash or gold bars" and will never allow direct purchase of camos (Steam post, 11 Aug 2026) [3].
- Official: "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" (Season 1 changelog, 9 Sep 2026) [4].
- Official: Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) went live 15 October 2026 after a 08:00 to 09:30 UTC maintenance window [14][15].
- Official (Season 02 patch notes, 14 Oct 2026): eight Gold Market skins across four camo families (Black & Gold Little Bird is a Season 2 exclusive), the Black & Gold AK camo removed from the Gold Market, and Gold Market listed as a WARDOG-track unlock at level 35 for $150k [14].
- Official: Season 02 changed the role-track XP curve for levels 10 to 50 (for example level 20: 250,000 to 111,500 total XP) [14].
- The Season 02 notes and release post do not mention a progression wipe, a cash and XP reset, or an automatic cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion [14][15].
- Press (quoting a devlog not in the snapshot): at season end cash and XP reset, leftover cash auto-converts to Gold Bars, and Gold Bars and cosmetics persist permanently [10][11][12]. Still unconfirmed officially.
- Not published anywhere found: the cash-to-Gold-Bar rate, and whether the starting cash is again $10,000 (the notes state no starting balance) [14].
- Official: exploit sanctions already reset cash and XP to 0 for individuals, a separate mechanism from any seasonal reset [5][6].

text:
- **Season**: a content and progression cycle; "Season 1.0" is the label for the 10 Sep 2026 launch changelog [4].
- **Cash**: persistent in-game currency, earned by teamplay and spent on loadouts [2][9].
- **Gold Bars**: the "endgame currency" obtained by exchanging cash, spent on cosmetics [2].
- **Gold Market**: the named store for cosmetic unlocks bought with Gold Bars [2].
- **Wipe / reset**: loss of cash and XP progression; in this KB "seasonal reset" is the press-reported end-of-season event, distinct from the exploit-sanction reset [5][10]. Not mentioned in the Season 02 notes [14].

text:
As of Update 0.2.0 (official posts through 2026-10-15; snapshot 2026-10-30):

- Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) is live: the patch notes were posted 14 Oct 2026 and the release post on 15 Oct 2026 says servers were back online [14][15]. No official post after 15 Oct is in the snapshot, so later hotfixes are neither confirmed nor ruled out.
- Cash persists between matches [2][9].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars; Gold Bars buy cosmetics in the Gold Market (18 Feb 2026 FAQ, not restated in later posts, including the Season 02 notes) [2][14].
- The Season 02 notes list eight new Gold Market skins, remove the Black & Gold AK camo, and list "Gold Market (LVL 35, $150k)" under WARDOG-track additional unlocks [14].
- Neither cash nor Gold Bars is ever to be sold, and camos are not to be purchasable directly [3].
- The only real-money item is the optional Supporter Edition (cosmetics) [3][9].
- The Season 02 XP curve for levels 10 to 50 is faster than Season 1 (see Detail) [14].
- The Season 02 notes mention no progression wipe, reset or Gold Bar conversion; whether one happened at the 15 Oct launch is unconfirmed officially [14][15].
- The studio frames progression as "continue earning, progressing and adding value to your account even when not in a match" via a planned Metagame, including a Black Market and Vault and a Skills and Challenge system, built during Early Access [7]. The Season 02 notes do not list these [14].
- Superseded: the 22 Sep teaser (only "WARDOGS Season 02 is coming. 15th October 2026.") [1] and the 30 Sep promise of more information "next week" [5] are resolved by the 9 Oct preview, 14 Oct notes and 15 Oct release [13][14][15].

## Gold Bars: the Timesaver claim

Timesaver.gg claims leftover cash converts to Gold Bars and that Gold Bars and cosmetics are "the only things that survive" the wipe, and sells in-game cash [12]. Assessment: partly confirmed, confidence Medium. The Gold Bar currency, the cash exchange and the cosmetic role are in an official Steam post [2], and Vice and KeenGamer independently relay the same end-of-season rule [10][11]. The part still without a readable official text is the automatic conversion and permanence; Timesaver cites the 7 April devlog for it [12]. The official 7 April Steam post only announces the Metagame and links a video [7]. The Season 02 patch notes, released after this claim circulated, do not mention conversion [14]. Timesaver also has a commercial interest in cash, so its "spend first" advice and rate remarks are not evidence.

Rain: Vice reported BULKHEAD said on X that rain is an additional per-map weather state [10]. The official notes list a "New Rain Weather Preset" in Season 02 [14]. Not economy; see the weather docs.

## Season 02 Gold Market and unlock changes (Update 0.2.0)

From the 14 Oct 2026 patch notes [14]:

| Item | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|------|-------------------|
| New Gold Market skins | Eight, in four families: Black & Gold (Little Bird, "Season 2 Exclusive Gold Market Camo"); Chocolate Chip (Evo-3 Ultra, M14, TCX-SPR); Two-Tone Desert (Galil, Mosin, Havoc); Digital Wood (M500) |
| Removed | Black & Gold AK camo removed from the Gold Market |
| Gold Market unlock | WARDOG track, level 35, $150k (listed under additional unlocks) |

The notes do not say how the Gold Market is accessed before level 35, what Gold Bar prices apply, or whether owned Gold Market cosmetics carry over (not stated). Before this, the Gold Market was described only in the pre-launch FAQ [2].

## Season 02 XP curve (Update 0.2.0)

Total XP required per role-track level, as listed in the 14 Oct 2026 notes ("from" values are as the notes state them) [14]:

| 15 | 110,000 | 54,750 | 50% quicker |

| 25 | 365,000 | 206,600 | 43% quicker |
| 30 | 500,000 | 318,200 | 36% quicker |

| 40 | 975,000 | 712,500 | 27% quicker |
| 45 | 1,225,000 | 920,850 | 25% quicker |
| 50 | 1,500,000 | 1,150,000 | 23% quicker |

The notes' "from" values for levels 25 to 50 differ from the Season 1.0 changelog values recorded in the baseline table below (for example level 25: 325,000 in [4]); the level 10 to 20 values agree. The reason is not stated in either post. Full unlock tables are in progression-unlock-tables.

## Account checks to settle the wipe question

Because the notes are silent, these in-game checks would resolve it (none has been done by this pipeline):

1. Own account: cash balance, per-track level and XP for all six tracks, Gold Bar count, owned cosmetics, compared with any values noted before 15 Oct.
2. Whether the Gold Market UI shows an exchange rate or a conversion notice (no rate is published) [2][11].
3. Whether starting cash is again $10,000 [9].
4. Whether a progression reset notice appeared at the 0.2.0 deploy.

## Exploit-reset precedent

Separate from seasons, the 0.11 and 0.1.2 posts state that exploiters receive a timed ban and "We will reset your cash and XP to 0", and that anyone caught with economy exploits or real-money trading "has had their cash and progression reset" [5][6].

title: Control Zone & Match Flow
topic: Match lifecycle, Control Zone and Hot Zone scoring, win conditions, spawning, team balance

text:
The official sources describe the match loop in a few sentences: three teams contest a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside a 256 km2 map, the team with the most players inside earns points, and the first to 100 points wins [1][2]. A Hot Zone is a shifting sub-zone inside the Control Zone where each player counts double towards the player count and cash is doubled [2]. That remains the whole of the officially published scoring rule; Update 0.2.0 (15 Oct 2026) did not change it [14].

Everything finer-grained is player-reported: the 30-second scoring tick, one point per tick, the tower and code mechanic that drags the Hot Zone, the deployment board, the APC spawn and its cooldown [12][13]. No official source published at 2026-10-08 states respawn timers, spawn placement rules, team-balance rules or match length. Update 0.2.0 added official match-flow rules around the loop: team-switch restrictions once a team is more than 10 points ahead, a victim-driven Forgive/Punish vote on team kills, a Squad Intent UI, server seeding rewards with pre-match entertainment, a 20% vendor discount for a team at least 40 points behind second place, and a Lonestar faction experiment [14]. The Season 01 baseline is kept below as dated history.

Confidence is Medium. The core rule and the 0.2.0 rules rest on the Steam page, the Top Questions post and the Season 02 patch notes; spawn, tick and tower detail still rests on player-reported guides, which may not raise a claim above Medium. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

text:
- Win condition: first team to 100 points wins; the team with the most players inside the Control Zone earns points (official, stated 18 Feb 2026 and on the store page, unchanged through 2 Oct 2026) [1][2].
- Hot Zone: officially a shifting sub-zone; players count as double towards the player count and it yields double cash [2].
- Map scale: the Control Zone is 2x2 km inside a 256 km2 map, so it is a fraction of the map [2].
- Tick rate and points per tick are not official; one player-reported guide says one point per 30 seconds [12][13].
- Official posts still do not publish respawn timers, spawn rules or team-balance logic; the Deploy flow added in 0.1.2 is a server-browser screen, not an in-match spawn screen [7].
- Team switching (0.2.0, notes of 14 Oct 2026): once a team is more than 10 points ahead, a player cannot switch teams again for 15 minutes after joining one, their map stays obscured until they first reach the Control Zone, and they cannot use the spawn vehicle until then [14].
- Team kills (0.2.0): the victim chooses Forgive or Punish; Punish marks accumulate towards kicks and escalating bans; leaving the safe zone after respawning without voting forgives automatically [14].
- Squads have no size limit and give extra UI, communication tools and vehicle locking [2].
- The "Tactical Depth & Teamplay" post is a video wrapper; its text states only that decisions affect account balance [4].

text:
Season 01 statements verified 2026-10-08; Update 0.2.0 statements verified 2026-10-30 against the 14 Oct patch notes [14] and the 15 Oct release post [16].

- Up to 100 players in three teams fight over one Control Zone [1][2]. Official team names are Lonestar, Valkyra and Manticore (18 Feb 2026) [2].
- The Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area within a 256 km2 map; zone location varies per match [2].
- The team with the most players in the zone earns points; the first team to 100 points wins [1][2].
- The Hot Zone is a shifting sub-zone; players count double towards player count and it pays double cash [2].
- Players start with $10,000 and buy a loadout each life; cash persists between matches [1][2].
- Squad size is unlimited; squads get extra UI, communication tools and vehicle locking [2].
- The live store page uses both phrases: "proximity voice chat" in the Early Access state list and "local voice chat" in About This Game; the 18 Feb 2026 post says proximity chat [1][2].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026): revive validity checks are now fully server authoritative, vehicle fly-through rewards are capped, buildable-destruction rewards scale with build progress, and depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone pays reduced rewards [7].
- 2 Oct 2026 balance hotfix: IR Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02 (where they will require batteries); the CIWS destroys the Havoc in about 6 seconds instead of 12 [8].
- Season 02 was dated 15 Oct 2026 by the 22 Sep teaser and released as Update 0.2.0 on 15 Oct 2026; servers were back online per the release post [7][9][16].
- 0.2.0 team switching: once a team is more than 10 points ahead, a player cannot switch teams again for 15 minutes after joining one; if they switch or join a match in progress their map stays obscured until they first reach the Control Zone, and they cannot use the spawn vehicle until then. The notes say this adds friction for team-switch abusers while still letting players join friends [14].
- 0.2.0 team kills: when a teammate kills you, you are asked to Forgive or Punish; Punish results accumulate against the teamkiller, leading to kicks and escalating bans for repeat offenders; Forgive removes a potential mark; respawning and then leaving the safe zone without voting forgives automatically [14]. Thresholds for kicks and bans are not stated.
- 0.2.0 Squad Intent UI: squad leaders can set a team-visible intent from a pre-defined list, shown on the squad list before a player chooses to join; squad invites and other timed prompts now queue [14].
- 0.2.0 server seeding and pre-match entertainment: players who join and populate empty servers earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins; before the match, each spawn has guns with targets, a football and a hidden radio [14]. Reward and discount sizes are not stated.
- 0.2.0 Lonestar faction experiment (Season 2 only): Lonestar cash and XP win bonus and Lonestar teamplay-action cash and XP multipliers, with sizes not stated; all faction spawns on Bakurani were moved and rebuilt with purpose-built routes to the zone; community-server hosts seen exploiting the faction bonus will be punished [14]. The developer calls it a social experiment prompted by Lonestar's lower win rate and uniform visibility [14]. The preview adds that Lonestar uniforms are more desaturated [15].
- 0.2.0 losing-team discount: any team at least 40 points behind second place gets 20% off vendor purchases; this applies to all teams, not just Lonestar [14].
- 0.2.0 assistance request ping timer: 20 s to 60 s [14].
- 0.2.0 parachutes: longer to open, no opening below about 10 m, fall damage if opened below roughly 50 m while falling fast; prices are in price-tables-season-1 [14].
- 0.2.0 controller changes (summary): Aim Assist strength slider in Settings > Controller > Advanced (default 1, 0 is off), Aim Assist on Firing Range target dummies, adjusted sensitivity and Aim Acceleration, and rebinds including Cycle Minimap Zoom and Reject Tip on View, Deploy Crate on D-Pad Up (hold), and squad invite accept/reject moved to View/Menu [14].
- 0.2.0 Wager Vendor: not available at launch, opens later in Season 2, not permanent [14][15].

text:
## Baseline values

All values are as of Season 01, 0.1.2 plus 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes, unless a different date is shown. The 0.2.0 notes change none of the scoring or zone values, and the Season 02 rows are at the end. "Official" means developer-published; "PR" means player-reported.

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Max players per match: 100 | Season 01 (store page, 18 Feb 2026 post) | Official [1][2] |
| Teams: 3 (Lonestar, Valkyra, Manticore) | Season 01 | Official [2] |
| Win threshold: 100 points | Season 01 | Official [1][2] |
| Control Zone size: 2x2 km, randomised | Season 01 | Official [1][2] |
| Map size: 256 km2 | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Hot Zone presence weight: x2 per player | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Hot Zone cash multiplier: x2 | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Starting cash: $10,000 | Season 01 | Official [1] |
| Squad size: unlimited | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Scoring tick: 30 s, 1 point to leader | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [12][13] |
| Players per team: about 33 | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Capture towers per Control Zone: 3 to 5 | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Drill rig activation: 6,000 fuel | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Zone occupation pay: $160 (Control Zone), $320 (Hot Zone) per cycle | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| M113 APC unlock: any faction at 20 points | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| APC spawn personal cooldown: 10 minutes | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| New Recruit discount: 50% until account level 9 | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Match length: can exceed 1 hour | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| CIWS time to destroy Havoc: about 6 s (was 12 s) | 2 Oct 2026 hotfix | Official [8] |
| IR Rangefinder: disabled in vendor until Season 02 | 2 Oct 2026 hotfix | Official [8] |
| Community-server end-of-match cash bonus: 5% for one week | 0.11, 14 Sep 2026 (expired) | Official [6] |
| Season 02 date: 15 Oct 2026 | Teaser 22 Sep 2026; released 15 Oct | Official [9][16] |
| Team-switch lock: 15 min, when a team is more than 10 points ahead | 0.2.0, 14 Oct 2026 | Official [14] |
| Losing-team vendor discount: 20% at 40+ points behind second | 0.2.0, 14 Oct 2026 | Official [14] |
| Assistance ping timer: 60 s (was 20 s) | 0.2.0, 14 Oct 2026 | Official [14] |

## Match lifecycle

| Stage | What is known | Class |
|-------|---------------|-------|
| 0. Seeding (0.2.0) | Players who populate an empty server earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins; pre-match entertainment is available before the match [14] | Official |
| 1. Find a server | From 0.1.2, Deploy offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level lists; the browsers were split into Official and Community in 0.11; a queue position is shown after Join [6][7] | Official |
| 2. Spawn and buy | Buy a loadout each life at the Equipment Vendor in the Safe Zone, then spawn through the deployment board; "Rebuy Last Loadout" restores the previous kit [1][12][13] | Store page official; interface detail PR |
| 3. Reach the zone | Transporting friendlies to the zone earns cash; ground vehicles and helicopters carry players [1][13] | Official / PR |
| 4. Contest | The team with most players in the zone earns points; Hot Zone doubles presence [1][2] | Official |
| 5. End | First team to 100 points wins [1][2] | Official |

Not published officially: what happens after a win (map rotation, scoreboard, lobby return), match-length targets and round time limits. Assessment: the lifecycle after step 5 cannot be described from sources; confidence Low.

## Control Zone and scoring

Officially, scoring is a comparison of player counts inside the zone, awarding points to the leader, to a threshold of 100 [1][2]. The official text does not say how often points are awarded, whether a tie awards points, or whether the margin matters. One player-reported guide gives a 30-second check with one point to the leading team, which implies a minimum of about 50 minutes (100 checks) if a team leads every check [13]. Assessment: that figure is arithmetic on a player-reported tick, not a measured match length; confidence Low. The same guide says matches can pass an hour [13].

## Hot Zone

Official: a shifting sub-zone within the Control Zone; players count as double towards player count, "leading to match-swinging potential", and it yields double cash [2]. The store page repeats "chase the Hot Zone to earn double the cash" [1].

Player-reported: it appears as a yellow sub-zone on the tactical map with a circular minimap outline; size and relocation interval are not published [12]. A second guide describes a drifting circle that can be pulled toward a tower by entering a master code, and toward a player FOB by a fuel-fed drill rig [13]. These tower and rig mechanics are not described in any official post read for this document.

## Three-team dynamics

The developer designed three teams so that the zone is a three-way contest, with a lore split: Lonestar (Western paramilitary), Valkyra (Soviet-revival) and Manticore (Persian shadow army) [2]. Because points go to the team with the most players, a team can lead while outnumbered by the other two combined; this follows from the rule as stated and is an inference (Assessment: confidence Medium; basis: the scoring rule at [2]). No official source states how players are assigned to teams or whether teams are balanced to equal size. The 0.11 post listed "Team Switching Controls" and "AFK kicking during seeding disabling" as upcoming features on 12 Sep 2026 [6]; team switching restrictions shipped in 0.2.0 (next section), while the notes do not mention AFK-kick changes [14]. A player-reported guide gives about 33 players per team [13].

## Team switching restrictions (0.2.0)

Aim stated in the notes: stop late switching from deciding matches. Trigger: a team more than 10 points ahead. Effects: no switching teams again for 15 minutes after joining one; the map stays obscured until the first arrival at the Control Zone after a switch or a mid-match join; the spawn vehicle is unusable until then [14]. Whether it is a server setting is not stated.

## Team-kill Forgive / Punish (0.2.0)

Victim-driven vote after a teammate kills you. Punish accumulates marks leading to kicks and escalating bans; Forgive removes a potential mark; respawning and leaving the safe zone without voting forgives automatically [14]. Mark counts, ban lengths and any difference between Official and Community servers are not stated.

## Squads, Squad Intent and prompts (0.2.0)

Squad leaders choose a team-visible intent from a pre-defined list (the entries are not listed in the notes); it shows on the squad list before joining. Squad invites and other timed prompts now queue [14]. Squad size remains unlimited per the 18 Feb 2026 post [2]; the notes do not change it.

## Server seeding, pre-match entertainment and the losing-team discount (0.2.0)

Seeding: rewards and a vendor discount for players who join and populate empty servers, granted once the match begins. Pre-match entertainment: guns with targets, a football and a hidden radio in each spawn [14]. Separately, the Lonestar experiment adds a Season 2 win bonus and teamplay multipliers for Lonestar, and a 20% vendor discount for any team at least 40 points behind second place [14]. The notes give no sizes for the bonuses, seeding rewards or seeding discount; cash and XP figures are owned by cash-rewards-and-costs and vendor prices by price-tables-season-1.

## Ping limits and Wager Vendor (pointers)

Region-based ping limits and server-browser ping filters arrived in 0.2.0; see server-hosting-and-browser [14]. The Wager Vendor is not available at launch and opens later in Season 2 [14]; see gameplay-modes-foundation.

## Spawn, respawn and deploy

- Official: the 0.1.2 Deploy flow is a pre-match server selection screen aimed at steering players to Infantry Mode and Low-Level servers [7].
- Official: revive validity checks are server authoritative from 0.1.2 [7].
- Player-reported: loadout purchase at the Equipment Vendor, then spawn via the deployment board [12].
- Player-reported: there is no squad spawning; an M113 APC unlocks once any faction reaches 20 points, the deployment computer can teleport you to an allied APC with a 10-minute personal cooldown, and destroying an APC's satellite dish disables its spawn function [13].
- Player-reported: reviving is cheaper than respawning [13]. Revive duration is not given [12].
- Official (0.2.0): all three Bakurani team spawns were moved and rebuilt with purpose-built routes to the zone [14]. Map detail is owned by maps-environment-foundation.
- Not published: respawn timer, spawn point distribution, spawn protection, spawn-camping rules.

## Developer statements on intended tactical play

The "Tactical Depth & Teamplay" post (21 May 2026) gives three bullets: real-world ballistics, audio and flight models; every decision affects your account balance; a 100% player-driven militaristic sandbox. It frames a Debrief video on three pillars of tactical depth [4]. The post text names no mechanic more specific than that; the video content is not transcribed in the snapshot. Related official statements elsewhere:

- "Teamplay isn't encouraged, it's rewarded": revives, transport, kills, spotting and more pay cash in the zone [2].
- Roles are player-defined by purchased gear, earning XP across six tracks [2].
- "There are no set rules of engagement"; examples include chasing the Hot Zone, sniping in a ghillie suit, helicopter supply runs, building a forward operating base at a chokepoint, and artillery tanks [1].
- The mode was developed with the original ARMA King of the Hill mod creators as a standalone KOTH-inspired shooter [3].
- A 16 Jun 2026 devlog says the line between arcade and realistic has been drawn by the developer, without stating mechanics [5].

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter in Steam Early Access since 10 September 2026 [1][2]. Its core mode is the Control Zone: three teams contest a randomised 2x2 km zone inside a 256 km2 map, the team with the most players inside earns points, and the first to 100 points wins [1][2]. A shifting Hot Zone inside it counts each player double and pays double cash [1][2]. Proximity voice chat is listed in the Early Access state and local voice chat in the game description, both on the store page [1][2].

Progression is cash-based, with cash persisting from match to match and exchangeable for Gold Bars, plus XP across six role tracks (Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot) that gate unlocks [2][3]. The developer states that each season gets a different XP curve and item order [3]. Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) went live on 15 October 2026 [20]. The 14 Oct patch notes add team-switching restrictions, a victim-driven Forgive/Punish team-kill vote, a Squad Intent UI, server seeding rewards with pre-match entertainment, a rain weather preset, new weapons, vehicles and buildables, a Lonestar faction experiment, and a Wager Vendor that is not open at launch [18]. The notes do not mention a progression wipe.

Confidence is High for the core claims, which rest on the live store page (live capture 2026-10-08), the Top Questions post, the Season 1 changelog, the 0.11 and 0.1.2 posts, the two 2 Oct posts and the Season 02 patch notes [18]. Level caps, scoring tick, tower mechanics and any Season 02 wipe are not in official text and are kept as player-reported or press-reported. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot; hotfixes after that date are neither confirmed nor ruled out.

text:
- Format: up to 100 players in three teams (Lonestar, Valkyra, Manticore) on a 256 km2 map; Early Access launched with three maps, each with three variations [1][2][12].
- Objective: a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone; the team with the most players inside earns points; first to 100 wins [1][2].
- Hot Zone: a shifting sub-zone where players count as double and cash is doubled [1][2].
- Voice: the store page uses both phrases, "Online multiplayer with proximity voice chat" in its Early Access state list and "local voice chat" in About This Game, and the developer FAQ says proximity chat [1][2]; the claim that it carries across all three teams rests on the Team17 press release [12].
- Progression: cash persists between matches and can be exchanged for Gold Bars [2]; XP accrues across six role tracks named Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [3].
- Seasons: each season has its own XP curve and item order [3]; Season 02 (Update 0.2.0) went live 15 Oct 2026 and the patch notes lower the XP needed per level (summary below; numbers owned by progression-and-role-tracks) [18][20]. The notes do not mention a wipe; a progression wipe is press-reported only [13].
- Update 0.2.0 match-flow changes (14 Oct 2026 notes): team-switch limits once a team is more than 10 points ahead, a Forgive/Punish vote on team kills, Squad Intent UI, server seeding rewards and pre-match entertainment, and a 20% vendor discount for a team at least 40 points behind second place [18]. Detail is in control-zone-and-match-flow.
- Modes: the Control Zone is still the only named core mode; Official servers run no modified modes, while Community servers can; since 0.1.2 a Deploy flow offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level servers [4][5].
- 1.0: no date; the store page plans around 1 to 2 years in Early Access, a higher full-release price and a broader feature set [1]; the 7 Apr 2026 post commits to building a metagame (Black Market and Vault, Player Skills and Challenge System) during Early Access [10].

text:
Season 01 statements were verified 2026-10-08 and the 0.2.0 statements 2026-10-30, each against the sources shown.

- Early Access began 10 Sep 2026; the developer describes it as fully playable and representing the core vision [2]. Setting is the war-torn region of Kolchia [2]; the store page describes the derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe and a destructible battlefield, and calls the game a militaristic sandbox [1].
- Matches support up to 100 players split across three rival teams on a 256 km2 map; squad size is unlimited [2].
- Teams fight for a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone; the team with the most players in the zone earns points and the first to 100 wins [1][2].
- The Hot Zone counts players double and yields double cash [1][2].
- Every player starts with $10,000 and buys a loadout each life; teamplay actions such as reviving, transporting friendlies and controlling the objective earn cash; cash persists between matches [1].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars, used for cosmetics in the Gold Market; the developer says cash and Gold Bars will never be sold for real money [2][9].
- Voice: the store page says "Online multiplayer with proximity voice chat" in its Early Access state list and "local voice chat" in About This Game; the FAQ says proximity chat, including loudspeakers players can construct [1][2].
- Launch content is three maps, each with three variations, with infantry and vehicle combat [12].
- The Season 1 changelog (9 Sep 2026, pre-load) slowed the XP curve and moved unlocks; it also fixed voice dropping after a failed join, push-to-talk targeting and re-login recovery, and added a visible communication status [3].
- Patch 0.11 (14 Sep 2026) split the server browser into Official and Community lists, removed filters from the Official list, and gave Community servers a 5% end-of-match cash bonus for one week [4].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) made revive checks server authoritative, capped fly-through rewards, scaled buildable-destruction rewards by build progress, reduced rewards for FOB pallet deposits outside the zone, added the Deploy flow, and added Advanced Filters back to the Official list [5].
- 2 Oct 2026 brought two official posts: a security and stability hotfix at 08:00 UTC with no gameplay detail, and a balance hotfix disabling IR Rangefinders in the vendor until Season 02 (where they will need batteries) and cutting the CIWS kill time on the Havoc from about 12 s to about 6 s [6][7].
- Season 02 was dated 15 Oct 2026 by the official teaser of 22 Sep 2026 and released as Update 0.2.0 on 15 Oct 2026 (servers back online after a maintenance window announced for 08:00 to 09:30 UTC) [8][18][20]. The Season 01 statements above are the history baseline; the 0.2.0 facts follow.
- 0.2.0 (14 Oct 2026 notes): once a team is more than 10 points ahead, a player cannot switch teams again for 15 minutes after joining one, their map stays obscured until they first reach the Control Zone, and they cannot use the spawn vehicle until then [18].
- 0.2.0: team kills trigger a Forgive or Punish prompt for the victim; Punish marks accumulate towards kicks and escalating bans, Forgive removes a potential mark, and respawning then leaving the safe zone without voting forgives automatically [18].
- 0.2.0: squad leaders can set a team-visible squad intent from a pre-defined list, visible on the squad list before joining; squad invites and other timed prompts now queue [18].
- 0.2.0: players who join and populate empty servers earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins; pre-match entertainment (guns with targets, a football and a hidden radio in each spawn) is available before the match [18].
- 0.2.0: Lonestar faction experiment for Season 2 only, with Lonestar win bonuses and teamplay multipliers, and a new 20% vendor discount for any losing team at least 40 points behind second place; the notes do not state the bonus sizes [18].
- 0.2.0: Wager Vendor (bet your own cash on your own performance) is not available at launch; it will open later in Season 2 and is not a permanent addition [18][19].
- 0.2.0: the rain weather preset, four new weapons, four new vehicles and three new buildables are listed in the notes (owner documents hold the detail), and the assistance ping timer rose from 20 s to 60 s [18].
- 0.2.0: parachutes take longer to open and do not open below about 10 m; opening below roughly 50 m while falling fast causes fall damage; the Basic Parachute rose from $100 to $500 and the Sport Parachute fell from $1,000 to $700 (prices owned by price-tables-season-1) [18].
- 0.2.0: controller changes include an Aim Assist strength slider (Settings > Controller > Advanced; default 1, 0 turns it off), adjusted sensitivity and aim acceleration, and several rebinds; the full bind list is in the notes [18].

text:
## Match format and objectives

| Element | Fact at Season 01 | Source |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| Players | Up to 100 | [1][2] |
| Teams | 3: Lonestar, Valkyra, Manticore | [2] |
| Map size | 256 km2 | [2] |
| Zone | Randomised 2x2 km Control Zone per match | [1][2] |
| Win condition | First team to 100 points | [1][2] |
| Scoring basis | Team with the most players in the zone earns points | [1][2] |
| Hot Zone | Shifting sub-zone; players count double; double cash | [1][2] |
| Squads | Unlimited size; extra UI, comms and vehicle locking | [2] |
| Maps | 3, each with 3 variations | [12] |

Player-reported mechanics (not stated in any official post): a tick of roughly one point every 30 seconds, three to five tower capture points inside the Control Zone, and a code from towers that lets a team drag the Hot Zone toward a held tower [16][17]. Treat these as player-reported. See control-zone-and-match-flow for the full baseline and the unpublished gaps (respawn, spawn rules, team balance).

## Cross-team voice chat

The store page uses both phrases: "Online multiplayer with proximity voice chat" in the Early Access state list and "local voice chat" in About This Game (live capture 2026-10-08); the developer FAQ also calls it proximity chat [1][2]. The two wordings describe the same feature and are not treated as a contradiction. Audibility across teams rests on the Team17 press release, which says it is audible across all three teams [12]. The Season 1 changelog lists fixes to voice cutting out after a failed join, stale channel rejoins, push-to-talk targeting and re-login, and a visible communication status [3].

## Progression and unlocks

| Element | Detail | Source |
|---------|--------|--------|
| Starting cash | $10,000 per player; a loadout is bought each life | [1] |
| Cash earning | Teamplay actions (revives, transport, kills, spotting, objective); Hot Zone doubles cash | [1][2] |
| Cash persistence | Persists match to match; exchangeable for Gold Bars | [2] |
| Role tracks | Six: Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot (the 0.2.0 notes also use "Assault" and "WARDOG" track headings; see progression-and-role-tracks) | [2][3][18] |
| Track cap | Level 100 per track and account level to 600: player-reported only; no official cap | [15] |
| Unlock cost | Reaching a level makes an item buyable; the changelog moves items between levels and tracks | [3] |
| Per-season curve | "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" | [3] |
| Season reset | Not stated in official text, including the 0.2.0 notes, which do not mention a wipe; press reports cash and XP reset with leftover cash converted to Gold Bars | [13][18] |
| Season 02 XP curve | 0.2.0 notes lower total XP per level; they state level 20 now takes less than half the Season 1 playtime. Numbers: progression-and-role-tracks | [18] |

The official Season 1 changelog (history) slowed levels around 10 to 20 and flattened the curve from level 35: level 10 rose from 25,000 to 35,000 XP, level 15 from 54,750 to 110,000, level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000 and level 50 from 838,000 to 1,000,000; an air-vehicle player kill pays 250 XP, down from 300 [3]. The developer targets a median player at 20 to 25 hours being around level 20 [3]. The official name "Career" is used in the changelog; "Assault" is a player-guide name [3][15]. Economy abuse penalties (timed ban with cash and XP reset to 0; permanent ban for exploit tutorials and XP farming) are official from 0.11 and were reaffirmed in 0.1.2 [4][5]. The 14 Oct 2026 notes reverse that slowdown for Season 02; their own "before" figures for levels 10 to 20 match the Season 1 changelog figures quoted here, but give 1,500,000 rather than 1,000,000 as the old level 50 value, so the figures conflict at level 50 [3][18]. Full tables are in progression-and-role-tracks, progression-unlock-tables and season-reset-and-currencies.

## Modes available at Early Access

The only core mode named in official text is the Control Zone [1][2]; the 0.2.0 notes add no new mode, but a Wager Vendor feature is due later in Season 2 (below) [18]. Official servers do not run modified game modes, while Community servers can [4]. The 0.1.2 Deploy flow lets players choose Official, Community, Infantry Mode or Low-Level servers, described as a first step to signpost servers running these modifiers; the post does not define the rules of either modifier [5]. Assessment: a full catalogue of community-server modes is unavailable; confidence Low.

## Wager Vendor (not open at 0.2.0 launch)

The 14 Oct notes state the Wager Vendor is not available at Season 2 launch and will open later in Season 2; it lets a player bet their own cash on their own performance, with a live wager tracker above the minimap, and it is not a permanent addition but is meant to come and go through a season [18]. The 9 Oct preview describes it as experimental, with chosen objectives, a death budget and longer odds as objectives stack [19]. No opening date is given; none is seen in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.

## Planned for 1.0

The 7 Apr 2026 post says the Metagame (the frontend experience to keep earning and progressing outside a match) is designed and will be built throughout Early Access, including the Black Market and Vault and a Player Skills and Challenge System [10]. The store page (live capture 2026-10-08) plans to expand in several areas: more maps, weapons, vehicles and gameplay variety; more in-depth progression systems; a stronger seasonal meta game; new vehicle types including fighter jets; expanded weapon categories; and additional objective variations [1]. It expects Early Access to last around 1 to 2 years, with the duration liable to change, and plans to price the game lower during Early Access and higher at full release [1]. These are developer plans, not dated commitments. A third-party roadmap article adds new objective types and says no dated roadmap will be published, but does not say which items are official [14].

text:
This document explains how WARDOGS progression works: role tracks, the role-track XP curve, XP events, level caps, the account-wide WARDOG level, the exploit policy and what the developer has said about seasons. It is revised for Season 02 (Update 0.2.0), using the full official patch notes (14 Oct 2026) [10] and the release post (15 Oct 2026) [11]. Full per-item unlock levels and costs are in progression-unlock-tables.

The 0.2.0 notes replace the Season 1 XP curve: reaching level 20 now takes 111,500 total XP instead of 250,000 (55 percent quicker) and level 50 takes 1,150,000 instead of 1,500,000 (23 percent quicker); the developer says level 20 now takes less than half the playtime it did in Season 1 [10]. The notes name seven track headings: WARDOG, Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot and Driver [10]. The Season 1 changelog (9 Sep 2026) used Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [1]. The notes also move some XP between roles: buildable destruction, IEDs and C4 now give Assault XP, artillery gives Driver XP, and repair XP goes to Driver or Pilot [10].

Confidence is Medium. The XP table, event values and reassignments rest on the official notes (High on their own). The level cap, the WARDOG level formula and the seasonal wipe rest on player-reported or press sources, or are not mentioned in the notes, which holds the document at Medium [8][9][10].

text:
- Season 02 (Update 0.2.0, notes 2026-10-14, live 2026-10-15) lowered the total XP needed at every published level from 10 to 50: level 10 35,000 to 25,000; level 20 250,000 to 111,500; level 50 1,500,000 to 1,150,000 [10][11].
- Season 1 history: the 9 Sep 2026 changelog had slowed the curve (level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000; level 50 from 838,000 to 1,000,000) [1]. The 0.2.0 notes print different "before" values for levels 25 to 50 (for example level 50: 1,500,000); the discrepancy is unexplained [1][10].
- Seven track headings appear in the 0.2.0 notes: WARDOG, Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot, Driver [10]. "Career" from the Season 1 changelog is not used in the notes; Assessment: WARDOG matches Career by level (Deagle 85, Sport Parachute 35), confidence Medium [1][10].
- 0.2.0 role-XP reassignment: destroying a buildable, IED and C4 now give Assault XP (was Support); artillery gives Driver XP (was Support); repair XP goes to Driver or Pilot by vehicle [10].
- Season 1 developer statement: "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" [1].
- The 0.2.0 notes do not mention a Season 02 progression wipe, automatic cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion or any level cap; the unconfirmed press claim of a wipe stays in Open Questions [8][10].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) fixed several cash and XP exploits and ended first-offence leniency; 0.2.0 adds more exploit fixes (spotting, supply crates, FOB assist) [2][10].
- Two Season 1 XP event values (air vehicle kill 250 XP; low-value crate sale 1 XP) are not mentioned in the 0.2.0 notes (not changed in the notes) [1][10].

text:
- **Role track**: a per-role XP and level track that gates which items can be bought. The 0.2.0 notes use the headings WARDOG, Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot and Driver [10]; the Season 1 changelog used Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [1].
- **Total XP required**: the 0.2.0 notes' name for the XP needed to reach a level [10]. The Season 1 changelog called these XP bands [1].
- **WARDOG level**: an account-wide level, described by a player-reported guide as the sum of the six track levels [9]. Not defined in any official post I read. The 0.2.0 notes also use "WARDOG" for a track heading [10].
- **Season**: a period after which, per press, cash and level progression reset; the developer says each season has its own XP curve [1][8]. Season 02 is the first season after Season 1.

- Developer intent: "Levels 10 to 20 were a slow grind, and many players stalled out before unlocking the gear that defines each role"; level 20 now takes less than half the Season 1 playtime [10].

text:
## Role tracks and the 4-versus-6 and naming conflicts

| Question | Official text | Other sources | Resolution |
|----------|---------------|---------------|------------|
| How many tracks? | Season 1 changelog (9 Sep 2026): six names, Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot [1]. Update 0.2.0 notes (14 Oct 2026): seven headings, WARDOG, Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot, Driver [10] | Six tracks, four levelled by weapons and tools, Driver and Pilot levelled by vehicles (player-reported) [9] | The count depends on date and on whether Career and WARDOG are one track. As of 0.2.0 the notes show seven headings. Whether Assault is a new seventh track is not stated. |
| What is the first track called? | Season 1: "Career" [1]. 0.2.0: "WARDOG Progression Track" [10] | "Assault", levelled from assault rifles (player-reported) [9] | Assessment: WARDOG is Career renamed, because the levels match (Deagle 85, Sport Parachute 35, 556mm AP 83 before the 0.2.0 change), confidence Medium [1][10]. The notes never say so. |
| Is Assault an official track? | The 0.2.0 notes have an "Assault Progression Track" heading and say "Assault is now the role for attacking enemy bases" [10] | Guides use "Assault" for the rifle track [9] | Yes, as of 0.2.0. The Season 1 changelog did not list it [1]. |
| Does an official post call the tracks "roles"? | The Season 1 post says "role track"; the 0.2.0 notes say "Role Track XP" and "Role Track Unlocks" [1][10] | Guides say "roles" [9] | Use "role track". |

Evidence that WARDOG is a full track and not a catch-all: the 0.2.0 notes list unlocks such as pallets, pistols, ammo types, armour and the Gold Market under it [10]. Items keep moving between tracks: in Season 1, Music Tape H from Pilot to Driver and Heavy Tank from Career to Driver [1]; in 0.2.0, the SPH-2 from WARDOG level 90 to Driver level 31, the C4 charge from Support to Assault, and many scopes and foregrips between WARDOG, Assault, Medic and Support [10].

## XP sources named in official text

| Source | Value | Source of value |
|--------|-------|-----------------|
| Player kill using an air vehicle | 250 XP (was 300), Season 1; not mentioned in the 0.2.0 notes | [1][10] |
| Supply crate item sold under $75 | 1 XP (was 25), Season 1; not mentioned in the 0.2.0 notes | [1][10] |
| FOB hacking (teammates in radius) | $1,000 / 250 XP; the hacker still gets $2,500 / 250 XP (0.2.0) | [10] |
| Destroying a FOB | bonus up to +$7,500 / +250 XP by supplies held, maxed at 25,000 supplies (0.2.0) | [10] |
| Capturing a hostile drill tower | $750 to $1,500 and XP 250 to 300 (0.2.0) | [10] |
| Logistics delivery streaks | e.g. crates +$100 / +50 XP per crate in a row up to 10 (0.2.0; updated values include the zone multiplier) | [10] |
| Revives | Validity now server authoritative (value not published) | [2] |
| Destroying buildables | Reward scales with build progress (0.1.2); in 0.2.0 the XP goes to the Assault track and cash matches the build supply cost with XP about 25 percent of cash | [2][10] |
| Vehicle fly-through | Rewards capped (cap not published) | [2] |
| FOB pallet deposit outside the zone | Reduced reward (value not published) | [2] |

0.2.0 role-XP reassignment: destroying a buildable, IED and C4 now give Assault XP instead of Support; artillery gives Driver XP instead of Support; repair XP goes into Driver or Pilot depending on the vehicle repaired instead of a flat Support amount [10]. Amounts for all reward events are owned by cash-rewards-and-costs.

Other XP sources (kills, objectives) are described only in guides; the guide says Driver XP comes from "kills and objectives from a ground vehicle" and Pilot XP from flying helicopters (player-reported) [9].

## Season 02 role-track XP curve (Update 0.2.0)

The notes list "Total XP Required" per level, with the old value before the arrow [10].

| Level | Old (per 0.2.0 notes) | Season 02 | Change stated |
|-------|-----------------------|-----------|---------------|
| 10 | 35,000 | 25,000 | 29% quicker |
| 15 | 110,000 | 54,750 | 50% quicker |
| 20 | 250,000 | 111,500 | 55% quicker |
| 25 | 365,000 | 206,600 | 43% quicker |
| 30 | 500,000 | 318,200 | 36% quicker |
| 35 | 750,000 | 525,000 | 30% quicker |
| 40 | 975,000 | 712,500 | 27% quicker |
| 45 | 1,225,000 | 920,850 | 25% quicker |
| 50 | 1,500,000 | 1,150,000 | 23% quicker |

Source: [10]. Conflicts and limits:

- For levels 25 to 50 the "old" value in the 0.2.0 notes (365,000 to 1,500,000) is higher than the value in the Season 1 changelog (325,000 to 1,000,000) in the history table below [1][10]. The notes do not explain the difference. Season 02 values are taken from the notes only.
- The Season 02 totals at levels 10, 15 and 20 equal the pre-Season-1 ("beta") values printed in the Season 1 changelog (25,000 / 54,750 / 111,500) [1][10]. The notes do not comment.
- No values are published for levels below 10, between listed levels or above 50; the notes do not say whether a figure is cumulative, though "Total XP Required" reads as cumulative (Assessment: Medium confidence) [10].

## Season 1 curve versus beta (history, superseded by 0.2.0)

The changelog says the earlier balancing "was designed specifically for weekend long beta tests" and that the new values are "in-line with where we believe they should be" [1]. The "old" column below is therefore the beta-era curve, as stated by the developer.

| Level | Beta XP | Season 1 XP | Change as published | Derived: Season 1 XP added since previous band |
|-------|---------|-------------|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Below 6 | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | n/a |
| 6 | 8,750 | 9,250 | 5.7% slower | n/a |
| 10 | 25,000 | 35,000 | 40.0% slower | 25,750 |
| 15 | 54,750 | 110,000 | 100.9% slower | 75,000 |
| 20 | 111,500 | 250,000 | 124.2% slower | 140,000 |
| 25 | 192,000 | 325,000 | 69.3% slower | 75,000 |
| 30 | 293,750 | 400,000 | 36.2% slower | 75,000 |
| 35 | 416,500 | 500,000 | 20.0% slower | 100,000 |
| 40 | 551,250 | 650,000 | 17.9% slower | 150,000 |
| 45 | 689,500 | 800,000 | 16.0% slower | 150,000 |
| 50 | 838,000 | 1,000,000 | 19.3% slower | 200,000 |

Source for the first four data columns: [1]. The last column is my subtraction of adjacent Season 1 values and is not in any source. Assessment: the headline says the slowdown is "around 10 to 20" with flattening from 35 onward, yet the published bands show every band to level 50 slower than beta by at least 16 percent; confidence High that this is what the table says, Low on what the developer meant by "flatten" (the post does not elaborate) [1]. The same section describes "a larger increase at level 10" than the 5.7 percent at level 6 [1].

Intermediate levels (for example 7 to 9, 11 to 14) have no published XP value; the post gives bands only [1]. Whether the figures are cumulative per track or per level is not spelled out; the XP-to-reach wording ("Level 10: 25,000 to 35,000") reads as cumulative requirement (Assessment: Medium confidence, based on the figures rising monotonically) [1].

## Level caps and WARDOG level

- Official: no level cap is stated. The highest levels named in the changelog are Career level 90 (Artillery Tank) and Career level 85 (Deagle), so a cap of at least 90 is implied (Assessment: High that the cap is 90 or more, from [1]).
- Player-reported: each track caps at level 100, and the account-wide WARDOG Level is "the sum of all six tracks" capped at 600 [9]. The arithmetic (6 x 100 = 600) is consistent with a cap of 100, but neither number is in an official post I read.
- Official XP stops at level 50 (Season 1: 1,000,000 XP [1]; Season 02: 1,150,000 XP [10]); XP needed for levels 51 to 100 is not published. The 0.2.0 notes do not state a cap, and the highest level named in them is WARDOG level 90 (the SPH-2, before its move to Driver) [10].

| XP design target | Tuned for weekend-long tests | Tuned for long-term play; per-season curves | [1] |
| XP curve | See table above | Slowed at every published band from level 6 | [1] |
| Air vehicle kill XP | 300 | 250 | [1] |
| Low-value supply crate sale XP | 25 | 1 | [1] |
| Supply crate purchase curve | 25 to 250 | 1 to 200 ("rescaled") | [1] |
| Items per track | Many items at earlier levels | Many moved (see below) | [1] |

## 0.1.2 XP and cash exploit fixes (30 Sep 2026)

All from the official 0.1.2 post [2]:

1. Revive action validity checks are fully server authoritative.
2. Vehicle fly-through exploit fixed; rewards capped.
3. Rewards for destroying buildables scale with build progress.
4. Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone awards reduced rewards.
5. Policy: anyone caught abusing cash and XP exploits or Real Money Trading "has had their cash and progression reset and risks being permanently banned"; first-time leniency is over; repeatable unintended exploits can bring a permanent ban without warning [2].

The earlier patch 0.11 post (12 Sep 2026) set the tiers: cash exploits get a timed ban and a cash and XP reset to 0; tutorials on exploits count as advertising cheats and get a permanent ban; XP farming "will result in the most serious bans" and joining a known XP-farming server for more than a few minutes risks a permanent ban [4]. The post gives no figure for the reduced or capped rewards [2].

## What Season 02 says about XP and resets

The Season 02 teaser (22 Sep 2026) gave only the date 15 October 2026 [3]. The outcome, as published:

- Official: the 0.2.0 notes (14 Oct 2026) contain a "Progression Changes" section with the Role Track XP table and unlock changes [10]. The release post (15 Oct 2026) says only that Update 0.2.0 is released and servers are back online [11]. Neither mentions a progression wipe, a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion or a change to the account level; the notes are silent, which is not a statement that none occurred.
- Official, indirect: "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" (Season 1 changelog) [1]; Season 02 was described as "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [2].
- Official, Season 02 only: Lonestar faction cash and XP win bonus and teamplay cash and XP multipliers, "Season 2 only", plus a 20 percent vendor discount for a team at least 40 points behind second place [10]. The bonus amounts are not stated.
- Press: Vice (23 Sep 2026) said players "should expect a progression wipe", that cash and level progression reset at the end of a season, that leftover cash converts to Gold Bars and that Gold Bars and cosmetics persist; the unlock order and conversion rate were not yet shared [8]. The official 0.2.0 posts neither confirm nor deny this.
- Player-reported: a guide says WARDOG Level and cash "drop to zero" when a major update cycle ends [9].

## Exploit fixes added in 0.2.0

Spotting added and removed rewards scale with build progress; destroying a buildable pays by how built it is; selling from a supply crate has diminishing returns per buyer until you break even with no profit or XP; selling to an enemy player gives no cash or XP; destroying an empty enemy crate pays half cash and half XP; supply crate rewards scale with the supplies inside; FOB Supplied Assist is split between assisting players [10]. Reward amounts: see cash-rewards-and-costs.

text:
This is the reference table of role-track unlocks and the role-track XP curve for WARDOGS, updated for Season 02 (Update 0.2.0). The developer published the full 0.2.0 patch notes on 14 Oct 2026 [8] and announced the update live on 15 Oct 2026 [9]. The notes give, for every track, the unlock level and unlock cost of each added item, each item moved between tracks and each changed item, plus a new total-XP table for levels 10 to 50 [8]. The Season 1 values from the 9 Sep 2026 changelog are kept below as history [1].

The headline changes in 0.2.0: reaching level 20 now takes 111,500 XP instead of 250,000 (55 percent quicker) and level 50 takes 1,150,000 XP instead of 1,500,000; the notes name the tracks WARDOG, Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot and Driver, so the 0.2.0 notes show seven track headings against the six counted in earlier official text; most attachments moved to earlier levels or to other tracks; the Little Bird AH-6M [Miniguns] moved from level 4 to level 8 and from $50k to $125k; the SPH-2 moved from WARDOG level 90 into the Driver track at level 31 [8].

Limits: the notes list only changes and additions, so a full level-by-level table per track still does not exist in official text. Where an item is not mentioned, this document says "not changed in the notes" and does not infer a value. The notes disagree with the earlier Season 1 changelog on the "before" XP values for levels 25 to 50, and some item names differ between the two posts; both are flagged below. The notes do not mention a Season 02 progression wipe [8].

text:
- Season 02 (Update 0.2.0, notes 2026-10-14, live 2026-10-15): the role-track total-XP table for levels 10 to 50 was lowered at every published level, from 29 percent quicker at level 10 to 23 percent quicker at level 50 (peak 55 percent at level 20) [8][9].
- Seven track headings appear in the 0.2.0 notes: WARDOG, Assault, Medic, Recon, Support, Pilot, Driver [8]. The Season 1 changelog used "Career" as a heading [1]; the 0.2.0 notes never use "Career".
- The Assault track gained the Molotov Cocktail (level 13, $25k), the TCX-SPR (level 20, $100k) and the C4 charge with Remote Detonator (moved from Support level 2 to Assault level 4) [8].
- The Medical Bag now unlocks at Medic level 14 for $50k (was level 24, $75k); the PKM now unlocks at Support level 15 for $100k (was level 30, $150k) [8].
- Driver gained the Wolf-110 (level 8, $50k), the Wolf-110 [M2 Browning] (level 16, $125k), the T-72B3 (level 20, $250k) and the Flakpanzer Gepard (level 25, $300k) [8].
- Recon gained the M14 (level 25, $100k); Support gained the Evo-3 Ultra (level 30, $200k) [8].
- Role XP reassignment: destroying a buildable, IED and C4 now give Assault XP; artillery now gives Driver XP; repair XP goes to Driver or Pilot by vehicle [8].
- The notes do not mention a progression wipe, a level cap or a change to the account-level formula [8].

The notes say the Little Bird AH-6M [Miniguns] "was too strong for how early it unlocked, so it now unlocks later and costs more" [8].

| Item | Level | Cost |
|------|-------|------|
| Little Bird AH-6M [Miniguns] | 4 → 8 | $50k → $125k |
| Z20 Lakota [Miniguns] | n/c | $75k → $85k |
| Havoc | n/c | $500k → $650k |
| Music tapes | "reshuffled between the Driver and Pilot tracks"; no per-tape values stated | not stated |

Conflict: the Season 1 changelog lists the Z20 Lakota at $35,000 under Pilot price lines, while the 0.2.0 notes print $75k as the "before" value for the Z20 Lakota [Miniguns] [1][8]. The two posts may describe different variants or price types (the Season 1 post does not say); not resolved. The Season 1 Little Bird price of $50,000 matches the 0.2.0 "before" value [1][8].

## Driver track

The notes say Drivers "now have more ways to get kills before reaching the L2A6" [8].

### Driver: additional unlocks

| Item | Level | Cost |
|------|-------|------|
| Wolf-110 | 8 | $50k |
| Wolf-110 [M2 Browning] | 16 | $125k |
| T-72B3 | 20 | $250k |
| Flakpanzer Gepard | 25 | $300k |
| Music Tape "Dyshat' - Baryber" | 33 | $25k |

### Driver: moved into the track

| Item | Level | Moved from | Cost |
|------|-------|-----------|------|
| SPH-2 | 31 | WARDOG level 90 | $500k → $350k |

| Item | Level | Cost |
|------|-------|------|
| Dune Buggy | 8 → 9 | n/c |
| Humvee | 15 → 14 | $25k → $75k |
| Ural Defender | 18 → 15 | n/c |
| Large Crate | 16 → 17 | n/c |
| Ural Defender [M249] | 25 → 22 | $125k → $100k |
| Humvee [M249] | 20 → 24 | n/c |
| Music tapes | reshuffled between Driver and Pilot; no per-tape values stated | not stated |

Name differences between the two posts: the Season 1 changelog lists "URAL Covered" at level 18 and "URAL Attack" at level 25, while the 0.2.0 notes print "Ural Defender" at 18 → 15 and "Ural Defender [M249]" at 25 → 22 [1][8]. Assessment: the levels match, so these are probably the same items under new names; the posts do not say so. Confidence: Medium. Season 1 Driver items not mentioned in the 0.2.0 notes (not changed in the notes): Kodiak Assault level 6, Kodiak Flatbed level 10, Humvee with minigun level 30, Heavy Tank level 35, Music Tape H level 23 and the Season 1 URAL level 3 and prices [1][8].

## Role XP reassignment in 0.2.0

The notes change which track receives XP for some actions: destroying a buildable now gives Assault XP instead of Support XP; artillery now gives Driver XP instead of Support XP; IED and C4 give Assault XP instead of Support XP; repair XP goes into the Driver or Pilot track depending on the vehicle repaired, instead of a flat Support amount [8]. Cash and XP amounts are owned by cash-rewards-and-costs.

text:
This depth document goes beyond maps-environment-foundation on how WARDOGS describes its destruction, its level design and its map scale, using the full text of Bulkhead's official Steam posts saved locally on 2026-10-08. It was first written as a pre-Season-02 baseline (2026-10-08) and was revised on 2026-10-30 for Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, released 15 Oct 2026), so every number below is stamped with the version it applies to.

The headline finding is that the official "Level Design & Performance" devlog (16 Jul 2026) is a short video post. Its text says nothing about map size, map count, destruction rules or the "sandbox" term; it only says the team gathered references "firsthand in Georgia", optimised across a wide range of hardware, and offers graphics options [3]. The map-size and sandbox questions are answered by other official text. An 18 Feb 2026 Bulkhead post states that the Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area "within a large-scale 256km² map" [2]. The foundation has since been revised to match. The Steam store page calls the game a "large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox" with "building and destruction mechanics" and "larger maps" [1]. The "3 maps x 3 variations" count appears only in the Team17 press release as quoted by the foundation [9].

Confidence is Medium. The scale, sandbox and destruction claims rest on official Bulkhead text, but no official source describes the destruction model, terrain deformation, persistence or the performance cost of destruction, and the 0.2.0 rain notes give no numbers. The rain preset itself is now official [14][15].
title: Destructibility & Level Design

text:
- Official text resolves "sandbox": the Steam page and Bulkhead's posts use it for the player-driven, build-and-destroy play space ("a large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox", "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox"), not for a map type [1][4][5]. It does not conflict with a fixed roster of maps (Season 01) [1][9].
- Official text states a 256 km² map and a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside it, in a Bulkhead post of 18 Feb 2026 (pre-release) [2]. The Steam page itself says only "larger maps" and gives no total size [1].
- A 256 km² area is 16 km x 16 km if square, which matches the community "about 16 km edge to edge" claim arithmetically; the official text does not state the shape [2][13].
- The official destruction statements are: a "destructible battlefield" [1], rocket launchers can destroy apartment blocks [1], and "the world around you reacts to your presence" [1]. Nothing official says terrain is deformable or that damage persists across matches.
- The "Level Design & Performance" post is about performance, not destruction rules: Georgian reference gathering, hardware optimisation, and graphics options [3]. Bulkhead says the engine is UE5 enhanced by a custom "WAR DYNAMICS FRAMEWORK" for 100-player density [2].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) made destroying buildables scale with build progress, so a placed schematic no longer pays a full reward [7].
- Update 0.2.0 (released 15 Oct 2026) adds an official rain weather preset that interacts with destruction: "Destroy a roof and the rain starts visually coming through it" [14][15][16]. Earlier press claims of rain are officially confirmed; the "fixed for the whole match" detail is still press-only [10][11][15]. The notes name no new map and add no terrain-deformation or persistence statement [15].

Verified 2026-10-30 against official Steam text through the 15 Oct 2026 post; items dated 2026-10-08 are the unchanged Season 01 baseline.

- The Steam page describes "building and destruction mechanics in a large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox" [1].
- The page says players can "destroy apartment blocks with rocket launchers or tear your way through towns in heavily armoured tanks" and that "the world around you reacts to your presence" [1].
- The short description reads "on a destructible battlefield" [1].
- Zones are randomised 2x2 km areas "within larger maps" [1]. Bulkhead's 18 Feb 2026 Top Questions post states the map as 256 km² [2].
- Bulkhead's Early Access content list includes "Destruction & Build Mechanics" [2].
- The 16 Jul 2026 devlog states performance has been a priority "since day one", references were gathered "firsthand in Georgia", and graphics options let players tune performance [3].
- Patch 0.1.2 changed buildable-destruction rewards and fixed buildable crit spots that jumped or reappeared in the same place [7].
- Update 0.2.0 (14 to 15 Oct 2026) adds the rain preset (details under Weather and rain), and its building changes touch destruction: doors and gates can no longer be breached with a hammer while the Halligan bar can breach both; unfinished buildables collapse as soon as they lose a support; CIWS cannon damage against structures was retuned to shred light cover and struggle against heavy fortifications; Large Shelter was added [15]. Build costs and rewards are owned by fob-and-base-building and cash-rewards-and-costs.
- The 15 Oct 2026 post states Update 0.2.0 was released and servers were back online [16]. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.
