text:
## Settling "sandbox" versus "3 maps x 3 variations"

| Question | Official answer | Source |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| What does "sandbox" mean? | Player-driven play space with build and destroy freedom; "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox"; clips recorded in a "100 player Tactical All Out Warfare sandbox" | [1][4][5] |
| Is there an open-world sandbox map? | No official text says so. The mode is a King of the Hill style fight over a Control Zone "within larger maps" | [1][2] |
| How many maps? | Three maps with three variations each (Team17 press release, quoted via the foundation; not re-read here) | [9] |
| What is a "variation"? | Not defined in any official text read | [1][2][3] |

Assessment: Medium confidence that "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations" are compatible. "Sandbox" describes freedom of play inside a map; the press release counts map assets. The official 18 Feb post describes "multiple locations and POIs" in the setting "Kolchia" [2], which could be what a "variation" refers to, but this is an inference and unconfirmed.

## Map scale: what official text says

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Control Zone size: randomised 2x2 km | Steam page, Season 01 (checked 2026-10-08); also 18 Feb 2026 post | [1][2] |
| Map size: 256 km² | 18 Feb 2026 post (pre-release); not repeated on the Steam page | [2] |
| Max players per match: 100 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Teams: 3 | Season 01 | [1][2] |
| Points to win: 100 | Season 01 | [1][2] |

Assessment: Medium confidence that 256 km² remains current. It is official but dated seven months before launch, and the Steam page uses only "larger maps". The 2x2 km zone is 4 km², about 1.6% of 256 km² (arithmetic from [2]). Community figures (about 16 km edge to edge, 500 m radius play circles) are player-reported or unattributed, and the 500 m figure conflicts with the 2x2 km zone [12][13].

## Level design philosophy as stated

Official statements are thin. The 16 Jul 2026 devlog gives three points: real-world reference gathering in Georgia, continuous optimisation across a wide range of hardware, and tunable graphics options [3]. The 21 May 2026 Debrief lists "real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" and "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox" [5]. The Top Questions post says the setting offers "varied, grounded militaristic gameplay" with "multiple locations and POIs" [2]. No official text describes sightline, chokepoint or zone-placement design rules. Playtesters are quoted as surprised at performance, which is Bulkhead's own characterisation [3].

## What can be destroyed

| Item | Status | Source |
|------|--------|--------|
| Apartment blocks | Destroyable by rocket launchers | [1] |
| Towns and buildings generally | "Destructible battlefield"; tanks can "tear your way through towns" | [1] |
| Player buildables (FOB parts, schematics) | Destroyable; destruction reward scales with build progress since 0.1.2; in 0.2.0 buildable-destroyed cash matches each buildable's build supply cost | [7][15] |
| Roofs | Destroying a roof makes rain visibly come through it (0.2.0) | [15] |
| Doors and gates | Cannot be breached with a hammer; the Halligan bar breaches both (0.2.0) | [15] |
| Terrain deformation | No official statement; a third-party roadmap claims terrain is destructible | [12] |
| Persistence across matches | No official statement | - |
| Which structures are indestructible | No official list | - |

Destruction is also a listed Early Access pillar: "Destruction & Build Mechanics" [2], and "Infantry, Vehicles, Base Building & Destruction" in the announcement trailer post [4]. The roles list includes Demolitions [4]. The gameplay trailer post lists "building, destruction" among the features [6]. Player-built structure rules are in fob-and-base-building.

## Destruction and performance

No official source ties destruction to a performance cost, a debris cap or a server tick budget. What is official: Bulkhead built a custom framework on UE5 to handle 100 players [2]; performance was prioritised from day one [3]; graphics options exist [3]. The Steam requirements and minimum spec are in system-requirements-and-performance. Assessment: Low confidence that destruction limits exist; the KB neither confirms nor denies them.

## Weather and rain (Update 0.2.0)

Season 1 (0.1.2) baseline: the 30 Sep 2026 notes said only that Season 02 brings "new map conditions", and press attributed a rain state to Bulkhead [7][10][11]. Season 02 (0.2.0, notes of 14 Oct 2026, release 15 Oct 2026) makes this official with a "New Rain Weather Preset" [15][16]:

- Surfaces, vehicles and characters become visibly wet as rain falls [15].
- Rain sounds differ by what it falls on and where you stand: under cover, indoors, inside a vehicle or in the open [15].
- Destroy a roof and rain visibly comes through it [15]. The 9 Oct 2026 preview adds that rain "interacts with the environment, including damaged and destroyed structures" and that the preset changes "visibility, engagement ranges and sound" [14].
- Thunder rolls in during heavier rain; every player on the server hears the same strike at the same moment from the same direction, and it is loud enough to mask footsteps [15].
- Spotting range is affected by rain; Molotov fire is reduced by rain, and Molotovs can burn destructible foliage [15].
- The Large Shelter buildable (medium hammer and above, 250 build supply) is "for covering key assets or keeping the rain off" [15].

The notes give no numbers (spotting-range change, fire reduction, thunder frequency), do not say how a match is assigned rain, and do not say whether it can change mid match; the press claim of a fixed per-match state is not repeated officially [10][15]. Whether rain affects aircraft is not stated. Assessment (confidence Medium): the roof and foliage entries show weather and destruction are designed to interact, but no official text describes the destruction model itself.

Bakurani: the same notes moved and rebuilt all three team spawns, each with purpose-built routes to the zone; no new named map was added [15]. Per-map detail is in launch-maps-reference.

text:
Officially, WARDOGS launched with three maps, each with three variations [2], and a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside a 256 km2 map, set in a war-torn region called "Kolchia" [1][10]. Revised 2026-10-08 against the full text of all 32 saved Steam posts: none of them, nor the Steam store data, names Bakurani, Ozeti, Zestafona, Jutari or Saburtulo, profiles a map, or explains rotation [1][10][11][12]. The per-map profiles below therefore remain player-reported: Bakurani, Ozeti and Zestafona, plus the unconfirmed Jutari and Saburtulo [3][4][5][6][7].

Several community sources agree on the three names, their settings and the existence of roughly three rotating areas per map. They disagree on play-area size, control-zone counts and whether a fourth map exists. Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, released 15 Oct 2026) officially adds a rain weather preset and moves and rebuilds all three team spawns on Bakurani, each with purpose-built routes to the zone; the notes name Bakurani but add no new named map [16][17][18]. Player-reported Bakurani details written before 15 Oct 2026 may be outdated.

Confidence stays Low (the 0.2.0 facts are official but do not change this): the per-map names and profiles, which are the point of this document, are player-reported and the sources conflict. The official text only upgrades the generic map facts (256 km2 map, 2x2 km zone, "Kolchia"), which other documents already use.

text:
## Map profiles (all player-reported, Season 01 baseline)

Update 0.2.0 moved and rebuilt all three team spawns on Bakurani [17]. The Bakurani column below was collected before that change (accessed 2026-10-08) and does not describe the new spawns or routes; the notes do not say which areas were affected [17].

| Attribute | Bakurani | Ozeti | Zestafona |
|-----------|----------|-------|-----------|
| Region label | Kavkazi [3] | Europe [3] | North America [3] |
| Setting | Eastern European mountain river valley [3][4][7] | Wooded river basin around a hill town [3][4][5] | Industrial rail hub on a river bend [4][5][7] |
| Relative size | Smallest [4] | About 4x Bakurani's play area [4] | About 4x Bakurani's play area [4] |
| Play-circle radius (community) | 500 m [3] | 550 m [3] | 500 m [3] |
| Terrain | Valley floor, factory district, forested ridges, farmland, snowy northern peaks [3][4] | Hill town, orchards, farmland, forest, river across the south [3][4] | Warehouses, rail yards, shipping, farmland, forest [3][4] |
| Named areas | Default, Farmland, Lumberyard [3][7] | Default, Church, River (Farmland defined but not in rotation) [3][7] | Default, Water Treatment, Houses (Small Factory defined but not in rotation) [3][6][7] |

## Notable points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Features | Source |
|-----|----------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, factory and containers, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, sunflower fields and church, Lumberyard, numbered towers (7 plus 4 abandoned in one list; 5 drill towers in another) | [4][7] |
| Ozeti | Walled football stadium with parking and garages, six-part Hillside Church, Apartments, Shops, Pool, Industrial, farms, 4 towers in two lists | [3][4][7] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, offices, water towers, northern Water Treatment, 3 drill towers | [4][6][7] |

## Typical Control Zone behaviour (player-reported)

- allthings.how: one objective ring of 85 m radius at the centre of the live play area; on Zestafona the three live areas are picked at equal frequency [3][6]. On Bakurani it says the Default area is picked twice as often as the other two [3]; no other source says this.
- allthings.how: the farthest area centres are 285 m apart on Bakurani, 693 m on Ozeti and 531 m on Zestafona [3][6]. These distances fit a 500 m circle model, not a 2x2 km zone.
- Hot Zone: roams inside the Control Zone and counts double [6][7]. Boostroom says Bulkhead confirms double cash for it; I could not trace that to an official page [7].
- Terrain effect: Bakurani high ground over the valley road decides engagements [3]; Ozeti open approaches to the town are exposed [3][7]; Zestafona has long exposed approaches in the yards [3][7].

## Unconfirmed maps

| Map | Claim | Source |
|-----|-------|--------|
| Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari | Sniper Showdown map on the Kavkazi world; 350 m play circle, 75 m objective ring, single fixed area, no rotation; status "not confirmed as playable" | [3] |
| Saburtulo | Listed as a King of the Hill map under Russia; no play area or objective; not playable | [3] |

No other source read mentions either name; the guides from xgamingserver.com, gamebrief.net and boostroom.com name only three maps [4][5][7]. Treat both as unconfirmed.

## Rotation

- Official: no rotation is documented. Bulkhead says only that the Control Zone is randomised [1].
- Player-reported: each map has three live areas drawn from a defined list of three or four; allthings.how says selection on Zestafona is equally likely [3][6]. Gamebrief says the whole map is not confirmed to reroll each match and no map vote or map order is documented [5].
- Assessment (Low): the "three variations" per map [2] plausibly match the three live areas, but no source states this.

## Conflicts between sources

| Topic | Source A | Source B | Treatment |
|-------|----------|----------|-----------|
| Play area | Official 2x2 km Control Zone [1][10] | 500 m radius circles, 85 m ring [3][6] | Not reconciled; official figure stands, community figures unverified |
| Whole-map size | Boostroom: 256 km2 attributed to Bulkhead [7] | Steam page gives no map size [1]; Bulkhead post of 18 Feb 2026 states 256 km2 [10] | Resolved: official, but pre-release; the Boostroom figure matches it |
| Control zones | 171 named zones across three maps [4] | One ring per map [3]; three to four positions per map [5] | No figure adopted |
| Map count | Three maps [2][4][5] | allthings.how introduction says four playable, details list three [3] | Three; internal inconsistency noted |
| Tower count | Bakurani 7 plus 4 abandoned [4] | Bakurani 5 drill towers [7] | Not reconciled |
| Bakurani rotation | Default picked twice as often [3] | No weighting documented [5][7] | Single source |

## Season 02 weather and Bakurani (Update 0.2.0)

Official, from the Season 02 patch notes (14 Oct 2026) and the release post (15 Oct 2026) [17][18]:

- Rain preset: surfaces, vehicles and characters look wet; rain sounds differ by surface and by whether you are under cover, indoors, in a vehicle or in the open; a destroyed roof lets rain visibly through; thunder in heavier rain is synchronised across the server, heard by everyone at the same moment from the same direction, and loud enough to mask footsteps; spotting range is affected by rain; Molotov fire is reduced by rain, and Molotovs can burn destructible foliage [17]. The 9 Oct 2026 preview says the preset changes "visibility, engagement ranges and sound" [16].
- Large Shelter: a buildable "for covering key assets or keeping the rain off" (medium hammer and above, 250 build supply) [17].
- Bakurani: all three team spawns moved and rebuilt with purpose-built routes to the zone, intended to give a more balanced match [17]. The notes do not mention spawn changes on Ozeti or Zestafona.
- Not stated: numeric rain effects, how a match gets the preset, whether rain can change mid match, and any new named map. The press claim of a fixed per-match state [8] is not in the official text.

text:
Officially, WARDOGS is set in war-torn "Kolchia", where the fight is over a resource called PV-1, in "derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe" on a destructible battlefield [1][3]. Bulkhead's own 18 Feb 2026 FAQ states that three teams fight over "a randomized 2x2km Control Zone within a 256km² map" [3]. The Steam page repeats the 2x2 km zone, places it "within larger maps" and lists "large-scale maps with dynamic objective zones" as part of the current Early Access build, but does not give the 256 km² total, so that figure is official yet pre-release [1][3]. The count of "3 maps x 3 variations" appears only in the Team17 press release, and "variation" is never defined [2].

The map names (Bakurani, Ozeti, Zestafona), their points of interest and relative sizes remain player-reported [14][15][16]. Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, released 15 Oct 2026) now officially adds a rain weather preset, moves and rebuilds all three team spawns on Bakurani, and adds a Large Shelter buildable "for covering key assets or keeping the rain off" [17][18][19]. The official 0.2.0 notes name Bakurani (in the spawn change) but add no new named map; the Steam page still says only that "more maps" are planned [1][18]. The earlier press-reported rain claims are therefore officially confirmed in substance; the "fixed for the whole match" detail is still press-only [11][12][18].

Confidence is Medium (raised from Low in v1.0.0). Scale, setting, destruction headlines, the sandbox usage, the 0.2.0 rain preset and the Bakurani spawn move rest on official text (Steam page captured 2026-10-08; Season 02 posts of 9 to 15 Oct 2026); the other named map detail does not and is labelled player-reported. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot. Depth is in launch-maps-reference and destructibility-and-level-design.

text:
Verified 2026-10-30 against Update 0.2.0 (official posts 9 to 15 Oct 2026); items dated 2026-10-08 are the unchanged Season 1 baseline.

- Official: the setting is "derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe" with a destructible battlefield (Steam page, live capture 2026-10-08) [1]. The name "Kolchia" and the PV-1 conflict come from the FAQ (18 Feb 2026), not the Steam page [3].
- Official: the Steam page states the current Early Access build has "large-scale maps with dynamic objective zones" and a "100-player, three-team" experience [1].
- Official: the Steam page says the full version is planned to include "more maps" and "additional objective variations", alongside new vehicle types including fighter jets; no map is named and no date given (live capture 2026-10-08) [1]. "Additional objective variations" is not defined and is not shown to be the press release's "variations" [2].
- Official: the Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area within a 256 km² map (FAQ, 18 Feb 2026, pre-release). The Steam page repeats the 2x2 km zone "within larger maps" but not the total [1][3].
- Official: players can destroy apartment blocks with rocket launchers and tear through towns in armoured tanks; players can build and fortify key locations, for example a forward operating base at a chokepoint (Steam page, live capture 2026-10-08) [1].
- Official: Early Access includes "Destruction & Build Mechanics" (FAQ, 18 Feb 2026) [3].
- Press release (Team17, 10 Sep 2026): three maps, each with three variations [2]. No official Steam post in the snapshot repeats this count.
- Official: Season 02 was announced for 15 Oct 2026 (22 Sep 2026 teaser) as "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" (30 Sep 2026) [5][7]. The Season 02 patch notes (14 Oct 2026) describe a "New Rain Weather Preset" and the 15 Oct 2026 post states Update 0.2.0 was released and servers were back online [18][19].
- Official (0.2.0, 14 to 15 Oct 2026): the rain preset makes surfaces, vehicles and characters visibly wet; rain sounds differ by what it falls on and whether you are under cover, indoors, in a vehicle or in the open; destroying a roof makes rain visibly come through it; thunder rolls in during heavier rain, every player on the server hears the same strike at the same time from the same direction, and it is loud enough to mask footsteps; spotting range is affected by rain; Molotov fire is reduced by rain [18]. The 9 Oct 2026 preview describes the preset as changing "visibility, engagement ranges and sound" and says rain "interacts with the environment, including damaged and destroyed structures" [17].
- Official (0.2.0): Bakurani's three team spawns "have been moved and rebuilt, each with purpose-built routes to the zone", which Bulkhead says "should provide a more balanced match across each team" [18]. The patch notes do not give new spawn coordinates or say which areas are affected [18].
- Official (0.2.0): a new Large Shelter buildable ("a large metal shelter for covering key assets or keeping the rain off"), buildable with the medium hammer and above, costing 250 build supply [18].
- Official: the posts through 2026-10-15 add no new named map; the Steam page's "more maps" remains an unspecified plan [1][18]. No official post after 2026-10-15 is in the 2026-10-30 snapshot.
- Press (pre-release): rain is "an additional weather state per map and not a dynamic event mid match", attributed by Vice to a Bulkhead post on X that was not viewed [11][12]. The official notes do not state whether the rain state can change within a match.
- Official: patch 0.1.2 changed buildable-destruction rewards and buildable crit-spot behaviour; it has no map, terrain or weather entry [5]. The Season 1 changelog has one map-related fix (below) [6].

text:
## Reconciling "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations"

Official usage of "sandbox" is consistent across posts: "a large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox" with "building and destruction mechanics" on the Steam page, "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox" in the 21 May 2026 post, "makes the sandbox 100% player-driven" in the FAQ (about proximity chat), and a "100 player Tactical All Out Warfare sandbox" in the announcement trailer post [1][3][8][9]. It describes freedom of play, not a type of map. The map count comes only from the press release: three maps with three variations each [2]. The two are compatible.

"Variation" is undefined in every official text read [1][2][3][4]. A community guide lists about three named areas per map (for example Default, Farmland, Lumberyard on Bakurani) that come up from a rotation [16]. This plausibly matches "three variations" but is an inference, and the FAQ's "multiple locations and POIs" in Kolchia is an equally plausible referent [3]. Treat the equivalence as unverified.

## Player-reported map roster (Season 01)

Player-reported; see launch-maps-reference for the full profiles and the source conflicts.

| Map | Region label | Described terrain | Relative size | Source |
|-----|--------------|-------------------|---------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Kavkazi | River valley, town, factory district, snow-capped northern mountains | Smallest | [14][15][16] |
| Ozeti | Europe | Wooded river basin, hill town, walled football stadium, church, farmland | About 4x Bakurani | [14][15][16] |
| Zestafona | North America | River bend, warehouse and rail districts, shipping, farmland, forest | About 4x Bakurani | [14][15][16] |

A further "Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari" sniper map and "Saburtulo" appear in one roster but are listed as not confirmed playable [16]. They are not counted as launch maps. The "Georgia" in the devlog is a real-world reference-gathering trip, not a map name [4]. Assessment: the Georgian-sounding map names fit that trip, but no official text links them (confidence Low).

## Points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Named features | Source |
|-----|----------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, Sunflower complex and church, Lumberyard, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, numbered towers | [15] |
| Ozeti | Stadium complex, hillside churches, Shops, Pool, Industrial, Lumberyard, farms, numbered towers | [15] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, large factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, Offices, Water Towers, farmland | [15] |

One guide counts 171 control zones across the three maps [15]. Another records three or four zone positions per map and three live tower objectives on Zestafona [14]. These counts differ, so no figure is given as fact. The only official statement about locations is "multiple locations and POIs" [3].

## Size

| Claim | Value | Class | Source |
|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| Control Zone | Randomised 2x2 km | Official (Steam page and FAQ) | [1][3] |
| Whole map | 256 km² | Official (FAQ, 18 Feb 2026, pre-release) | [3] |
| Whole map, repeated | 256 km², fully destructible | Third-party roadmap | [13] |
| Whole world | About 16 km edge to edge | Player-reported | [16] |
| Play circle | 500 m radius (550 m Ozeti) | Player-reported | [16] |

Assessment: 16 km x 16 km equals 256 km², so the community figure is consistent with the official area if the map is square, which the official text does not say. Medium confidence that 256 km² still holds: it dates from seven months before launch and is absent from the Steam page. The 2x2 km zone is 4 km², about 1.6% of the map (arithmetic from [3]). The 500 m radius play-circle claim conflicts with the official 2x2 km zone and is not adopted [1][16].

## Destructibility

Official: a destructible battlefield where rocket launchers destroy apartment blocks and tanks tear through towns, and "the world around you reacts to your presence" [1]. "Destruction & Build Mechanics" is a listed Early Access pillar [3], and "Base Building & Destruction" is a trailer feature [9]. Since 0.1.2, rewards for destroying buildables scale with build progress [5]. No official source gives a per-structure destruction model, which terrain can be deformed, or whether damage persists across matches. A third-party piece says terrain as well as buildings can be reshaped [13]; official sources mention only buildings. See destructibility-and-level-design.

## Weather and time of day

Since Update 0.2.0 (14 to 15 Oct 2026) the game has an officially documented rain weather preset [18]. Documented effects, all from the patch notes: wet surfaces, vehicles and characters; rain audio that depends on the surface and on whether you are under cover, indoors, in a vehicle or outdoors; rain visibly coming through destroyed roofs; server-synchronised thunder during heavier rain, loud enough to mask footsteps; a change to spotting range; reduced Molotov fire [18]. The Molotov entry also says it can burn destructible foliage and is affected by rain [18]. The preview adds that the preset changes "visibility, engagement ranges and sound" [17].

The notes give no numbers (spotting-range change, Molotov reduction, thunder timing), no statement of how a match gets the rain preset, and no statement that it is fixed for the match; the "not a dynamic event mid match" wording is press-only [11][18]. They do not mention a day/night cycle or other presets, and none is documented in any official text read. Assessment (confidence Medium): the Large Shelter's purpose line suggests rain matters for assets left uncovered, but the notes do not state a gameplay penalty. Season 1 (0.1.2) baseline: no weather state was documented, only "new map conditions" [5].

text:
This document does two jobs. First, it lists the channels BULKHEAD and Team17 are confirmed to use for WARDOGS, based on the official Steam posts saved locally on 2026-10-08. Second, it rates every outlet and site cited anywhere in this knowledge base for reliability, commercial conflict of interest and track record against the official text. It is the basis for future staleness and trust decisions.

The Steam store page (browser-rendered live capture of 2026-10-08) and the Steam News hub are the only channels whose address and content are fully verified. Official posts confirm that a community Discord and "socials" exist [6][11], and that a Twitch show and a contest site were used [9][22], and the live store page links Discord, X, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and QQ [1], but neither the snapshots nor the capture contain a Discord invite or X handle. On 2026-10-08 the live page showed English "Mostly Positive" (63,179) and "Total reviews in all languages: 95,146" [1], while the storefront review API showed 109,396 reviews (81,290 positive, 74.3% computed) [3]; the two all-language totals disagree and the cause is unexplained.

Season 02 gave a first test of the outlets against official text. Update 0.2.0 (released 15 Oct 2026) was documented in the Season 02 Preview (9 Oct), Patch Notes (14 Oct) and the live post (15 Oct) [58][59][60]. Scored against them, pre-release press and seller claims split: confirmed items were mostly specific, concrete content (rain, four weapons, a Molotov, an anti-air vehicle), while every claim about a progression wipe, cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, Gold Bar persistence or the Black Market is not mentioned in the notes. The full scorecard is in season-2-announcements; this document records what it means for reliability grades. The Preview also repeats the studio's "3+ million sales and counting" (9 Oct), a self-reported figure [58].

Confidence is Medium. The channel and review facts rest on official or first-party data (High on their own). The outlet ratings are judgements. I did not re-open every outlet page this session, so track-record notes compare claims already recorded in other KB documents against the official posts, and each rating states that basis.

text:
- Steam is the authoritative channel: 32 of the 65 items in the saved news feed are official posts from BULKHEAD (Steam news snapshot, 2026-10-08) [1][2].
- Official posts confirm a community Discord of "10k+ members" on 9 Feb 2026 and refer to "socials" and Discord announcements, but give no invite link or X handle. The live store page links Discord, X, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and QQ and says developers engage via Discord, X and YouTube; the link targets (handles, invites) were not captured, so they stay unconfirmed [1][6][7].
- Review figures at 2026-10-08 have two scopes that disagree. Live store page: English Mostly Positive (63,179) and "Total reviews in all languages: 95,146" [1]. Storefront review API (same day): 81,290 positive, 28,106 negative, 109,396 total [3]. The 95,146 versus 109,396 gap is unexplained.
- Methodology lesson: the storefront-API JSON omits page-only fields (anti-cheat product, Steam Deck status, the Early Access developer Q&A), so absence from the API JSON is not evidence of absence from the page; the live page capture is the Primary store source [1].
- The live page names the anti-cheat as Elytra (kernel level) and shows Steam Deck compatibility as Unsupported [1].
- Steam post bodies are now readable from the local snapshot, so patch facts can rest on official text. The earlier "bodies do not render" caveat in other documents is resolved for the 32 official posts.
- Official text confirms, against earlier uncertainty: the 2 Oct balance hotfix (IR Rangefinders disabled until Season 02, CIWS about 6 s instead of 12 s) [21], the 30 Sep date for 0.1.2 [19], and three approved hosts named on 8 Sep [22].
- Season 02 outcome (0.2.0): the official notes do not mention a progression wipe or a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, so those pre-release claims stay unconfirmed; the only support after launch is press paraphrase (PCGamesN 17 and 25 Oct) [59][62][63]. Absence from the notes is not a denial.
- How press rumours scored against the 0.2.0 notes: 12 of 29 pre-release claims confirmed, 3 partly, 2 contradicted, 10 not mentioned, 2 press-only (season-2-announcements). Specific content claims held up; wipe and currency claims did not gain support [59].
- The 2026-10-30 feed index lists 84 items, 35 official; the three new official posts are the Preview, Patch Notes and the live post, and later items are press (PCGamesN, SteamDB, PlayGround.ru). No official post after 2026-10-15 was seen. PlayGround.ru items are not used in this KB.
- Press (PCGamesN, 16 to 27 Oct 2026, fetched 2026-10-30, not archived): a removed blue-team bonus and Driver-track exploit bans, a possibly early Season 3, slower season cadence and two new approved hosts. These are press only and never establish a fact alone [61][62][63][64].
- Commercial sellers (boosting, hosting) and single-source outlets are rated lowest; their claims are leads, never facts (see the register).

text:
- **Official**: authored by BULKHEAD or Team17 (Steam announcements, official sites, press release). Source rank 1-3 in `SOURCE_REGISTRY.md`.
- **Press**: independent news outlet reporting on the game (rank 5).
- **Player-reported**: fan sites, guides, wikis, hosts, sellers (ranks 4 and 6). Never establishes a fact alone.
- **COI**: commercial conflict of interest, meaning the publisher sells something the article promotes (boosting, hosting, cash).
- **Reliability grade**: R1 matches official text and is usable as a secondary confirmation; R2 usable with corroboration; R3 lead only, label player-reported; R4 do not cite for facts. Grades are Assessment, not fact.
- **Baseline**: values recorded on 2026-10-08, before Season 02, so later diffs are mechanical. After 15 Oct 2026 they are history, not current values.

| Gaming with Daopa | Community repost | Unknown | Closed-beta notes dated 14 Aug are not in the saved official feed; unverified [2][57] | R4 |
| PCGamesN (Season 02 coverage, 10 to 27 Oct) | Press | None found | Its 10 Oct blue-team article matches the official faction experiment (Bakurani spawn changes, Lonestar bonuses, 20% discount for a losing team) [58][59][65]. The 16, 17, 25 and 27 Oct items (bonus removal, early Season 3, cadence, new hosts) have no official counterpart in the snapshot and cannot be tested [61][62][63][64] | R2 for what the notes confirm; items without an official counterpart are leads only |

Assessment: ranking the outlets by agreement with official text, wire and aggregator press (Gfinity, MP1st, InGameNews, PlayDay, Push Square) is dependable on dates and patch contents; sellers and wikis are dependable only when an official post confirms the specific claim. Confidence High for the agreement findings (compared line by line to official text), Medium for the COI judgements (inferred from what each site sells).

## Season 02 rumour scoring (reliability lessons)

Scored on 2026-10-30 against the official Preview, Patch Notes and live post [58][59][60]; the claim-by-claim table is in season-2-announcements.

| Source type | Pre-release behaviour | Outcome against 0.2.0 | Lesson |
|-------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------|
| Official posts (teaser, 0.1.2, hotfix) | Date, "larger content update", IR Rangefinder batteries | All five official-confirmed claims confirmed | Official forward statements held |
| Press (Vice, KeenGamer) | Rain, a wipe, Gold Bar conversion | Rain confirmed; wipe and conversion not mentioned in the notes | Content claims reliable when concrete; currency and wipe claims relayed from a video or unnamed source were not supported |
| Seller blogs (Timesaver, MMOEXP) | Mix of inference and podcast items | Weapons confirmed; launch time and grind claims contradicted; honeypot, ammo, season length not mentioned or press-only | Keep R3/R4; use only where an official post confirms the item |
| Wiki (Dexerto) | Black Market, wipe | Notes name the Gold Market only | Undated wikis stay R3 |

Assessment: concrete, falsifiable content claims (named weapons, a Molotov, an anti-air vehicle) were mostly right, which fits a leak or a seen preview; claims about currency, wipes and later seasons had no support in the notes. Confidence Medium: it rests on a single set of notes and on "not mentioned".

## Where earlier KB documents are corrected or sharpened by official text

| Topic | Earlier KB wording | Official text | Effect |
|-------|--------------------|---------------|--------|
| IR Rangefinders and CIWS (2 Oct) | CWIS 12 s to 6 s "reported by a conflicted source"; battery rule "player-reported" | Official: Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02 where they "will require batteries"; CIWS now about 6 s versus 12 s [21] | Can be treated as official; supersedes the conflict note |
| Security hotfix (2 Oct) | Ambiguous whether scheduled or completed | Post at 00:13 UTC announces a planned 08:00 UTC fix on "Friday 2nd", one hour [20] | Resolved: scheduled |
| Closed beta dates | Open question whether 21-23 Aug and 3-6 Sep were one beta | Two betas: 21-23 Aug closed beta [7][8][9]; Closed Beta 02 announced 1 Sep, opened to all on 5 Sep until Sunday 08:00 UTC [10][11] | Resolved: two betas |
| Season 1 changelog date | 10 Sep | Official "Pre-Load Live & Season 1 Changelog" is dated 9 Sep [12] | Date should read 9 Sep for the notes, 10 Sep for launch |
| Season 02 wipe | Reported by Dexerto and Timesaver | Teaser contained only the date; the 0.2.0 Patch Notes (14 Oct) do not mention a wipe or a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion [17][19][59] | Still unconfirmed by official text; press (PCGamesN) paraphrases a wipe or economy reset after launch [62][63] |
| Hosting partners | Fan guide says QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM | Official post names the same three on 8 Sep [22] | Confirmed |

topic: Editions, regional pricing, Supporter Pack contents, platform roadmap, Early Access policy

text:
WARDOGS is sold on Steam as two purchase options plus a separate DLC: the Standard game (package 671715), the Supporter Edition (package 1746527) and the Supporter Pack DLC (app 4809960) [1][2]. In the 2026-10-08 store snapshot the US prices are USD 39.99, 49.99 and 12.99 and the UK prices are GBP 36.99, 45.99 and 11.99, with no discount active [1][2]. A second storefront snapshot on 2026-10-30, after Update 0.2.0 (15 Oct 2026), shows the same US and UK prices, the same Windows-only platform flags and no discount for the base game and the Supporter Pack [19]. Store prices did not change with Season 02. The Supporter Pack is cosmetic content (camos, a scoreboard icon, two bobbleheads). The developer's stated policy is that it is the only monetisation during Early Access and that in-game cash, gold bars and camos will never be sold [2][4].

Steam lists Windows only and the live store page shows Steam Deck compatibility as "Unsupported" [1][18]. The official Steam posts in the snapshot say nothing about Linux, Xbox or PS5; those statements (Xbox and PS5 "sometime in 2028", Linux unsupported with Proton work ongoing) come from press reports and are labelled as such [13][14][15][16]. The store page's own Early Access section says the developers plan a lower price during Early Access and a higher price at full release, and expect Early Access to last around 1 to 2 years [18]. Official Steam posts record 1.25 million copies sold on 11 Sep, 2 million on 15 Sep and 3 million on 26 Sep 2026 [5][6][7]; the Season 02 Preview of 9 Oct says "3+ million sales and counting" (studio claim, no new figure) [20]. Reviews on 2026-10-08 differ by source: the reviews API gave 81,290 positive of 109,396 (74.3%) while the live store page showed 95,146 total in all languages, both "Mostly Positive"; the gap is unexplained [11][18].

Confidence is Medium. Prices, DLC contents, sales milestones, the monetisation and pricing policy and review counts rest on official Steam data. The console and Linux claims rest on press only and cap the document.

- The Supporter Edition was announced on 11 Aug 2026 alongside pre-orders, which granted guaranteed Closed Beta access [4].
- Supporter Pack contents: three "Starter Weapon" camos (Valkyra A-91, Lonestar Bushmaster, Manticore KH-2002), a Littlebird Helicopter "Taxi" camo, a hideable scoreboard Supporter Icon, a Grenade Bobblehead and a Helmet Bobblehead [2][4]. The cosmetic-only character is the developer's own statement.
- Developer policy: no monetisation during Early Access except this pack; cash and gold bars never sold; camos never directly purchasable [2][4]. Earlier FAQ: "No Battlepass. No Pay to Win" [9].
- Steam lists Windows only; no Mac or Linux support flag on the store [1]. Steam Deck compatibility is officially "Unsupported" on the live store page [18]. Console and Linux/Proton status is press-reported, not in the official posts.
- Official pricing policy (store page, Primary): priced lower during Early Access, higher at full release; the price may be raised closer to full release; Early Access expected to last around 1 to 2 years [18].
- Sales (official Steam posts): 1.25 million (11 Sep), 2 million (15 Sep), 3 million (26 Sep 2026) [5][6][7].
- Reviews (2026-10-08): API all-language 81,290 of 109,396 positive [11]; live store page English 63,179 and all-language total 95,146, both "Mostly Positive" [18]. The 109,396 versus 95,146 difference is unexplained.

## Editions (snapshot 2026-10-08)

The store snapshot (US and GB storefronts) shows the Standard and Supporter Edition options on the main page and the Supporter Pack as DLC; the pack's own entry also offers the Supporter Edition as the bundle [1][2]. The main page lists two DLC app ids (4809960 and 4809930); only 4809960 (Supporter Pack) was captured, so the second is unidentified [1]. Neither storefront showed a discount [1][2].

## Supporter Pack contents

The DLC entry says the pack "offers additional cosmetic content" and lists three "Starter Weapon" camos (Valkyra Branded A-91 Rifle, Lonestar Branded Bushmaster, Manticore Branded KH-2002), a Littlebird Helicopter "Taxi" camo, a Supporter Icon on the scoreboard (can be hidden in settings), a Grenade Bobblehead and a Helmet Bobblehead [2]. The identical list appeared in the 11 Aug 2026 announcement [4]. The developer's three stated rules: no monetisation during Early Access, in-game cash and gold bars are never monetised, and camos can never be directly purchased [2][4]. The launch press release repeats that cash, gold bars and status-based camouflage are not for sale [12]. Nothing in these sources lists a gameplay advantage, so cosmetic-only is the developer's statement, not independently tested.

## Platforms

The store snapshot flags Windows true, Mac false, Linux false; minimum OS Windows 10, recommended Windows 11 [1]. The live store page (live capture 2026-10-08) shows "Steam Deck Compatibility: Unsupported", an official Valve status, and lists Kernel Level Anti-Cheat: Elytra [18]. The official Steam posts in the snapshot contain no statement on Linux, Xbox or PS5. A 3 Mar 2026 post lists "Console Release?" among questions answered, but the answer is in a video and not in the post text [10]. Press reports Xbox and PS5 versions for "sometime in 2028", and Xbox Store wishlists open on 10 Sep 2026 [13][14].

## Review snapshot

Steam's review summary (all languages, scope `language=all`) on 2026-10-08 was "Mostly Positive": 81,290 positive and 28,106 negative, 109,396 total, 74.3% positive [11]. The earlier English-only figure is a different scope and is not comparable. The live store page (live capture 2026-10-08) shows English reviews "Mostly Positive (63,179)" and "Total reviews in all languages: 95,146 (Mostly Positive)" [18]. This is 14,250 fewer than the API's 109,396 for the same day; the cause is unexplained, so both figures are recorded and neither is preferred. The page does not show the earlier "79%" English percentage, which is not repeated here. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026 [14].

The US and GB rows come from the 2026-10-08 store snapshot; the other rows come from an earlier price-field fetch the same day and are not in the snapshot [3]. The Supporter Edition costs USD 10.00 / GBP 9.00 more than Standard, against USD 12.99 / GBP 11.99 for the pack alone, so the bundle saves USD 2.99 / GBP 2.99 versus buying both separately (arithmetic on the snapshot prices) [1][2]. Assessment: the Turkey price is far below the others; confidence High as a reading of the table, with no inference about intent.

## Early Access pricing and monetisation statements

The developer's 11 Aug 2026 post says its devlog covers "early access strategy, stair stepped pricing and long-term monetisation plans" but gives no price steps in the post text [4]. The press release describes a tiered model rewarding earlier backers and gives USD 39.99 [12]. No full-release price or Early Access end date appears in the snapshot posts or press release [4][12]. The live store page's Early Access section is the official statement: "we plan for WARDOGS to be priced lower during Early Access, with a higher price at full release"; asked whether pricing differs during and after Early Access, it answers "Yes" and adds "we may raise the price closer to full release"; and it expects Early Access to last "around 1 to 2 years", with the exact duration subject to change [18]. No full-release price or fixed date is given there either [18]. The 7 Apr 2026 post says a metagame (Black Market and Vault, Player Skills and Challenge System) will be built throughout Early Access; it states no pricing [8]. The 18 Feb 2026 FAQ states "No Battlepass. No Pay to Win. Earn cosmetics by playing." [9]. The developer also encourages refunds if the game or beta does not meet expectations [4].

## Store-page features

The live store page lists Online PvP, Steam Achievements (10) and Accessibility Features (4), the content note "Includes Interactive Elements (In-game chat, Online interactivity)", 14 supported languages (English has interface, full audio and subtitles; French, Italian, German and Spanish - Spain are among those listed) and the requirement to agree to the WARDOGS EULA [18].

## Pre-order and beta access

Pre-orders opened on 11 Aug 2026 for the 10 Sep Early Access launch and granted guaranteed access to the Closed Beta of 21 to 23 Aug; the developer said Steam key caps ended the old signup route [4].

## Platform roadmap and statements

| Platform | Status | Date of statement | Source and class |
|----------|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| Windows (Steam) | Live, Early Access since 10 Sep 2026; Windows flag true | 2026-10-08 | [1] official |
| Mac | Store flag false | 2026-10-08 | [1] official |
| Xbox | "Sometime in 2028"; wishlists open | 10 Sep 2026 | [13] press, not in official posts |
| PS5 | "Sometime in 2028" | 11 Sep 2026 | [14] press, not in official posts |
| Steam Deck | Compatibility "Unsupported" | 2026-10-08 | [18] official |
| Linux / SteamOS | Store Linux flag false; Proton work ongoing per press | Aug to 25 Sep 2026 | [1] official flag; [15][16] press |

On 5 Sep 2026 the developers were reported to say "We do not officially support Linux and we cannot commit to having support for launch", that earlier Linux success in tests was by chance, and that buyers who expected Proton support could ask for a refund [15]. A developer comment dated 25 Sep 2026 (in the reader comments of that article) says there is no new timeline [15]. In August a developer was reported on the Steam forums as working on Proton support [16]. The Steam Deck status is officially "Unsupported" [18]; the Linux and Proton items above are press-only context. The store page names Elytra as the kernel-level anti-cheat, but press reports linking an anti-cheat to the Linux block are unconfirmed [15][18].

## Sales milestones (official Steam posts)

| Milestone | Date (UTC) | Source |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| 1.25 million copies sold | 11 Sep 2026 | [5] |
| 2 million copies sold | 15 Sep 2026 | [6] |
| 3 million copies sold, "in just over 2 weeks since launching into Early Access" | 26 Sep 2026 | [7] |
| "3+ million sales and counting" (no new number; studio claim) | 9 Oct 2026 | [20] |
| Peak 428,666 concurrent on Steam | about 13 Sep 2026 (press) | [17] |

Earlier drafts used press figures ("over 1 million" on 13 Sep and "3 million at 18 days"). The official posts supersede them: 3 million was announced 26 Sep, 16 days after the 10 Sep launch, not 18 [7][17]. The 1.25 million post carries no detail beyond the figure and an apology for delays [5]. The 2 million post's numbers snapshot is an image and was not read [6].

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter developed by BULKHEAD (Derby, UK) and published by Team17 [1][2]. It entered Steam Early Access on 10 September 2026 at a Standard price of GBP 36.99 (UK) and USD 39.99 (US) [1][5]. A launch-day official post says consoles are coming in 2028 [18]. The launch was preceded by two closed betas: 21 to 23 Aug, then Closed Beta 02, announced 1 Sep and opened to everyone on 5 Sep [6][11][12].

Official Steam posts now confirm the full patch sequence: the Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep, at pre-load), Launch Stability Hotfix #1 (10 Sep), Patch 0.11 (announced 12 Sep, scheduled for 14 Sep), Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep), a security and stability hotfix (2 Oct) and an IR Rangefinder and CIWS balance hotfix (2 Oct) [17][19][21][25][26][27]. BULKHEAD announced 1.25 million copies sold on 11 Sep, 2 million on 15 Sep and 3 million on 26 Sep [20][22][24]. Season 02 was released as Update 0.2.0 on 15 October 2026 (live post 09:59 UTC, "Servers are back online") after a Preview on 9 October and full Patch Notes on 14 October [34][35][36]. The Preview repeats the studio's own claim of "3+ million sales and counting" [34]. The live Steam page shows English reviews "Mostly Positive" (63,179) and 95,146 reviews in all languages, while the review API returned 109,396 on the same day; that gap is unexplained [1][33].

Confidence is Medium. Dates, prices, patch contents, sales milestones, the Early Access statement and the Season 02 statement rest on official Steam posts and the live store page, but the headline all-language review count conflicts between the page (95,146) and the API (109,396) with no explanation. Press is used only where no official text exists (console platform names, beta-participant figures) and is labelled. The 0.2.0 notes do not mention a progression wipe or a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, so those stay unconfirmed; no official post after 15 October appears in the 2026-10-30 snapshot. Press (PCGamesN, 16 to 27 Oct) is used only as labelled press [37][38][39][40]. Store prices were unchanged between the 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-30 storefront snapshots [1].

## Developer, publisher and platforms

BULKHEAD is a Derby-based studio founded in 2015, previously known for The Turing Test and Battalion 1944; Team17 (part of everplay Group plc) publishes [2]. The Steam store data lists BULKHEAD as developer and Team17 as publisher, with Windows as the only platform (Mac and Linux false) [1][5]. Minimum OS is Windows 10 and recommended is Windows 11 [5]. The live page lists Steam Deck compatibility as Unsupported, and notes kernel-level anti-cheat (Elytra) and a third-party WARDOGS EULA (live capture 2026-10-08) [1]. Team17's game page also lists NVIDIA GeForce NOW [3]. The official launch-day post reads "COMING TO CONSOLES IN 2028" [18]; the PS5 and Xbox names and the "sometime in 2028" wording come from press (Sep 2026) [28][29]. Linux and Proton status is in editions-pricing-platforms.

## Editions and pricing (checked 2026-10-08)

| Item | GBP | USD | Source |
|------|-----|-----|--------|
| WARDOGS (Standard) | 36.99 | 39.99 | [1][5] |
| Supporter Edition (base game plus Supporter Pack) | 45.99 | 49.99 | [1][5] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC, sold separately) | 11.99 | 12.99 | [1][5] |

GBP 36.99 and USD 39.99 are the same Standard edition in two currencies; the Supporter Edition is a separate SKU [5]. The Supporter Pack is cosmetic only (camos, a scoreboard icon and bobbleheads). BULKHEAD's official pre-order post states there is no monetisation during Early Access beyond it, that in-game cash and gold bars will never be monetised, and that camos can never be bought directly [6]. Contents and regional prices are in editions-pricing-platforms. The pre-order post refers to "stair stepped pricing" [6], and both the launch press release and the Steam page's Early Access section say the game is priced lower during Early Access with a higher price at full release, possibly raised "closer to full release" as content is added; no full price is disclosed [1][2].

## Reception (checked 2026-10-08)

Two Steam sources disagree on the review total, both captured 2026-10-08. The live store page shows English reviews "Mostly Positive" (63,179) and "Total reviews in all languages: 95,146 (Mostly Positive)" [1]. The review API summary (score 6, "Mostly Positive") shows 81,290 positive and 28,106 negative, 109,396 in total across all languages, about 74.3% positive [33]. The 95,146 versus 109,396 gap (14,250) is unexplained; a different counting basis such as purchase type is a possible cause but neither source confirms it. The API gives a positive split and the page does not, so the 74.3% is API-scoped only. Version 1.0.0 of this document recorded 79% of 63,152 English-only reviews, a different filter, so figures across scopes are not a trend. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026, scope unstated [29].

## Developer roadmap statement

The Steam page's Early Access section (live capture 2026-10-08) says: "We expect WARDOGS to remain in Early Access for around 1 to 2 years", while adding that the developers do not want a long Early Access; the duration "may change" [1]. It says the full version is planned to be broader and more polished, and lists planned expansion: more maps, weapons, vehicles and gameplay variety; more in-depth progression systems; a stronger seasonal meta game; systems rewarding combat, support and logistics; new vehicle types including fighter jets; expanded weapon categories; additional objective variations; and continued balance, performance and stability work [1]. These are plans, not commitments or dates.

The official 7 Apr 2026 post says that throughout Early Access BULKHEAD is building a metagame including "The Black Market & Vault" and a "Player Skills & Challenge System"; the metagame foundation "is designed, but we will be building it throughout Early Access" [7]. The launch press release adds that work continues toward the wider meta game and long-term systems for 1.0 [2]. No dated roadmap to 1.0 is published; the only dated item is Season 02 on 15 Oct 2026 [23]. See season-2-announcements.

## Community channels

The Steam store page and Steam News hub for app 1867240 are the primary announcement channel [1][4]. Official posts confirm a community Discord ("10k+ members" on 9 Feb 2026), a community sign-up at community.wardogs.com, the Twitch show "The FPS Games Show" and three Approved Hosting Partners (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM) [8][9][13]. Team17's WARDOGS page links Team17's Discord, X and YouTube [3]. The Steam store page lists links to Discord, X, TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and QQ, and says players can engage with the developers via Discord, X and YouTube (live capture 2026-10-08); the link targets, invites and handles were not captured [1]. See community-and-source-reliability.

## Release timeline

| Date | Event | Source |
|------|-------|--------|
| 9 Feb 2026 | Announcement trailer; community Discord of "10k+ members" | [8] |
| 10 Feb 2026 | 100,000 Steam wishlists in three days | [14] |
| 26 May 2026 | 500,000 Steam wishlists | [15] |
| 11 Aug 2026 | Pre-orders open; Closed Beta dated 21 to 23 Aug; Supporter Edition announced | [6] |
| 13 Aug 2026 | Press release: "passed 800,000 wishlists" | [2] |
| 14 Aug 2026 | 1 million Steam wishlists, "six months after revealing" the game | [16] |
| 21-23 Aug 2026 | Closed Beta, pre-order access guaranteed; recap posted 24 Aug | [6][9][10] |
| 1 Sep 2026 | Closed Beta 02 announced; pre-order access handed out in waves | [11] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | Closed Beta 02 "is now an open beta", running until Sunday 08:00 UTC (6 Sep) | [12] |
| 9 Sep 2026 | Pre-load live and Season 1 changelog posted | [17] |
| 10 Sep 2026 | Steam Early Access launch (16:00 UTC per press); launch trailer; Launch Stability Hotfix #1 | [1][18][19][28] |
| 11 Sep 2026 | 1.25 million copies sold (official post 01:05 UTC) | [20] |
| 12 Sep 2026 | Patch 0.11 post thanks players for "400,000 Peak Concurrent Users" | [21] |
| 15 Sep 2026 | 2 million copies sold | [22] |
| 22 Sep 2026 | Season 02 teaser: 15 Oct 2026 | [23] |
| 26 Sep 2026 | 3 million copies sold in "just over 2 weeks"; Golden Joystick nomination for Best Early Access Game 2026 | [24] |
| 9 Oct 2026 | Season 02 Preview and press conference; "3+ million sales and counting" (studio claim) | [34] |
| 14 Oct 2026 | Season 02 Patch Notes posted; maintenance announced for 15 Oct | [35] |
| 15 Oct 2026 | Update 0.2.0 (Season 02) released, 09:59 UTC post | [36] |

The beta sequence resolves the earlier open question: the 21 to 23 Aug Closed Beta and Closed Beta 02 (announced 1 Sep, opened to everyone on 5 Sep, ended 6 Sep 08:00 UTC) were separate events [6][11][12]. The 3 to 6 Sep dates in the Gfinity changelog that v1.0.0 relied on match Closed Beta 02; the official posts are the authority for its window.

Concurrency figures differ by scope and date. The official 12 Sep post claims 400,000 peak concurrent users after launch [21]. CoGConnected reported 245,118 peak concurrent in the final playtest and nearly 500,000 Closed Beta participants (13 Sep) [30]. These measure different periods (launch weekend versus the pre-launch playtest), so they do not conflict. Push Square cited nearly 300,000 concurrent per SteamDB on 11 Sep [29]. Early Access content at launch was three maps with three variations each [2].

## Patch history

All rows rest on the official Steam posts. Full per-change lists are in patch-history.

| Date | Version | Headline changes | Source |
|------|---------|------------------|--------|
| 9 Sep 2026 (pre-load; live for launch) | Season 1 changelog | Church roof exploit fix, report tracking with weighted reports, server browser filtering rework, Z20 Lakota balance pass, crash fixes; XP curve slowed for levels 6 to 50 (level 20: 111,500 to 250,000); Artillery to Career 90, Heavy Tank to Driver 35; Forward Operating Base vendor price $2,500 to $7,500 and other price changes | [17] |
| 10 Sep 2026 | Launch Stability Hotfix #1 | Forced client restart and controlled login batches for join failures, unexpected kicks and long login queues | [19] |
| 12 Sep post; maintenance Mon 14 Sep 08:00 UTC | Patch 0.11 | Server browser split into Official and Community, text search and persistent Community Server IDs, more Asia capacity, cash exploit and GPU crash fixes, 5% end-of-match cash bonus on Community servers for one week; economy-abuse stance announced | [21] |
| 30 Sep 2026 | Update 0.1.2 (Minor Patch) | Fix for crash WD-L020 linked to Windows 11 update KB5124010; server-authoritative revive checks, vehicle fly-through reward cap, buildable and FOB pallet reward limits; new Deploy flow; admin daily restart, RCON AllowedHosts and message caps; zero-tolerance exploit warning | [25] |
| 2 Oct 2026 | Security and stability hotfix | Announced 2 Oct 00:13 UTC for 08:00 UTC the same day; "minor security and stability issues"; about one hour downtime | [26] |
| 2 Oct 2026 | IR Goggles and CIWS balance hotfix | IR Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02, where they will require batteries; CIWS destroys the Havoc in about 6 s instead of 12 s ("we overcorrected"); no client download or downtime | [27] |
| 9 Oct 2026 | Season 02 Preview | Devlog; four weapons, Molotov, four vehicles, three buildables, rain, experimental Wager Vendor, faction experiment | [34] |
| 14 Oct 2026 | Season 02 Patch Notes | Full 0.2.0 notes; maintenance 15 Oct 08:00 to 09:30 UTC | [35] |
| 15 Oct 2026 | Update 0.2.0 (Season 02) | Released, servers back online | [36] |

The 0.11 post is an announcement dated 12 Sep with maintenance scheduled for 14 Sep; the saved posts include no separate deployed notice. The 2 Oct balance post is titled "IR Goggles" but its body names IR Rangefinders [27].

## Season 02 (released 15 Oct 2026)

BULKHEAD's "Season 02 Teaser" of 22 Sep 2026 gave 15 Oct 2026 and a trailer [23]; the 0.1.2 post described Season 02 as "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [25]. The Preview of 9 Oct 2026 (16:00 UTC) previewed the content and promised notes "early next week" [34]. The Patch Notes of 14 Oct 2026 (14:59 UTC) gave a maintenance window of 08:00 to 09:30 UTC on 15 Oct, about 90 minutes of downtime [35]. The live post of 15 Oct (09:59 UTC) reads "We have now released Update 0.2.0. Servers are back online." [36]

Headline content (Update 0.2.0, 14-15 Oct 2026, final names from the notes): four weapons (TCX-SPR, PP-19 Bizon, Evo-3 Ultra, M14); a Molotov; four vehicles (Wolf-110, Wolf-110 [M2 Browning], T-72B3, Flakpanzer Gepard); three buildables (MG Nest, Large Shelter, Wooden Step); a rain weather preset; IR Rangefinder batteries; a combat, suppression, build, economy and role-track XP rebalance; team switching limits, a Forgive/Punish team-kill vote, region-based ping limits; and a faction experiment with Season 2 only Lonestar bonuses [35]. Values live in the owner documents (see patch-history for the pointer table). The Wager Vendor "is not available at Season 2 launch" and is "not a permanent addition" [35].

Not mentioned in the notes: a progression wipe, a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, death-penalty rules, new named maps, RCON or ini changes, console or Linux statements and Season 3 timing [35]. Absence from the notes is not a denial. The pre-release wipe, rain and Gold Bar claims came from a boosting-seller article and a community wiki [31][32]; rain was confirmed, the wipe and conversion are not mentioned. Graded rumours are in season-2-announcements, and the currency model is in season-reset-and-currencies. Assessment: confidence in the official 0.2.0 lines is High; in any wipe or Season 3 claim Low.

Press only (PCGamesN, fetched 2026-10-30): on 16 Oct a blue-team bonus (5% cash, 2.5% XP) was reported removed and a mid-season update promised [37]; on 17 Oct Season 3 was reported as possibly coming "significantly" forward [38]; on 25 Oct a roughly three-month season cadence and a Season 3 target of 12 Nov were reported [39]; on 27 Oct two new approved hosts (GG Host, 1of1 Servers) were reported [40]. None of these is in an official post in the snapshot.

- Launch-day instability (join failures, kicks, long login queues) was addressed by Launch Stability Hotfix #1 on 10 Sep 2026 [19].

- Patch 0.11 apologised for the server browser and Community Server handling and set a one-week 5% Community-server cash bonus (scheduled 14 Sep 2026) [21].
- 0.1.2 fixed a Windows 11 crash and tightened exploit rewards (30 Sep 2026) [25].
- IR Rangefinders are disabled in the vendor until Season 02 and will require batteries on return; CIWS time to kill on the Havoc was cut to about 6 s (2 Oct 2026) [27].
- Update 0.2.0 (15 Oct 2026) changed many Season 1 and 0.1.2 values; IR Rangefinders now run on batteries, and the Wager Vendor is announced but not live at launch [35].
- Pre-launch, BULKHEAD published a "10 Reasons NOT to Buy WARDOGS" video and an "11th Reason" post on anti-cheat and community servers [6][13].

Version 1.2.0 adds the Season 02 Preview (9 Oct), the Season 02 Patch Notes (14 Oct) and the "Season 02 is now live" post (15 Oct) from the 2026-10-30 snapshot [19][20][21]. The official titles settle the version labels: "Patch 0.11", "Update 0.1.2 (Minor Patch)" and, for Season 02, the live post says "We have now released Update 0.2.0" [9][10][21]. The two 2 Oct entries are two separate official posts [11][12]. ## Beta dates from the official posts

- **Closed Beta weekend**: the 20 Aug post says the closed beta is "this weekend", that the NDA is lifted, that a first wave of invites went out and that 'WARDOGS Playtest' can be pre-loaded; the schedule itself is an image, so no dates are in the text [3]. The 24 Aug recap names pre-order access "between August 21st - 23rd" and says that weekend's closed beta is over [4]. 21-23 Aug 2026 is therefore the official closed beta window.
- **Closed Beta 02**: announced 1 Sep 2026 "ahead of The FPS Games Show" (3 Sep, 18:00 UTC) as a scale test, with access in waves for pre-orders, and tests named as server scaling and browsing, Twitch Drops, DLC entitlements, VOIP and the login queue [5]. The post gives no start or end date. A press-reported 3-6 Sep window is in the unconfirmed list.
- **Open beta**: on 5 Sep 2026 at 21:08 UTC the closed beta became an open beta "until the Beta ends - Sunday at 08:00 UTC" [6]. The Sunday after that post is 6 Sep 2026 (derived from the post date).
- The recap announces The FPS Games Show for 3 Sep 2026, 18:00 UTC [4]. The 14 Aug closed beta notes found earlier are not in the official feed; see the Unconfirmed list.

## 9 Sep 2026, Pre-Load Live & Season 1 Changelog (Official) [7]

The post is the Early Access launch changelog (launch 10 Sep 2026 [2]).

- Exploits: fixed an exploit reaching an unintended church roof position.
- Reporting and moderation: new report tracking system; reports weighted so repeat and bad-faith reporters carry less influence; cheater bans announced in server when match termination is off; the "kicked from server" message appears only if actually banned.
- Server browser and front end: reworked server browser filtering; community server images no longer scale incorrectly; Host a server button links to the hosting page.
- Voice chat: fixed voice cutting out permanently after a failed join (stale channel rejoins, push to talk targeting and re-login recover); improved reliability under load and added a visible communication status.
- Gameplay and vehicles: Z20 Lakota balance pass and sluggish pitch fix; helicopter input damping on every input device; maximum operator rotation speed for vehicle turrets; 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables take more loadout room; tank aiming DPI fix; Z20 Lakota chase camera rotation rattle reduced by 6 dB.
- Performance and stability: DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without restart and the render target pool is configurable; fewer shadow cache refreshes; two frame generation crash paths fixed; more detailed GPU crash reports; a legacy graphics dependency removed; shadow quality clamped to Low on high benchmark scores; fixed crashes from off-thread network calls, closing a chatbox entry tooltip, buildables, and firing a weapon whose owner had left; dropped items no longer affect navigation; better startup reliability and messages.
- Progression: levels 10 to 20 slowed and the curve flattened from 35 onward; Artillery to Career level 90; Heavy Tank to Driver level 35; Forward Operating Base and Large Hammer vendor prices raised.

## 10 Sep 2026, Launch Stability Hotfix #1 (Official) [8]

- A small client update. Logged-in players were forced to close and restart, then prompted to download the update; all players returned to the login queue and were admitted in controlled batches, gradually increased as players successfully populated servers.
- Targets: players unable to join servers, players kicked unexpectedly during play, extended login queue times.
- No gameplay or economy values changed in the post.

## 14 Sep 2026, Patch 0.11 (Official) [9]

Announced in the 12 Sep 22:26 UTC post. Maintenance on Monday 14 Sep 2026 at 08:00 UTC (01:00 US Pacific), about one hour.

- Server browser: front end split into Community and Official browsers; unnecessary filtering removed from Official (no official modified game modes); filtering reliability improved on Community; text search added to Community; Show Empty/Full added to the quick bar; Host button directed to the correct location.
- Community Server IDs persist between matches and restarts, and each server has a unique ID (longer for security); they were previously wiped on map change and restart.
- Server names: must sort alphabetically regardless of special characters and numbers; more than one space at a time is no longer allowed.
- Apology bonus: community servers give a 5% End of Match cash bonus for the next week.
- Other fixes: various cash exploits fixed; more GPU crashes addressed.
- Capacity: server capacity in Asia increased.
- Economy abuse sanctions: cash exploit or bug abuse gets a timed ban scaled to prior bans and a cash and XP reset to 0; content that tutorialises exploits without reporting is treated as advertising cheats (permanent ban); XP farming gets the most serious bans, with permanent bans for joining XP-farming servers for more than a few minutes.
- Listed as not yet ready: community server favouriting, tiered priority queues for Community servers, Message of the Day prompt, improved warmup activities, disabling AFK kicking during seeding, team switching controls.

## 30 Sep 2026, Update 0.1.2 (Minor Patch) (Official) [10]

Posted 06:57 UTC; maintenance at 08:00 UTC, estimated one hour.

- Crash fix: WD-L020 crash caused by Windows 11 update KB5124010.
- Cash and XP exploits: revive validity checks fully server authoritative; vehicle fly-through exploit fixed with capped rewards; buildable destruction rewards scale with build progress (destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward); depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone awards reduced rewards.
- Sanctions: players caught abusing cash and XP exploits or Real Money Trading had cash and progression reset and risk permanent bans; leniency for first-time offenders is over.
- Server browser and UI: new DEPLOY flow (Official, Community, Infantry Mode, Low-Level); Advanced Filters back on the Official list; long server names no longer truncated (hover for the full name); Join shows connecting then queue position; Anonymous mode hides the server name on the loading screen and in the pause menu unless shown; region select shows how many regions are selected; gamepad support on DEPLOY.
- Server admins: daily restart time (UTC); RCON AllowedHosts; RCON message and broadcast lengths capped; RCON defaults to Standard response detail rather than Full, and config responses no longer expose server internals; ServerImageURL checked when config loads.
- Server stability: various stability hotfixes and increased server security.
- Bugs: throwables (grenades, smoke, C4) blocked from enclosed vehicle seats; adaptive crosshair hides when aiming down sights; buildable crit spots no longer reappear in place, get pushed into corners or jump to the far side, and favour a reachable spot; Havoc bug causing extra damage from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire fixed; localisation improved.
- Forward look: Season 02 is described as a larger content update with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and features.

## 2 Oct 2026, two official posts

| Post | Time (UTC) | Contents |
|------|-----------|----------|
| WARDOGS / Security & Stability Hotfix [11] | 00:13 | Heads-up that a hotfix is planned "tomorrow, Friday 2nd" at 08:00 UTC for minor security and stability issues affecting some players; expected downtime one hour |
| IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix [12] | 15:39 | Two balance changes within 12 hours as regional servers restart; no new client download or server downtime |

- Security and stability hotfix [11]: the post gives no detail of the issues and does not mention gameplay, balance or economy. The date wording ("tomorrow, Friday 2nd") sits oddly with a post time of 2 Oct 00:13 UTC; the hotfix time is stated as 08:00 UTC on Friday 2 Oct, so the post was presumably written the evening before in an Americas time zone. Assessment: Medium confidence, inferred from the post time.
- Balance hotfix [12]: IR Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02, where they will require batteries; the CIWS now destroys the Havoc in around 6 seconds instead of 12. BULKHEAD says it overcorrected the CIWS in the previous patch and hotfixed it "this morning".
- Whether the 08:00 UTC security hotfix and the CIWS "this morning" hotfix are the same operation is not stated; the posts are treated as separate.

## Season 02 teaser (Official, historical) [13]

Posted 22 Sep 2026 at 16:53 UTC: "WARDOGS Season 02 is coming", dated 15 October 2026, "Stay tuned for more details". The 0.1.2 post adds that Season 02 is a larger content update with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features [10]. Nothing else was official until the Preview of 9 Oct [19].

## 9 Oct 2026, Season 02 Preview (Official) [19]

Posted 16:00 UTC. A devlog recap and preview titled "Road to Season 2". It says Season 01 "is coming to a close", cites "3+ million sales and counting" (studio claim) and says full patch notes drop "early next week".

- Previewed content: four weapons (TCX Spear, M14, PP-19 Bizon, Evo-3 Ultra), a Molotov, four vehicles (Wolf-110, Wolf-110 (Assault), T-72, Flakpanzer Gepard), three buildables (MG Nest, Large Shelter, Wooden Step), a rain preset, an experimental Wager Vendor, IR Rangefinder batteries and helmet changes.
- Faction experiment: Lonestar (blue) gets Season 2 only cash and XP bonuses and multipliers and less visible uniforms; a vendor discount of 20% for a team at least 40 points behind second place; all faction spawns moved on Bakurani; hosts exploiting the faction bonus will be punished.
- Also: a first pre-season press conference, a Golden Joystick Awards reminder and a 24-hour extension of the 100K Clip Contest.
- The post says it is "the surface of what's coming" and that details could change. Names differ from the final notes (see below); the notes win.

## 14 Oct 2026, Season 02 Patch Notes (Official) [20]

Posted 14:59 UTC with a trailer. Maintenance window: 15 Oct between 08:00 and 09:30 UTC, "roughly 90 minutes of downtime". These are the full Update 0.2.0 notes; values live in the owner documents, so this entry lists headlines only.

| Area | Headline change (0.2.0) | Owner document |
|------|-------------------------|----------------|
| Weapons | TCX-SPR [7.62x39mm], PP-19 Bizon [9x19mm], Evo-3 Ultra [.308 Win], M14 [.308 Win]; new optics, muzzle devices, magazines, bipods | weapons-catalogue |
| Gear | Molotov (impact plus damage over time; burns foliage; reduced by rain); IR Range Finder on batteries (about 80 s); Level 4 Helmet muffled audio, restricted field of view, fogs when sprinting; Medical Bag durability 100 to 150 | gadgets-armor-and-equipment |
| Vehicles | Wolf-110, Wolf-110 [M2 Browning], T-72B3, Flakpanzer Gepard; private inventories by default; Humvee handling reworked | vehicle-roster-and-prices |
| Buildables | MG Nest, Large Shelter, Wooden Step; build costs, drill rig, Talon and Mortar rebalance | fob-and-base-building |
| Weather | New rain preset; thunder synchronised across the server, masks footsteps; rain reduces spotting range and Molotov fire | maps-environment-foundation |
| Cosmetics | Eight Gold Market camos; Black & Gold AK camo removed from the Gold Market | season-2-announcements |
| Wager Vendor | "Not available at Season 2 launch. It will open later in Season 2"; not a permanent addition | season-2-announcements |
| Match flow | Team switching restrictions once a team is more than 10 points ahead; Forgive/Punish team-kill vote; Squad Intent UI; rebuy last loadout; server seeding rewards; pre-match entertainment; region-based ping limits | control-zone-and-match-flow, server-hosting-and-browser |
| Maps | All three team spawns on Bakurani moved and rebuilt | maps-environment-foundation |

| Progression | Role-track XP cut (level 10 35,000 to 25,000; level 20 250,000 to 111,500; level 50 1,500,000 to 1,150,000); unlocks reshuffled in every track | progression-unlock-tables |

| Controller | Aim Assist strength slider, bind changes, fixes | none |

- In-post update: the logistics streak values were first posted as base design values without the zone multiplier, then revised to the values players actually receive in the Control Zone [20].
- Preview versus final names: T-72 became T-72B3, Leopard became L2A6, Wolf-110 (Assault) became Wolf-110 [M2 Browning], TCX Spear became TCX-SPR, Super Heavy Helmet became Level 4 Helmet [19][20].
- The notes' "before" XP values for levels 25 to 50 (for example level 25: 365,000) differ from the 9 Sep changelog (325,000) [7][20]; the cause is not stated.
- Not mentioned in the notes: a progression wipe, cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, death-penalty rules, new named maps, RCON or ini settings, console or Linux statements, Season 3.

## 15 Oct 2026, Season 02 is now live (Official) [21]

Posted 09:59 UTC: "We have now released Update 0.2.0. Servers are back online." The post embeds a trailer and links to a patch notes address that is not in the snapshot; the 14 Oct post is cited here as the notes.

title: Season 02: Pre-Release Claims Scored Against Update 0.2.0
topic: What was said about Season 02 before launch, scored against the official Update 0.2.0 notes (14-15 Oct 2026)

text:
This document records what was claimed about Season 02 before launch and scores each claim against the official Update 0.2.0 text. The pre-release baseline was taken on 2026-10-08. The official outcome posts are the Season 02 Preview (9 Oct 2026) [18], the Season 02 Patch Notes (14 Oct 2026) [19] and the "Season 02 is now live" post (15 Oct 2026, 09:59 UTC), which says Update 0.2.0 was released and servers were back online [20]. Season 02 therefore started on the announced date, 15 October 2026 [1][20]. It deepens meta-release-foundation; the dated release list is in patch-history.

Scorecard result: of 29 pre-release claims, 12 are confirmed by the official notes, 3 are partly confirmed, 2 are contradicted, 10 are not mentioned in the notes and 2 are supported only by press. All five claims graded Official-confirmed before launch were confirmed. Of the 19 graded Rumour, 6 were confirmed, 2 partly confirmed, 2 contradicted, 8 not mentioned and 1 is press-only. The five Press-graded claims split: rain was confirmed, the rain preset wording partly, the wipe is press-only, and the cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion and Gold Bar persistence are not mentioned in the notes.

The notes do not mention a progression wipe, a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, a death-penalty rule change or a launch of the Black Market. Their absence from the notes is not proof that they did not happen; it means no official source in the snapshot states them. Later press (PCGamesN, 17 and 25 Oct) speaks of a Season 2 wipe or economy reset and of a Season 3 target; that is press only [22][23]. Confidence is Medium: outcomes rest on Primary posts, but the "not mentioned" and press-only verdicts rest on absence of text, and two verdicts rest on press.
title: Season 02: Pre-Release Claims Scored Against Update 0.2.0
topic: What was said about Season 02 before launch, scored against the official Update 0.2.0 notes (14-15 Oct 2026)

text:
- Official, 2026-10-15: Update 0.2.0 released, servers back online (post 09:59 UTC); maintenance was announced for 15 Oct 08:00 to 09:30 UTC, about 90 minutes of downtime [19][20].
- Confirmed by the notes (0.2.0): four new weapons (TCX-SPR, PP-19 Bizon, Evo-3 Ultra, M14), a Molotov, four vehicles (Wolf-110, Wolf-110 [M2 Browning], T-72B3, Flakpanzer Gepard), three buildables (MG Nest, Large Shelter, Wooden Step), a rain weather preset, IR Rangefinder batteries (about 80 s of use) and a role-track XP rework [19].
- Not mentioned in the notes: a progression wipe, a cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion, a conversion rate, Gold Bar persistence, the Black Market, new ammo types, the "honeypot" AK and a HammerGun [19].
- Contradicted by the notes: a 16:00 UTC launch time (the maintenance window was 08:00 to 09:30 UTC) and "grind not eased" (level 20 now needs 111,500 XP, down from 250,000, "less than half the playtime") [19].
- Wager Vendor: announced in the Preview as an experimental feature; the notes say it is not available at launch, will open later in Season 2 and is not a permanent addition [18][19].
- Faction experiment: Lonestar (the blue team) gets Season 2 only cash and XP bonuses; a 20% vendor discount goes to a team at least 40 points behind second place; Bakurani spawns moved [18][19].
- Preview names differ from the final notes (T-72 became T-72B3, Leopard became L2A6, Wolf-110 (Assault) became Wolf-110 [M2 Browning], TCX Spear became TCX-SPR, Super Heavy Helmet became Level 4 Helmet); this KB uses the final names [18][19].
- Press only: PCGamesN reported on 16 Oct that a blue-team bonus (5% cash, 2.5% XP) was removed and on 17 and 25 Oct that Season 3 may come early, around 12 Nov [21][22][23].
