Rows dated before 2026-10-09 are the pre-release record, kept as history. Their outcome is scored in the next section.

## Store-page roadmap (Primary, distinct from Season 02)

The live Steam store page, Early Access section (capture 2026-10-08), is a Primary statement of the longer roadmap. It is not dated to any season [12]:

| Topic | Page wording (summary) | Source |
|-------|------------------------|--------|
| Content breadth | More maps, weapons, vehicles and gameplay variety | [12] |
| Stated primary focus | "Deeper reasons to play beyond individual matches": more in-depth progression systems, a stronger seasonal meta game, and systems rewarding combat, support or logistics | [12] |
| Gameplay additions | New vehicle types including fighter jets; expanded weapon categories; additional objective variations | [12] |
| Ongoing priority | Balance, performance and stability | [12] |
| Early Access duration | "around 1 to 2 years"; the page says the exact duration may change | [12] |
| Pricing | Priced lower during Early Access, higher at full release; the price "may" rise closer to full release; no figure given | [12] |
| Community | "Run seasonal updates that respond directly to player behaviour" (community involvement section) | [12] |

The page says nothing specific about Season 02, its date, a progression wipe or cash converting to Gold Bars [12]. "Seasonal meta game" and "seasonal updates" are general intentions; they do not confirm any Season 02 claim in the register below. This list is a plan, not a delivery schedule.

## Roadmap to 1.0

The roadmap post of 7 Apr 2026 states that the metagame is "our frontend experience that will enable you to continue earning, progressing and adding value to your account even when not in a match" [2]. The post lists two named systems, the Black Market & Vault and the Player Skills & Challenge System, with no season attached [2]. The post's text does not mention seasons, a wipe, or a conversion of cash to Gold Bars; third parties attribute those to the video embedded in it (see the scorecard) [2][15]. No official 1.0 date or full-release price appears in the Steam posts in the snapshot; the store page gives an Early Access duration of "around 1 to 2 years" [12]. A podcast summary on a conflicted site quotes a developer as saying 1.0 is "roughly 23 months out" [17]; that is within the store page's range but is player-reported only.

## Terminology conflict

Official text uses "GOLD MARKET" for the cosmetic store that Gold Bars buy from (18 Feb 2026) [8] and "The Black Market & Vault" for a planned metagame feature (7 Apr 2026) [2]. Dexerto says Gold Bars buy "exclusive cosmetics from the Black Market" [16]. Whether these are one store or two is not resolved by any official source.

## Season 02 scorecard: pre-release claims against Update 0.2.0

text:
This document records what a read-only inspection of one installed copy of the WARDOGS Windows client shows, observed on 2026-10-30. It reads only file names, sizes, dates, executable version resources and the Steam app manifest. It does not unpack, decompile, or modify any game data, and it does not read saved settings or crash reports [1].

The install is the Season 02 / Update 0.2.0 build. Steam's manifest records build id 25937608, last updated 2026-10-15 09:57 UTC, about two minutes before BULKHEAD's "Season 02 is now live" post of 2026-10-15 09:59 UTC [1][3]. The client executable's version string is `++Wardogs+Live-CL-516586` [1]. The install occupies 48,905,446,067 bytes (about 48.9 GB, 45.5 GiB), consistent with the store page's "50 GB available space" requirement [1][2].

Confidence is Medium: the observations are first-hand and exact, but they come from a single machine, they show what is present rather than what is enabled, and the interpretations are labelled as inference.

text:
## Third-party components found

Presence of a component means its files ship with the game. It does not show that the feature is enabled or how it is used [1].

| Component | Where | Reading |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| NVIDIA DLSS and Streamline | `Plugins/External/Nvidia` | upscaling / frame generation support files |
| AMD FSR | `Plugins/External/FSR` | upscaling support files |
| Intel XeSS | `Plugins/External/XeSS` | upscaling support files |
| Sentry | `Plugins/External/Sentry`, `.sentry-native` | crash reporting runtime |
| Vivox | `Plugins/Online/VivoxCore` (`vivoxsdk.dll`) | voice communication SDK |
| atmoky TrueSpatial | `Binaries/Win64/atmokyTrueSpatial.dll` | spatial audio middleware |
| Direct3D 12 | `Binaries/Win64/D3D12` (`D3D12Core.dll`, `d3d12SDKLayers.dll`) | a bundled Direct3D 12 runtime folder |
| Bink video | `Content/Binks` (`.bk2`) | pre-rendered videos |

Engine third-party folders (CEF3, MsQuic, Steamworks, Ogg, Vorbis and others) and `EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll` also exist under `Engine`. Assessment: these are likely engine defaults rather than evidence of game features; Confidence Low; no use was observed [1].

Cross-checks against other documents: the Vivox SDK is consistent with the store page's proximity and local voice chat claims [2]; the upscaler plugins are consistent with the "Upscaled" notes in the store requirements [2]. The store page lists no DirectX version [2]; the bundled Direct3D 12 folder suggests, but does not prove, a Direct3D 12 renderer (Confidence Low).

## Content packaging

`Wardogs/Content/Paks` holds 66 files in 17 groups of `.pak`/`.ucas`/`.utoc`/`.sig` files, named `pakchunk<N>-WindowsClient` for N = 0, 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 23, 30, 50, 51, 52, plus `pakchunk10optional` and the `global` pair [1]. The largest are pakchunk51 (about 11.1 GB), pakchunk52 (about 9.3 GB), pakchunk50 (about 8.1 GB) and pakchunk0 (about 5.6 GB with its `.pak`) [1]. What each chunk contains was not examined.

`Content/Binks` holds videos including the tutorial clips, the three faction end-game videos (named for Lonestar, Manticore and Valkyra), and a front-end video named `UI_FrontendVideo_S02` of about 539 MB [1]. Assessment: the "S02" file name suggests the home-screen video was replaced for Season 02; Confidence Low; inferred from the name alone.

## How to reproduce

Any owner can repeat the checks without special tools: read `steamapps/appmanifest_1867240.acf` in their Steam library for `buildid`, `LastUpdated` and `SizeOnDisk`; right-click `WardogsClient-Win64-Shipping.exe`, then Properties, then Details for the version string; list the folders named above [1].

text:
This depth document goes below the admin summary in technical-servers-foundation: the RCON HTTP API, the `ServerSettings.ini` keys, the 0.1.2 hardening, the 2 October hotfix, third-party admin tooling and moderation. It is verified against Season 02, Update 0.2.0 (released 15 Oct 2026) for official statements, with the unofficial RCON reference still dating from before 0.1.2.

Revision 1.2.0 (30 Oct 2026): the 0.2.0 patch notes (14 Oct 2026) mention no RCON or ini change; the only server-admin items are that community admins "will be able to configure their own ping limits", a penalty for community hosts exploiting the faction bonus, and "Server stability & security improvements" with no detail [6]. The "now live" post (15 Oct) only confirms release and servers back online [7]. RCON and ini details therefore remain unconfirmed.

Revision 1.1.0 re-checks the topic against the full official Steam posts. The official text says four things about RCON and server admin, all in the 0.1.2 post of 30 Sep 2026 under "Community Servers (for Server Admins)": a daily restart time in UTC, "RCON AllowedHosts: you can now set this to restrict who can access RCON", capped RCON message and broadcast lengths, and a Standard default response detail with config responses that no longer expose server internals [1]. It also says `ServerImageURL` "is now checked when the config loads" [1]. The official posts give no syntax, default or failure behaviour for any of these, and none of the other official posts read mentions RCON or AllowedHosts [2][3][4][5].

The 2 October security hotfix post says only that it addresses "minor security and stability issues affecting some players"; its text does not mention RCON [2]. Everything else (port, auth, endpoints, ini keys and defaults, the CL-501228 removals) still comes from an unofficial fan reference [10] and a tracker guide written by a tool vendor [11].

Confidence stays Low. The official text confirms the existence of the 0.1.2 admin changes but nothing about how the interface works, and the main reference was last updated before 0.1.2 shipped.

text:
- Official: Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) lets server admins set "RCON AllowedHosts" to "restrict who can access RCON". The post gives no format, default or example [1].
- Official: 0.1.2 also caps RCON message and broadcast lengths (no values given) and makes Standard the default RCON response detail "instead of Full" [1].
- Official: the 2 Oct hotfix post links to "minor security and stability issues affecting some players" and does not mention RCON [2].
- Official (Update 0.2.0, 14-15 Oct 2026): community admins can configure their own ping limits; the notes give no setting name, ini key or RCON endpoint for it. They also say community hosts seen exploiting the faction bonus will be punished and list "Server stability & security improvements" without detail. The notes do not mention RCON or AllowedHosts [6][7].
- Unofficial: the RCON interface is reported to be a versioned HTTP/JSON API (`/v1`), default port 7776, off by default, authenticated by a single shared bearer token with no read-only role (player-reported, reference v0.39 of 2026-09-21) [10][11].
- The fan reference does not mention AllowedHosts, because it predates 0.1.2; its key defaults may therefore be stale [10].
- Eight write endpoints were reported removed in build CL-501228 (14 Sep 2026) and replaced by edits to the config document. No official post says so; the official 0.11 post of the same date does not mention RCON [3][10].
- The listed `MaxPlayers` default of 128 is unexplained: the game is a 100-player format and no source gives a reason for 128 (see Detail and Open Questions) [10].
- Warcon and BattleMetrics are the named third-party panels; Warcon bans work only while the panel runs [11][12].

text:
- **RCON:** remote administration of a running server. Here it is an HTTP/JSON API, not a Source-style socket protocol [11]. The official posts use the term without defining it [1].
- **Config document:** the whole `ServerSettings.ini` text as read and replaced through `/v1/config` [10].
- **Revision:** a token returned with the config, sent back in `If-Match` to avoid overwriting newer edits [10].

text:
State at Season 02 / Update 0.2.0 (official posts through 2026-10-15; none seen in the 2026-10-30 snapshot after that). The 0.1.2 and earlier items below are dated history, checked 2026-10-08.

- Update 0.2.0 patch notes (14 Oct 2026 14:59 UTC), maintenance 08:00 to 09:30 UTC on 15 Oct: "Community Server admins will be able to configure their own ping limits, allowing for cross regional play (or more stringent rules) if desired"; "Community server hosts being seen to exploit the faction bonus will be punished"; "Server stability & security improvements" [6]. Release confirmed 15 Oct 2026 09:59 UTC [7]. Nothing on RCON, AllowedHosts, restart time or ini keys; whether 0.1.2 admin settings changed is not stated.

- No official RCON or server-settings documentation was found. The vendor guide says so directly (guide dated 2026-09-14, PR) [11]. A fan site relaying a hosting-policy thread (checked 2026-09-01, PR) says Bulkhead was developing an RCON tool and that moderation details were unpublished at that time [13].
- Official, 0.1.2 post (30 Sep 2026, 06:57 UTC), section "Community Servers (for Server Admins)", quoted in full (O) [1]:
  - "Scheduled restarts: you can now set a daily restart time (UTC)."
  - "RCON AllowedHosts: you can now set this to restrict who can access RCON."
  - "RCON message and broadcast lengths are now capped."
  - "RCON now defaults to Standard response detail instead of Full, and config responses no longer expose server internals."
  - "ServerImageURL is now checked when the config loads."
- The same post lists, under "Server Stability Improvements", "Various server stability hotfixes" and "Increased server security to prevent exploitation", without saying whether these touch RCON [1]. Its summary says the update is aimed at thwarting XP and cash exploits "and security issues seen since the early access launch" [1].
- What the 0.1.2 post does not say: the AllowedHosts value format, wildcard support, default or failure behaviour; the cap values; what "Full" and "Standard" include; how to set the restart time [1].
- Also in 0.1.2: revive action validity checks are "now fully server authoritative" (an exploit fix, not RCON) [1].
- Security and Stability Hotfix: the Steam post is stamped 00:13 UTC on 2 Oct 2026 and announces a hotfix "planned for tomorrow, Friday 2nd, at 08:00 UTC, to address minor security and stability issues affecting some players", with "Expected downtime is one hour." Its text does not link the fix to RCON, AllowedHosts or server administration, and gives no other detail (O) [2]. A press outlet adds that it carried no gameplay, balance or UI changes (S) [8].
- Official moderation statements that apply to players rather than admins: the 0.11 post (12 Sep 2026) sets out penalties for economy abuse (timed bans with cash and XP reset, permanent bans for tutorialising exploits or XP farming) and says the studio tracks "every server you enter" [3]. The 0.1.2 post says leniency for first-time economy exploiters "is now over" [1]. The Season 1 changelog adds that cheater bans are announced in-server when match termination is turned off and that reports are weighted [5]. None of these describes admin-side ban tooling.
- The 8 Sep 2026 post says use the in-game report function on official servers and, for "the ultimate protection", play on community-hosted servers "where admins can instantly ban bad actors". It names three Approved Hosting Partners: QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM [4]. It does not mention RCON.
- The 0.11 post (12 Sep 2026) is about the server browser: Community Server IDs persist between matches and restarts, server names are re-ordered and restricted. It does not mention RCON, AllowedHosts or build CL-501228 [3].

text:
## Transport and authentication (PR, reference v0.39, 2026-09-21) [10]

None of this table is stated in an official post.

| Item | Reported value |
|------|----------------|
| Base URL | `http://<host>:<port>/v1/` |
| Default port | 7776, settable in config or with `-RCONPort=` |
| Transport | Plain HTTP; HTTPS refuses the connection |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>` on every request |
| Roles | One token, full read and write, no read-only key |
| Body format | JSON; the two config-document endpoints use `text/plain` |
| Errors | Non-2xx with `{error:{code,message}}`; 412 stale revision, 422 rejected value, 404 removed route |
| Rate limit | None published |

Conflict: the vendor guide says any listener bound beyond loopback "must use TLS" and that hosts provide an https address [11], while the fan reference says an earlier claim that a network listener needs a certificate was corrected and HTTPS is refused [10]. Both are player-reported and neither is confirmed by an official post. Assessment (confidence Low): terminate TLS in a reverse proxy or use a tunnel rather than expecting the game to do it.

## Endpoints (PR) [10]

| Group | Reported routes |
|-------|-----------------|
| Read | status, players, capabilities, bans, reserved-slots, audit (limit 1-500, default 50), config, rotation, catalog (maps, lightings, experiences, alternators), sponsor, server-id, health |
| Player writes | kick (reason), kill, message, faction change (only if listed in capabilities) |
| Match writes | broadcast, map change, match end, match restart, lighting |
| Bans | POST ban (steamId, optional reason), DELETE ban |
| Config | validate (dry run), PUT replace with `If-Match`, optional `force=true`, `fullApply=true` |

The vendor guide counts "around 35 endpoints" [11]. Clients should read `GET /v1/capabilities` rather than assume a route exists [10]. The official posts confirm that message and broadcast operations exist only indirectly, through "RCON message and broadcast lengths are now capped" [1].

## Config document semantics (PR) [10]

- `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document; omitted sections are removed.
- Every value is revalidated on each apply; one bad value blocks all edits, and a non-empty `errors` array means nothing was applied.
- Array keys follow Unreal operators: `!Key=ClearArray` empties, `.Key=value` appends.
- Ban, reserve and rotation commands edit and persist back to the ini. Only whitelisted sections and keys are honoured.

## ServerSettings.ini keys (PR; defaults as listed by the fan reference, not stated officially, not verified in-game) [10]

Only the existence of `ServerImageURL` as a config key with load-time checking is supported by an official post [1]. All other rows are player-reported.

| Section | Key | Listed default | Applies |
|---------|-----|----------------|---------|
| WDRCONSettings | `bEnabled` | listener off by default; the key list shows `true` (inconsistent) | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `BindAddress` | 127.0.0.1 (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `Port` | 7776 | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `Password`, `PasswordHash` | empty password auto-generates to `Saved/RCON/ADMIN-PASSWORD.txt`; hash from `-GenerateRCONHash=` takes precedence | startup |
| WDGameSession | `ServerName` | none | immediately |
| WDGameSession | `ServerPassword` | empty (open) | next restart |
| WDGameSession | `ServerMin/MaxPlayerCash`, `ServerMin/MaxPlayerLevel` | 0 (no limit) | next restart |
| WDGameSession | `ServerImageURL` | none; 1024x256 PNG or JPEG on an allow-list | pending |
| WDGameSession | `MaxReservedSlots` | 20 | immediately |
| WDGameSession | `DefaultReservedPlayerIds`, `DefaultBannedPlayerIds` | one SteamID64 per line | n/a |
| Engine.GameSession | `MaxPlayers` | 128, clamped by a developer-set min and max | immediately |
| PreMatch PlayerCount | `MinimumRequiredPlayers` | 60 | next match |
| KOTH | `ScorePeriod` | 24 s, range 18-30 | next match |
| WDGameStateSession | `bLockOverpopulatedTeamsConfig`, `OverpopulatedTeamThresholdConfig` | true, 2 | next match |
| MapRotationSettings | `bEnabled`, `RotationMode`, `+RotationEntries` | true, Ordered (or Random) | immediately |

The reference states the RCON listener is off by default yet lists `bEnabled` as `true`; this inconsistency is unresolved, so treat the true default as unknown [10]. No `AllowedHosts` key name, section or default appears in any source: the official post names the setting only as "RCON AllowedHosts" in prose [1].

## MaxPlayers 128 versus a 100-player game

- The game format is 100 players in three teams (Steam page, via the foundation document). No official post read gives a server `MaxPlayers` value, and a web search of hosting wikis found no source for 128; those pages were not opened and are not relied on.
- The reference says the value is "clamped by a developer-set min and max" [10]. So 128 is at most a stored default, and the effective cap could be lower.
- Assessment (confidence Low): 128 is probably an engine-level or template default, not a supported player count. This is inference. Do not set it above 100 expecting more players, and confirm the clamp with your host.

## Build CL-501228 removals (PR, build dated 2026-09-14) [10]

Removed routes (now 404 on current builds, still served by older builds): `PATCH /v1/settings`, `POST` and `DELETE /v1/reserved-slots`, `POST` and `DELETE /v1/rotation/entries`, `POST /v1/rotation/entries/{i}/move`, `POST /v1/rotation/save`, `PUT /v1/sponsor`. The functions moved to config keys: `DefaultReservedPlayerIds`, `RotationEntries` with `bEnabled` and `RotationMode`, `ScorePeriod`, `ServerImageURL`. The build date coincides with the maintenance window of patch 0.11 (announced for 14 Sep 2026) [3], but the 0.11 post does not mention RCON or these removals, so no source ties the two explicitly.

## Hardening in 0.1.2 and the hotfix

| Change | Class | Note |
|--------|-------|------|
| "RCON AllowedHosts: you can now set this to restrict who can access RCON" | O [1] | Value format, wildcard and default are not stated in any source read |
| RCON message and broadcast lengths capped | O [1] | Cap values not published |
| Standard response detail by default "instead of Full" | O [1] | Whether Full is still selectable is not documented |
| Config responses no longer expose server internals | O [1] | Which fields were hidden is not documented |
| `ServerImageURL` checked when the config loads | O [1] | Consistent with the reference's allow-list note [10], which is not official |
| Scheduled daily restart time (UTC) | O [1] | How to set it is not documented |
| "Increased server security to prevent exploitation" | O [1] | Does not say RCON |
| Server-authoritative revive checks | O [1] | Gameplay exploit fix, not RCON |
| 2 Oct hotfix: "minor security and stability issues affecting some players" | O [2] | Text does not link to RCON; contents undisclosed |

## Admin tooling and moderation

- **Warcon** (PR, repository page): self-hosted panel (Bun, SvelteKit, Postgres, Docker Compose), MIT code, with map imagery excluded from the licence and owned by Bulkhead. Per-server roles viewer, operator and admin; stored RCON passwords encrypted (AES-GCM); audit log exportable to CSV or JSON; automation triggers. No game version is stated and commit dates were not visible [12]. The page says the protocol was reverse-engineered, so it can break when builds change [12].
- **Warcon bans** are enforced by the panel's worker, not the game: a banned player is removed when seen, and bans only hold while Warcon runs and reaches the server. Bans made outside the panel appear as "local" [12].
- **BattleMetrics** is reported to support WARDOGS RCON, paid after a free tier, and it stores your RCON password [11]. The vendor guide is by Warcon's publisher, so it is promotional [11].
- **Native bans:** by Steam ID, persisted in the ban list and `DefaultBannedPlayerIds` [10][11]. Officially, only the 8 Sep statement that community admins "can instantly ban bad actors" supports the existence of admin-side bans [4].

text:
- Treat the RCON password as full control. Keep it off the public internet: loopback or a VPN, SSH tunnel or TLS proxy [10][11], and set AllowedHosts. The setting exists officially [1]; its exact syntax is unverified.
- Hosting reality: server code is reportedly not released for self-hosting and RCON access depends on the host [11][13]. The official hosting route named on 8 Sep is the three Approved Hosting Partners [4]. Ask the host whether you can edit the ini, whether bans and rotation survive restarts, and whether third-party panels are allowed [11].
- Hosted third-party consoles hold full-access credentials once you give them the password [11].
- Scripts written against the fan reference should call `/v1/capabilities` first and handle 404, 412 and 422 [10].
- Assessment (confidence Low): the fan reference is stale-risk after 0.1.2 (the official post says default response detail and config reply contents changed), so re-diff your tooling against a live server after each patch.

text:
This depth document extends the technical-servers-foundation with how WARDOGS servers are obtained and found: the hosts-only model, the approved hosts, the Official and Community split introduced in patch 0.11, regions, browser behaviour, slot counts, restart handling and prices. Version 1.2.0 adds Season 02, Update 0.2.0 (patch notes 14 Oct 2026, released 15 Oct 2026) [7][8]. Version 1.1.0 had been revised against the full official Steam posts (snapshot of 8 Oct 2026), which were unreadable when version 1.0.0 was written from fan relays; its Season 1 / 0.1.2 content is kept as dated history. Update 0.2.0 added region-based ping limits with automatic kicks on Official servers, admin-configurable limits on community servers, ping tags and filters in the browser, server seeding rewards and a penalty for community hosts exploiting the faction bonus [7].

Headline findings: the studio's own 8 September 2026 post names three Approved Hosting Partners, QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM, and says Community Hosted Servers could be pre-ordered through them ahead of the 10 September launch [1]. That settles the two-versus-three conflict: the two-host figure was a fan-site statement dated 1 September [12]. The patch 0.11 browser changes and the 0.1.2 Deploy flow, restored Official filters and daily restart time are now confirmed from the official posts [2][3]. What remains unofficial is the self-hosting and server-code position, prices, slot tiers, regions and any default restart interval. The 12-hour versus 24-hour restart conflict is still unresolved: the official post states only that admins can set a daily restart time in UTC [3].

Confidence is Medium. The hosting model, host names, browser split and restart mechanism rest on official posts; prices, slot sizes, regions and the server-code claim rest on fan sites and commercial pages and are labelled player-reported throughout.

text:
- Official (8 Sep 2026): there are three Approved Hosting Partners, QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM, and Community Hosted Servers could be pre-ordered through them ahead of Early Access on 10 Sep [1].
- Official: community-hosted servers are where "admins can instantly ban bad actors"; the studio's advice on official servers is to use the in-game report function [1].
- Official (Update 0.2.0, notes 14 Oct 2026): Official servers enforce region-based maximum ping limits; players who consistently exceed the limit over a sustained period are kicked and cannot rejoin that server until the next map transition; community admins can set their own limits; the browser has maximum-ping tags and filters. The notes call the initial values "quite lenient" and give none [7].
- Official (0.2.0): players who join and populate empty servers earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins; community hosts "seen to exploit the faction bonus will be punished" (penalty not stated) [7].
- Press only: PCGamesN (27 Oct 2026) reports two new server hosts, GG Host and 1of1 Servers; no official post in the 2026-10-30 snapshot confirms it, so the approved list stays at three officially [11].
- Self-hosting is reportedly not offered: the developer is said not to release server code (fan-site relay; player-reported). No official post read states this [12][13].
- Official (patch 0.11, 14 Sep 2026): the browser split into Community and Official; Official lost its filters because there are no Official modified game modes; Community gained text search and filter reliability fixes; Show Empty/Full was added to the quick bar [2].
- Official: Community Server IDs persist across matches and restarts, are unique, and are longer for security [2].
- Official (0.1.2, 30 Sep 2026): admins can set a daily restart time in UTC; advanced filters returned to the Official list; the Deploy flow offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level [3]. No official post gives a built-in 12 h or 24 h interval.
- Listed monthly prices on provider pages (checked 13 Sep 2026): QONZER GBP 49.95 to 69.95, BisectHosting from USD 71.99, xREALM from EUR 59.99; smallest size sold is 60 slots. Player-reported compilation; no official price [13].
- No official region list exists; fan and tracker sources disagree on labels [14][15]. The only official regional statement is increased capacity in Asia [2].

text:
Statements at Season 02 / Update 0.2.0 unless dated otherwise (official posts through 2026-10-15; none seen in the 2026-10-30 snapshot after that). Items from earlier checks keep their dates.

- **Ping limits (0.2.0).** Official servers enforce region-dependent maximum pings; sustained excess causes an automatic kick (short spikes and server-side lag spikes are excluded) and a rejoin block on that server until the next map transition [7]. Community admins configure their own limits, allowing cross-regional play or stricter rules [7]. The browser shows maximum-ping tags and filters [7]. Values are not published.
- **Seeding (0.2.0).** Rewards and a vendor discount for players who populate empty servers, paid once the match begins; amounts not stated [7]. See control-zone-and-match-flow.
- **Release.** Maintenance 08:00 to 09:30 UTC on 15 Oct 2026 (about 90 minutes estimated), then Update 0.2.0 released and servers back online [7][8].

- **Approved hosts.** Three Approved Hosting Partners: QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM (official, 8 Sep 2026) [1]. A tracker (updated 14 Sep 2026) also says three exist and agrees [14].
- **Hosting model.** Community servers are bought through those partners [1]. That self-hosting is unavailable and that the developer withholds server code is player-reported only (fan site, evidence dated 1 Sep 2026) [12]; a second guide says no other host has access to the server code [13].
- **Browser.** Community and Official lists since 14 Sep 2026 [2]. The 0.1.2 Deploy flow offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level, and advanced filters are back on the Official list [3].
- **Restart.** Admins can set a daily restart time in UTC (official, 0.1.2) [3]; BisectHosting repeats this [9].
- **Regions.** The region selector exists and shows how many regions are selected [3]. No official region list was found; a tracker lists seven regions it tracks (see Detail) [14].

text:
## Resolving the host count (2 versus 3)

| Date of evidence | Claim | Source | Class |
|------------------|-------|--------|-------|
| 1 Sep 2026 | Two hosts passed launch standards, names unpublished, more in the pipeline | [12] | Fan site |
| 7 Sep 2026 | Studio names QONZER and BisectHosting (relayed) | [13] | Fan guide, unconfirmed |
| 8 Sep 2026 | Three Approved Hosting Partners named: QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM | [1] | Official |
| 14 Sep 2026 | "Only the three approved hosts run WARDOGS servers" | [14] | Tracker |

Assessment: confirmed. The conflict was stale evidence, not disagreement, and the official post names the same three the fan guide listed. Confidence High on the three names, resting on [1]. The fan guide's claim that the first two were named on 7 Sep and xREALM added on 8 Sep is not supported by the official post, which names all three together; no 7 Sep post is in the snapshot, so the stepwise dating stays unconfirmed [13]. Other sellers (XGamingServer, Survival Servers, LOW.MS, Supercraft) advertise WARDOGS hosting but are not on the official list; XGamingServer itself says it is "onboarding" through partners and does not claim approval [16][17]. Treat such pages as pre-approval marketing.

## Official versus Community (patch 0.11, 14 Sep 2026) [2]

| Aspect | Official | Community |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Operator | Bulkhead | Approved host customer |
| Filters | Removed in 0.11 (no Official modified modes); advanced filters added back in 0.1.2 [3] | Reliability improved, text search added |
| Quick bar | Show Empty/Full added to the browser quick bar (post does not split by list) | Same |
| Server ID | Not stated | Persistent, longer, unique, joinable by ID |
| Naming | Names sorted alphabetically regardless of special characters and numbers; no repeated spaces | Same |

The post frames the change as favouring community servers: it admits Community Servers "have been underserved" and that the studio rushed its Community Server strategy [2]. The studio notes that matchmaking would suit a game of this size but that it does not want community admins and hosts to suffer, hence the two browsers [2]. The Host button was updated to direct to the correct location [2]. PlayDay's press summary matches the official text [10].

Planned and not shipped per the 0.11 post: community server favouriting, tiered priority queues for Community servers, Message of the Day prompt, improved warmup activities, disabling AFK kicking during seeding, and team switching controls [2]. A one-week 5 percent End of Match cash bonus on Community servers ran from 14 Sep and has ended [2].

## Browser behaviour

- Official: 0.1.2 shows your place in the queue after clicking Join, no longer truncates long server names (hover shows the full name), and adds gamepad support on the Deploy screen [3].
- Region is picked via Deploy, Server Browser, Region, tick regions, Confirm (player-reported guide) [15]. The official 0.1.2 note says only that region select now shows how many regions are selected [3].
- Ticking several regions has been reported to return an empty list; guides advise selecting one and clearing persisted search text (player-reported) [13][15]. A fan site calls the one-region rule a temporary August Beta workaround, not a confirmed Early Access rule [12].
- Official: Asian capacity was increased in 0.11; no slot or per-region figures were published [2].

## Regions

| Source | Regions named | Class |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| Official 12 Sep post | "The Asian region" capacity increase only; no list | Primary [2] |
| Tracker, 14 Sep 2026 | Europe, North America East, North America Central, North America West, Oceania, Asia, South America | Player-reported [14] |
| Guide screenshot caption | Europe, North America, South America, Asia, with ping values | Player-reported [15] |
| Hosting vendor | Datacentres in East/West USA, Europe (Germany), Oceania, Singapore | Commercial [16] |

No official region list was found; labels disagree. Oceania as a browser region is unconfirmed [12][15]. The time-zone table in the 12 Sep post is a maintenance schedule, not a region list [2].

## Slots and capacity

No official post read states slot counts for community servers. Matches are 100 players across three teams per the foundation. Hosts sell by different units: xREALM 60, 80 or 100 player packages; QONZER sells by CPU threads (8, 10 or 12) and says it does not limit slots; the smallest size sold anywhere is 60 slots (player-reported compilation, 13 Sep 2026) [13]. The unofficial config reference lists `MaxPlayers` default 128, "clamped by a developer-set min/max" [18].

## Costs (provider pages as compiled 13 Sep 2026; verify before buying; no official price) [13]

| Host | Price shown | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| QONZER | GBP 49.95, 59.95, 69.95 per month | 5% quarterly, 10% semi-annual, 15% annual prepay discounts |
| BisectHosting | from USD 71.99 per month | per-tier prices not visible |
| xREALM | from EUR 59.99 per month | 60/80/100 slots |

Roundups conflict with these figures [13]. Pre-approval pages quote far lower numbers (for example XGamingServer USD 24.50 to 42.00 and a Supercraft reservation page USD 17.99 to 39.99), marked "coming soon" or reservation-only [16][17]; they are not approved-host prices.

## Restart cycles (12 h versus 24 h)

- Official: "Scheduled restarts: you can now set a daily restart time (UTC)" for community server admins, in 0.1.2 [3]. This is a once-per-day schedule, which fits "24 h", but the post states no default or minimum interval.
- Not documented: the unofficial config reference lists no scheduled-restart key, only on-demand `POST /v1/match/restart`; some session keys apply only at next restart [18].
- The 12 h figure was not found in any official post or any source I could open. The foundation's statement that host guides disagree remains unverified. Persistent IDs mean a restart no longer changes a server's identity [2].
- Whole-service maintenance is a separate matter: official one-hour windows at 08:00 UTC on 14 Sep, 30 Sep and 2 Oct [2][3][4].

## How a prospective admin gets a server

1. Choose one of the three Approved Hosting Partners (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM) [1]. 2. The in-game Host button links to the hosting page [2][6]. 3. Check slots, region, billing term and refund terms on the host's own page (player-reported advice) [12]. 4. RCON was described in August as in development, with day-one controls limited to maps and modes [12]; RCON additions including AllowedHosts arrived in 0.1.2 [3] (see rcon-and-server-admin).

text:
This depth document goes beyond the specification table in technical-servers-foundation. It collects what is officially documented about client performance and stability in WARDOGS (Steam app 1867240): the Steam store requirements as shown on the live store page (live capture 2026-10-08) and returned by the store API in the US and GB storefronts, what the official posts say about upscaling and frame generation, the Linux and Proton position, the WD-L020 crash and its Windows 11 KB5124010 link, and a post-by-post list of performance and crash fixes through the 2 October 2026 hotfixes [1][2][3][4][5][6][7]. Version 1.2.0 adds Update 0.2.0 (patch notes 14 Oct 2026, released 15 Oct 2026): the requirements in the 2026-10-30 store data (US storefront) are unchanged from the 2026-10-08 reading [1][11][12].

Headline facts: the store lists a 50 GB install, 16 GB RAM and a 1080p Low 60 fps (upscaled) minimum, lists Windows only, and carries no DirectX, VRAM or storage-type line [1]. Update 0.1.2 (30 September 2026) officially names a "Windows 11 'WD-L020' Crash Error Fix" and attributes the crashes to Windows 11 update KB5124010 [5]. The only official upscaling or frame generation wording is a DLSS Frame Generation toggle fix in the Season 1 changelog [2]. The store page states "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat: Elytra" and "STEAM DECK COMPATIBILITY: Unsupported" [1]; the developers' own posts say nothing about Linux, Proton or Steam Deck [10].

Confidence is Medium overall. The specification table, anti-cheat disclosure, Steam Deck label and language list are direct readings of the live store page and are rated High; the Linux and Proton timeline rests on one press article and the settings guidance is player-reported.

text:
## Specification wording (live Steam store page, live capture 2026-10-08; matches store API US and GB) [1]

Confidence: High. The live page lines match the storefront payloads, which are identical for US and GB.

| Item | Minimum | Recommended |
|------|---------|-------------|
| Architecture | 64-bit processor and operating system | 64-bit processor and operating system |
| OS | Windows 10 | Windows 11 |
| CPU | Intel Core i5 8600, AMD Ryzen 5 3500 | Intel Core i7 12700k, AMD Ryzen 7 5700x |
| RAM | 16 GB | 16 GB |
| GPU | Nvidia GTX 1660, Radeon RX 590 | Nvidia RTX 3070, AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT |
| Storage | 50 GB available space | 50 GB available space |
| Network | Broadband Internet connection | Broadband Internet connection |
| ADDITIONAL NOTES | 1080p Low @ 60fps (Upscaled) | 1440p Medium @ 70fps+ (Native) or 4k Medium @ 60fps+ (Upscaled) |
| DirectX | Not listed | Not listed |

Gaps in the official figures: no VRAM, no storage type (SSD or HDD), and no DirectX or Vulkan statement [1]. The minimum tier pairs a GTX 1660 class GPU with an "Upscaled" target, so players near the minimum should expect to rely on an upscaler. The live page confirms upscaling is part of both the minimum target and the 4K recommended target, while the 1440p recommended target is stated as Native; no upscaling technology is named [1]. Assessment: that reading is an inference from the note wording, Confidence Medium, resting on [1].

Other store data: 14 supported languages. The page shows English with interface, full audio and subtitles, and French, Italian, German and Spanish - Spain with interface and subtitles; the full list in the store data is English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Polish, Turkish and Ukrainian; accessibility tags include Camera Comfort and Custom Volume Controls [1]. The page also shows Steam Achievements: 10 [1].

## Graphics and upscaling settings

- **Documented officially:** the Season 1 changelog says DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without restarting and the render target pool is configurable; shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores rather than being switched off entirely; shadow cache refreshes were reduced, which cuts hitching when taking control of a character; dropped items no longer affect navigation, "which claws back a little performance"; a legacy graphics dependency was removed [2].
- **Official intent:** a 16 Jul 2026 devlog post states that performance "has been a priority for the entire team since day one", that the game was optimised "across a wide range of hardware" and that graphics options let players tune it to their PC; it gives no figures [8].
- **Not documented in the sources read:** an FSR or XeSS option list, DLSS quality modes, or a Reflex entry. No official post mentions FSR, XeSS, Reflex or VRAM [2][5].
- **Player-reported settings guide** (allthings.how, "Updated Sep 12, 2026"): lists an Overall Quality Custom profile; Global Illumination as the biggest single gain at roughly 20 percent on average; Shadows, Reflections, Shading, Post-Processing and Particle Spawn Rate at Low; Texture Streaming reduced first on VRAM warnings; DLSS on RTX cards and FSR on others, with Quality as the usual balance; Nvidia Reflex and a frame limit matching refresh rate [14]. These are one site's recommendations, not developer guidance, and the figure is not independently measured. Treat all settings advice as player-reported.

## Linux, Steam Deck and Proton

| Date | Statement | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 2026-10-08 | Live store page: "STEAM DECK COMPATIBILITY: Unsupported" (official Steam label) | [1] |
| 2026-10-08 | Store API: platforms Windows true, Mac false, Linux false; Linux requirements empty | [1] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | Developers "cannot commit to having Linux support for our Early Access launch"; still working on Proton compatibility (press report) | [13] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | An earlier community-manager Discord post implying support was called a communication mistake; earlier Linux functionality in tests was accidental (press report) | [13] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | Buyers who expected Proton support on 10 Sep were told to refund (press report) | [13] |

Steam Deck is officially labelled Unsupported on the store page [1]. The Steam news posts in the snapshot (official posts, February to 2 October 2026) contain no mention of Linux, Proton or Steam Deck, so the Linux and Proton timeline above, given as context, rests on the GamingOnLinux report [13].

## Anti-cheat disclosure

- Fact: the live Steam store page states "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat: Elytra" and "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA: WARDOGS EULA" (live capture 2026-10-08). The storefront API JSON omits these fields, so the page capture is the evidence [1].
- The developers' 8 Sep 2026 post says "There's a rule in game development: you don't talk about anti-cheat" and points players to the in-game report function and community-hosted servers [10]. GamingOnLinux says the game previously used Easy Anti-Cheat and the developers appeared to be testing something else (press report) [13]; the product named on the current store page is Elytra [1].
- Moderation side: the Season 1 changelog added a report tracking system, weighted reports, and in-server announcements of cheater bans [2]; see technical-servers-foundation.
- Assessment: a kernel driver generally installs at game launch, needs administrator rights, and commonly conflicts with Linux compatibility layers unless the vendor enables Proton support. Confidence Low to Medium: this is general reasoning, not a WARDOGS-specific statement.

## WD-L020 and KB5124010

- The 0.1.2 post (30 Sep 2026) lists "Windows 11 'WD-L020' Crash Error Fix" as a key update, and states: "Fixed the issue caused by the latest Windows 11 update, KB5124010, causing the recent WD-L020 crashes." [5]
- It was part of a minor patch aimed mainly at XP and cash exploits and security issues, with about one hour of maintenance from 08:00 UTC [5].
- No official post describes the mechanism, which hardware was affected, or a pre-patch workaround. No source recommends uninstalling the Windows update; do not infer it.

text:
This document covers what a player or server admin needs technically for WARDOGS (Bulkhead / Team17, Steam app 1867240) in Early Access: official system requirements, anti-cheat, platform support, the Community and Official server browsers, how community servers are hosted, the admin and RCON tooling, and modding status. Version 1.2.0 is revised against the full text of the official Steam posts, the store data snapshot of 2026-10-08 and the live Steam store page capture of 2026-10-08 (system requirements re-checked against the 2026-10-30 store data and unchanged), now through Season 02, Update 0.2.0 (released 15 October 2026) [1][11][12]. Earlier history covers Season 1, patch 0.1.2 (30 September 2026) and the hotfixes of 2 October 2026 [7][8][9]. Update 0.2.0 added region-based ping limits and kicks, server seeding rewards, a punishment for community hosts seen exploiting the faction bonus, and "Server stability & security improvements" [11].

Headline facts. The store data lists Windows only, with Windows 10 64-bit minimum and a 1080p Low 60 fps (upscaled) target [1]. Patch 0.11 (deployed 14 September 2026) split the browser into Community and Official lists [6]. Bulkhead itself names three Approved Hosting Partners (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM) in its 8 September post, which resolves the earlier two-versus-three count conflict by dating [3]. Update 0.1.2 added a Deploy flow, restored Advanced Filters to the Official list and added scheduled restarts and RCON hardening for community servers [7]. The detailed RCON and ServerSettings.ini reference remains unofficial only, and predates 0.1.2 [17].

The Steam store page (live capture 2026-10-08) states that the game uses kernel-level anti-cheat, names the product as Elytra, and requires agreement to a third-party EULA named WARDOGS EULA [1]. It also shows Steam Deck compatibility as Unsupported [1].

Confidence is Medium. System requirements, anti-cheat naming, patch contents and the approved-host list are Primary. RCON and config detail, self-hosting status and netcode rest on unofficial material or are undocumented.

- Minimum: Windows 10 64-bit, Core i5-8600 or Ryzen 5 3500, 16 GB RAM, GTX 1660 or RX 590, 50 GB storage, broadband, targeting 1080p Low at 60 fps (upscaled); recommended is Windows 11, an i7-12700K or Ryzen 7 5700X with an RTX 3070 or RX 6700 XT (Steam store page, live capture 2026-10-08) [1].
- Platform flags in the store data are Windows true, Mac false, Linux false [1]. Linux is not officially supported: the developers said on 5 Sep 2026 they cannot commit to it and are still working on Proton compatibility (press report) [13].
- Anti-cheat: the Steam store page (live capture 2026-10-08) shows "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat: Elytra" and "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA: WARDOGS EULA" [1]. Context: Bulkhead's 8 Sep post says nothing about the technology ("you don't talk about anti-cheat") and points players to the in-game report function and community-hosted servers [3].
- Steam Deck compatibility is shown as Unsupported on the store page [1]. Bulkhead's Early Access estimate on the page is around 1 to 2 years, and the game is planned to be priced lower during Early Access (page lists GBP 36.99) [1].
- Three Approved Hosting Partners (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM), named officially on 8 Sep 2026, sell community servers [3].
- Patch 0.11 (announced 12 Sep, deployed 14 Sep 2026) split the browser into Community and Official, removed filters from Official, added text search for Community and made community server IDs persistent [6].
- Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026, maintenance 08:00 UTC for about one hour) added the Deploy flow (Official, Community, Infantry Mode, Low-Level), restored Advanced Filters to the Official list, and added scheduled daily restarts and an RCON AllowedHosts setting [7].
- A security and stability hotfix on 2 Oct 2026 (08:00 UTC, about one hour) had undisclosed specifics; a separate no-downtime balance hotfix followed the same day [8][9].
- Update 0.2.0 (patch notes 14 Oct 2026, released 15 Oct 2026): Official servers enforce region-based maximum ping limits with automatic kicks for sustained excess, community admins can configure their own ping limits, the browser gained maximum-ping tags and filters, players who populate empty servers earn rewards and a vendor discount, and community hosts seen exploiting the Lonestar faction bonus "will be punished". The notes say the initial ping values are "quite lenient" and give no numbers [11][12].
- A 15 Oct 2026 maintenance window ran 08:00 to 09:30 UTC (about 90 minutes of downtime estimated); the "now live" post says Update 0.2.0 is released and servers are back online [11][12].
- Press only: PCGamesN (27 Oct 2026) reports two new server hosts, GG Host and 1of1 Servers; no official post in the 2026-10-30 snapshot confirms this, so it is unconfirmed [15].
- No official RCON or ServerSettings.ini documentation was found; the detailed reference is unofficial and Low confidence [17]. No mod support is mentioned in the store data, and no modding plan was found in the official posts read [1].

- **Platform and requirements.** Windows only per the store platform flags; full specification is in Detail [1]. Early Access began on 10 Sep 2026 [1]. The store page's Early Access section says Bulkhead expects WARDOGS to remain in Early Access for around 1 to 2 years, that the exact duration may change, and that the game is planned to be priced lower during Early Access with a higher price at full release (live capture 2026-10-08) [1]. Steam Deck compatibility is shown as Unsupported [1].
- **Languages and features.** The store page shows 14 supported languages; English has interface, full audio and subtitles, French, Italian and German are listed in the page's first rows, and Spanish - Spain has interface and subtitles, with the rest behind "See all 14 supported languages" (the full list of Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Polish, Turkish and Ukrainian comes from the earlier store data snapshot) [1]. The features block lists Online PvP, Steam Achievements (10 on the page) and Accessibility Features (4), and the content line cites in-game chat and online interactivity [1].
- **Anti-cheat.** Bulkhead's 8 Sep post says the most important thing players can do is use the in-game report function on official servers, and that community-hosted servers give "the ultimate protection" because admins can instantly ban bad actors [3]. The 9 Sep changelog added a report tracking system with weighted reports [4]. The Steam store page (live capture 2026-10-08) states "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat: Elytra" and "Requires agreement to a 3rd-party EULA: WARDOGS EULA" [1]. No official text read describes how Elytra works, and this document makes no claim about its behaviour.
- **Linux.** Not supported. Store flags show Linux false [1]. Press reported the developers' 5 Sep clarification [13].
- **Server browser.** Two lists, Community and Official, since 0.11 [6]. 0.1.2 added Advanced Filters back to the Official list and a Deploy flow offering Official, Community, Infantry Mode or Low-Level servers [7]. Detail in server-hosting-and-browser.
- **Community server availability.** Bulkhead's 8 Sep post says community hosted servers were available to pre-order through "our 3 Approved Hosting Partners; QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM" ahead of the 10 Sep launch [3]. The hosts-only model itself (no self-hosting, server code withheld) is still known only from a fan site and a tracker, not from an official statement read [16][18].
- **Modding.** The store data mentions neither dedicated servers nor mod support [1].

text:
## System requirements (Steam store page, live capture 2026-10-08)

| Item | Minimum | Recommended |
|------|---------|-------------|
| OS | Windows 10 (64-bit) | Windows 11 (64-bit) |
| CPU | Intel Core i5-8600 or AMD Ryzen 5 3500 | Intel Core i7-12700K or AMD Ryzen 7 5700X |
| RAM | 16 GB | 16 GB |
| GPU | Nvidia GTX 1660 or Radeon RX 590 | Nvidia RTX 3070 or Radeon RX 6700 XT |
| Network | Broadband Internet connection | Broadband Internet connection |
| Storage | 50 GB | 50 GB |
| Additional notes (as shown) | 1080p Low @ 60fps (Upscaled) | 1440p Medium @ 70fps+ (Native) or 4k Medium @ 60fps+ (Upscaled) |

Source for the table: [1]. Both columns state a 64-bit processor and operating system requirement. The page shows no Linux requirements [1]. See system-requirements-and-performance for depth.

## Performance and settings changes at launch (Season 1 changelog, 9 Sep 2026) [4]

- DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without a restart; the render target pool is configurable.
- Shadow cache refreshes were reduced (less hitching when taking control of a character); shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores rather than switched off.
- Dropped items no longer affect navigation.
- Startup reliability improved with clearer early-failure messages and a recovery route; a legacy graphics dependency was removed.
- Crash fixes covered two frame generation paths, network calls scheduled off the game thread, a chatbox tooltip, buildables, and firing a weapon whose owner had left. GPU crash reports carry more detail.
- Voice chat recovery after a failed join and under load was improved, with a visible communication status.
- Launch day: a client hotfix on 10 Sep forced a restart and staged re-entry through the login queue to address players unable to join, unexpected kicks and long queues [5].
- Netcode: none of the official text read describes tick rate, prediction or lag compensation. This is a gap, not a finding.

## Moderation and anti-cheat systems

- Report tracking: reports are weighted so repeat and bad-faith reporters carry less influence; cheater bans are announced in server when match termination is off; the "kicked from server" message appears only for real bans [4].
- Economy abuse (patch 0.11 post): cash exploits get a timed ban plus a reset of cash and XP to 0; content that tutorialises exploits is treated as advertising cheats and risks a permanent ban; the developer states "We track every server you enter" and joining known XP farming servers for more than a few minutes risks a permanent ban [6].
- 0.1.2 (30 Sep): leniency for first-time offenders is declared over; players caught abusing repeatable exploits or Real Money Trading risk permanent bans without warning [7].

## Server browser timeline

| Date | Change |
|------|--------|
| 10 Sep 2026 (Season 1 changelog, 9 Sep) | Filtering reworked; Host a server button links to the hosting page; community image scaling fixed [4] |
| 14 Sep 2026 (0.11) | Community and Official browsers; filters removed from Official; text search and Show Empty/Full on the quick bar for Community; persistent, longer unique server IDs; server names ordered alphabetically with single spaces only; Asian capacity increased; 5% End of Match cash bonus on Community servers for one week [6] |
| 30 Sep 2026 (0.1.2) | Deploy flow (Official, Community, Infantry Mode, Low-Level); Advanced Filters restored to Official; long names no longer truncated; queue position shown after Join; gamepad support on the Deploy screen [7] |

| 15 Oct 2026 (0.2.0) | Maximum ping tags and filters added to the server browser; region-based ping limits on Official servers [11] |

## Update 0.2.0 server rules (patch notes 14 Oct 2026; released 15 Oct 2026) [11][12]

| Topic | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|-------|------------------|-------------------|
| Ping limits | Not stated in the posts read | Official servers enforce different maximum pings by region; initial values "quite lenient", numbers not stated |
| High-ping kicks | Not stated | Players who "consistently exceed" the limit over a sustained period are kicked; server-side lag spikes are excluded; kicked players cannot rejoin that server until the next map transition |
| Community servers | Not stated | Admins can configure their own ping limits (cross-regional play or stricter rules) |
| Seeding | Not stated | Players who join and populate empty servers earn rewards and a vendor discount once the match begins (values not stated) |
| Faction bonus | Not applicable | Lonestar cash and XP bonuses are Season 2 only; community hosts "seen to exploit the faction bonus will be punished" (penalty not stated) |
| Stability and security | "Various server stability hotfixes" [7] | "Server stability & security improvements" (no detail) |

Team switching, forgive and punish are covered in control-zone-and-match-flow.

Planned but not shipped per the 0.11 post and not announced as shipped in 0.1.2 or the 0.2.0 notes read: community server favouriting, tiered priority queues, Message of the Day prompt, improved warmup activities, disabling AFK kicking during seeding, team switching controls [6][7].

text:
Source warning: Bulkhead has published no server-admin manual that was found. Only the 0.1.2 admin changes below are official; the RCON and config reference is unofficial, predates 0.1.2 and is labelled Low confidence.

**Hosting model.**

- Official: community hosted servers are sold through three Approved Hosting Partners, QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM, per the 8 Sep 2026 post [3]. The in-game Host button links to the hosting page [4][6].
- The 2-versus-3 conflict is resolved by dating: a fan site relaying evidence checked on 1 Sep 2026 said two unnamed hosts had passed launch standards [16]; a tracker updated 14 Sep 2026 says three [18]; the official post of 8 Sep confirms three and names them [3].
- Player-reported only: the fan site says server code will not be released for everyone to host (citing performance and security) and the tracker says RCON access depends on the host's panel [16][18]. No official statement of a hosts-only model, or of the absence of a downloadable dedicated server, was read in the snapshot. Consequence for admins: you probably cannot run your own SteamCMD or Docker server; confirm with your host. Detail in server-hosting-and-browser.

**Admin changes confirmed in 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026, official)** [7]:

- Scheduled restarts: a daily restart time can be set (UTC).
- RCON AllowedHosts setting to restrict who can access RCON.
- RCON message and broadcast lengths are capped.
- RCON now defaults to Standard response detail instead of Full, and config responses no longer expose server internals.
- ServerImageURL is checked when the config loads.
- Since 0.11, community server IDs persist across map changes and restarts and are longer for security reasons [6].

**Unofficial RCON and config reference** (wardogs.tech, self-described as not official docs, version 0.39, written before 0.1.2; player-reported, Low confidence) [17]:

- RCON is plain HTTP REST with JSON, base `http://<host>:<port>/v1/`, default port 7776 (`-RCONPort=`), no TLS, so the password crosses the network in clear text.
- Authentication is `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>`; one token has full read and write access with no read-only role. The listener is off by default (`bEnabled` in `[/Script/WDRCON.WDRCONSettings]`).
- Endpoint groups: status, players, bans, config, rotation, capabilities; writes include kick, kill, message, ban, broadcast and match map/end/restart. `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document and supports `If-Match` revision checks.
- Listed `ServerSettings.ini` keys include `ServerName`, `ServerPassword`, `ServerImageURL` (1024x256), cash and level min/max limits, `MaxReservedSlots` (default 20), `MaxPlayers` (listed default 128), `MinimumRequiredPlayers` (default 60), KOTH `ScorePeriod` (default 24 s) and map rotation (`Ordered` or `Random`).
- Several endpoints were reported removed in build ++Wardogs+Live-CL-501228 (2026-09-14) in favour of the config document [17]. Because the reference predates 0.1.2, response detail defaults and config output may now differ (the official 0.1.2 notes say Standard detail is now the default and config no longer exposes internals) [7].
- Assessment: because RCON as documented uses one shared secret over unencrypted HTTP, the official AllowedHosts setting [7] should be used and RCON kept on a private network or behind a TLS proxy. Confidence Low to Medium: the AllowedHosts fact is official, the transport detail is unofficial [17].

**Third-party tools** (player-reported, not endorsed): Warcon, an open-source (MIT) self-hostable multi-server RCON panel with per-admin roles and audit log [19]; BattleMetrics has reportedly added WARDOGS RCON support [18]. The guide at [18] was written by Warcon's builders, so its recommendations are promotional. See rcon-and-server-admin.

**Restart timers.** Host guides disagreed on any built-in restart timer (12 h versus 24 h of uptime); this is unverified. The only official restart statement is the configurable daily UTC restart time in 0.1.2 [7].

**Modding.** The store data lists no mod support [1]. No official modding toolkit or plan was found in the official posts read.

**Client notes.** Windows only [1]; Linux unsupported [13]; Windows 11 update KB5124010 caused crash WD-L020, fixed 30 Sep 2026 [7].

text:
This document goes deeper than the parent foundation on WARDOGS aircraft (all helicopters in Early Access) and the systems that counter them. Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, patch notes 14 Oct 2026, live 15 Oct 2026) is the first official source with numbers for most of this topic [9][10]. It adds the Flakpanzer Gepard as a vehicle-mounted anti-air option (Driver level 25, $300,000 unlock, $14,000 spawn), cuts the build cost of the Talon 9K-SAM (1,000 to 650 supplies) while slowing its reload (2 s to 5 s), cuts the Vanguard CIWS build cost (1,500 to 1,200), makes the Little Bird AH-6M [Miniguns] unlock later and cost more, raises the vendor price of every listed armed helicopter, and makes helicopter cockpit glass work both ways [9].

The Season 1 position (Update 0.1.2 plus the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix) is kept as dated history: the CIWS time to destroy a Havoc was halved from about 12 s to about 6 s, and IR Rangefinders were pulled from the vendor until Season 02 [3][4]. The notes also describe the Infrared Range Finder as battery-powered (about 80 s of active use) [9].

Confidence is Medium. Every Season 02 number is Primary, but the Season 1 roster, levels and anti-air costs came only from conflicting player guides, several levels are still not stated by any official post (Lakota, Havoc, AH-6R, MH-6), and sling-loading remains unconfirmed. The 2026-10-30 snapshot has no official post after 2026-10-15 [10].

As of Update 0.2.0 (15 Oct 2026).

- Season 02 went live on 15 Oct 2026 after a maintenance window of 08:00 to 09:30 UTC [9][10].

- Base-built anti-air changed: Talon 9K-SAM 1,000 to 650 supplies and Vanguard CIWS 1,500 to 1,200, all build supply costs [9]. The wider build-cost and Talon rebalance is owned by fob-and-base-building.
- The Little Bird AH-6M [Miniguns] moved to Pilot level 8 for $125,000. The notes say it "was too strong for how early it unlocked" [9].
- Purchased-vehicle inventories are private to the driver and their squad by default, which includes purchased helicopters; free team-spawn vehicles stay open to everyone [9].
- A vehicle's smoke screen and flares now appear for players who joined late [9].
- The Infrared Range Finder now runs on batteries: about 80 s of active use per battery, draining faster if toggled quickly on and off [9]. It is priced at $3,200 (was $1,200) [9]. Whether it is back on sale in the vendor is not stated in the notes; the 2 Oct 2026 post said it was disabled "until Season 02" [4].
- The Steam store page (live capture 2026-10-08) promotes ferrying supplies to teammates by helicopter and lists "new vehicle types including fighter jets" among planned additions, with no date or roster [1]. The 2026-10-30 store data still carries the helicopter line [2]; the fighter-jet wording is not present in that data, and no official post says it was dropped or kept [2].

Reward values are owned by cash-rewards-and-costs; they are shown for the air-combat trade-off only. Armed variants give 1.5x the XP of the default variant, and repair XP now goes into the pilot or driver track depending on the vehicle repaired [9]. The Gold Market gains a "Black & Gold" Little Bird camo and a "Two-Tone Desert" Havoc camo [9].

## Counter-air options (0.2.0)

| Option | How it is obtained | 0.2.0 facts | Source |
|--------|--------------------|-------------|--------|
| Flakpanzer Gepard | Driver track, level 25, $300,000; $14,000 at vendor | New in 0.2.0; destroyed reward $7,000 | [9] |
| Talon 9K-SAM | Base-built; build cost 650 supplies (was 1,000) | Reload 2 s to 5 s; restock from munition supplies 50 to 200; destroyed reward $2,000 to $650 | [9] |
| Vanguard CIWS | Base-built; build cost 1,200 supplies (was 1,500) | Cannon damage against structures retuned ("shreds light cover and struggles against heavy fortifications"); 2.25x longer to kill the Spawn Vehicle; destroyed reward $3,000 to $1,200 | [9] |
| Smoke screen and flares | Vehicle equipment | Now appear for late joiners; flare deployables took more loadout room since 10 Sep 2026 | [9][5] |

The notes give no damage, range, ammunition or seat figures for the Gepard, Talon or CIWS against aircraft, and do not say which hammer builds the Talon or CIWS. The Season 1 foundation placed anti-air among Large Hammer builds and Ammo as the supply for CIWS and SAM (player-reported) [15]. One Season 1 guide gave the CIWS build cost as 901 supplies [14]; the 0.2.0 notes give the old value as 1,500, which conflicts, so the 901 figure is not used (the notes may be counting a different supply type, no source says).

## Helicopter combat and handling changes (0.2.0)

- Cockpit glass: "now works both ways", shooting out through it damages the vehicle the same as incoming fire [9].
- Calibre base-damage cuts (.308 -25%, 7.62x54mmR -20%, 7.62x39mm -19%, .50 Cal -16%) apply to vehicle weapons, and the notes name the Little Bird AH-6M Minigun and the Z20 Lakota Minigun. The notes do not say which round those miniguns fire, so which cut applies is not stated [9].
- MGL-40 on the Little Bird bench seat: much more inaccuracy and sway, slower ADS and a reload penalty "to reduce reliability" [9].
- Parachutes: slower to open and will not open below about 10 m; opening below roughly 50 m while falling fast means fall damage. The notes add "Make sure you trust a pilot before getting into their aircraft" [9]. Basic Parachute $100 to $500, Sport Parachute $1,000 to $700 [9].
- Exiting a vehicle now places the player on the ground rather than pushing through it [9].
- Handling changes in the notes are for tracked vehicles, the Humvee and the Dune Buggy; no helicopter flight-model change is listed [9].

| MH-6 about $6,250 | Season 1 | player-reported [12]; no price in [9] |

The Season 1 guides say transport helicopters carry no offensive armament and that a free large transport helicopter and an SUV appear at team spawn a few minutes into a match (player-reported) [12][13].

## Press conflict of 2 Oct 2026 (history)

The official post "IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix" (15:39 UTC) is separate from the "Security & Stability Hotfix" announced for 08:00 UTC that day [4][6]. InGameNews reported that the 2 Oct hotfix had no gameplay changes, which is true only of the security hotfix [6][11]. Timesaver.gg and MMOEXP (player-reported) reported the IR nerf and the CIWS 12 s to 6 s change, which match the official post [4][16][17].

## Sling-loading

Unconfirmed. The official posts including the 0.2.0 notes, the Steam page and both vehicle guides never mention it; guides describe supply drops from the seat (`G` drops a crate) [12][13][9]. The store page's helicopter supply ferrying is not described as sling-loading [1].

text:
This document goes deeper than the parent foundation on forward operating bases (FOBs), the three hammer tiers, supply types, buildable structures and pallet logistics. Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, notes posted 14 Oct 2026, live 15 Oct 2026) gave the first official structure costs, so the document now tabulates the 0.2.0 values with their Season 1 predecessors where the notes state them [11][12]. Season 1 (0.1.2) values remain as dated history.

The official Building Balance section is "a full pass on build costs, build speed and durability" [11]. It adds three buildables (MG Nest, Large Shelter, Wooden Step), raises most supply costs, makes the Medium Hammer contribute less per swing, severely cuts Drill Rig uptime, slows the Talon and Mortar, and lets the Halligan bar breach doors and gates while hammers no longer can [11]. FOB hacking now also pays teammates in the radius, and destroying a FOB pays a bonus based on the supplies it held; cash and XP amounts are owned by cash-rewards-and-costs [11].

Not stated in the 0.2.0 notes: hammer unlock levels and prices, the FOB vendor price, structure health, build radius and FOB count limits, and whether Season 1 hammer values were changed. The notes do not mention a progression wipe. Confidence is Medium: costs and changes are official and Primary [11], but the build procedure, hammer-to-structure mapping for older structures and supply types still rest on player-reported guides [8][9][10].

## Update 0.2.0 Building Balance

Source: Season 02 patch notes, posted 14 Oct 2026, live 15 Oct 2026 [11][12]. All figures below are build supply costs unless stated; "old" is the Season 1 (0.1.2) value the notes give. Where the notes show only a new value, old is "not stated".

| Buildable | Old (0.1.2) | New (0.2.0) |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| Wood Base | not stated | 15 |
| Bremmer wall | 15 | 32 |
| Door | 22 | 80 |
| Gate | 85 | 200 |
| Large Shelter | not stated | 250 |
| Air raid shelter, bunker, crow's nest | 100 | 200 |
| L81 Mortar | 150 | 600 |
| Stingray | 150 | 650 |
| MG Nest | not stated | 650 |
| Talon 9K-SAM | 1,000 | 650 |
| Vanguard CIWS | 1,500 | 1,200 |
| Hot Zone Magnet | 2,250 | 2,750 |

New buildables and the hammer that builds them [11]:

| Buildable | Description (notes) | Built with |
|-----------|---------------------|------------|
| Wooden Step | "A step. Made of wood." | Small Hammer and above |
| Large Shelter | large metal shelter for covering key assets or keeping the rain off | Medium Hammer and above |
| MG Nest | manned M2 Browning emplacement | Large Hammer |

Build speed [11]: the Medium Hammer now contributes less per swing; critical spots give a smaller bonus than before; the Large Hammer build rate per swing is unchanged. Numeric rates are not stated. The stated aim is to make structures "a considered investment rather than something you spam" without hard limits on player freedom [11].

Drill Rig (severe cut to active time, to stop multi-rig builds dominating) [11]:

| Setting | Season 1 (0.1.2) | Season 02 (0.2.0) |
|---------|------------------|-------------------|
| Minimum fuel to activate | 1,500 | 2,000 |
| Duration per fuel | 0.05 (max uptime 375 s) | 0.03 (max uptime 300 s, "matches capturable towers") |
| Max fuel | 7,500 | 10,000 |
| Post-spawn cooldown | not stated | "substantially increased"; a destroyed rig cannot immediately be replaced |

Buildable weapons [11]: Talon reload 2 s to 5 s and restock from munition supplies 50 to 200; Mortar restock from munition supplies 75 to 150 ("to reduce the amount of shots that can be fired per pallet drop-off") and a new firing animation where the player drops the shell in as it fires, slowing fire rate.

Misc building changes [11]:

- Barbed wire and sandbags can be placed on top of Bremmer walls; barbed wire no longer gives cash or XP on kills.
- Foundations fit against slopes, stairs and walls; unfinished buildables collapse as soon as they lose a support instead of floating; tank traps can only be placed on a defined set of surfaces.
- Doors and gates can no longer be breached with a hammer; the Halligan bar can now breach both (Halligan breaching rewards, uses and vendor price: see cash-rewards-and-costs [11]).
- CIWS cannon damage against structures was "properly tuned": it shreds light cover and struggles against heavy fortifications, with no numbers stated [11]. Separately the Vanguard CIWS now takes 2.25x longer to kill the team Spawn Vehicle [11].

FOB hacking and destruction (amounts in cash-rewards-and-costs) [11]: hacking a FOB now also rewards teammates in the FOB radius (the hacker's own reward is unchanged); destroying a FOB pays a bonus based on the supplies it held, maxed at 25,000 supplies. Destroying a buildable now pays cash equal to its build supply cost, with XP about 25% of the cash, scaled by how built it is, and its XP is now assault XP rather than support [11]. FOB Supplied Assist is split between assisting players [11]. The notes state cash and XP pay amounts for these rewards; see cash-rewards-and-costs for the table rather than a copy here.

Logistics note [11]: base logistics rewards are lower, with new delivery streaks; the notes were edited after posting to give values including the Control Zone multiplier. Values: cash-rewards-and-costs.

## FOB price and mechanics

The vendor price is the only officially published FOB number; the raise was made so the FOB and Large Hammer are "more of a choice" [1]. Official posts describe the FOB as a way to fortify a chokepoint and list building as an Early Access feature [3][4]. Player-reported procedure: deploy the kit on valid ground, not inside a building, a main base or another FOB's radius; deposit supplies into base storage through the FOB console; choose a structure from the build wheel; finish it with the hammer [8]. FOBs do not refill by themselves [9]. Enemies reaching the FOB console can reportedly hack the base, with a siren [8]. FOB count limits, radius and health are not published.

## The four supply types

All four are player-reported [8]; no official post names them.

| Supply type | Used by (player-reported) |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| Build | Structures; $10 each or $500 per 50 [8] |
| Ammo | Mortar, CIWS, SAM [8] |
| Fuel | Refuel Station, Drill Rig [8] |
| Mechanical | Repair Station [8] |

Official text confirms only supply crates as a purchasable item class (Pilot small armoured supply crate, Driver Large Supply Crate, Kodiak Flatbed) [1] and that helicopters can ferry supplies to teammates [4].

## Hammer tiers and unlocks

| Tier | Unlock | Structures needing the tier (player-reported) |
|------|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Small | Default; $100 (player-reported) [8][9] | Sandbags, barbed wire, hedgehogs, Recon Tent; no FOB needed [8] |
| Medium | Support track, $25,000 (official) [1]; level 3 (player-reported) [8][9] | HESCO, doors, gates [8] |
| Large | Support track, level 8, $75,000 (official) [1]; vendor $2,400 (official) [1] | Bunkers, Recon Towers, mortars, anti-air, Repair and Refuel Stations, Drill Rig [8] |

The required tier reportedly applies only to starting a blueprint; any hammer finishes it [8]. Hammers switch to Dismantle on finished objects and also repair [9].

Conflict resolution:

- **Level 7 versus 8.** The Season 1 changelog states "Large Hammer: level 7 to level 8" [1]. One guide still gave level 7 [9]; that is the pre-Season-1 value. Level 8 is the baseline.
- **$800 versus $25,000.** The official changelog gives $25,000 as the Medium Hammer Support unlock (previously $10,000) and as the former Large Hammer unlock, now $75,000 [1]. No retrieved official or press text gives an $800 hammer price. Any $800 figure is unsupported here; see Open Questions.
- **Vendor versus unlock.** The Support track gates the right to buy the hammer ($75,000, level 8), and the vendor charges $2,400 for a Large Hammer [1]. Whether the vendor price recurs per purchase is not stated.

## Buildable structures and costs

Official 0.2.0 costs for named buildables are in the Building Balance section above [11]; there is still no complete official structure list (Repair and Refuel Stations, Drill Rig, sandbags and hedgehogs have no stated build cost). The earlier player-reported figures (Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901, Drill Rig 1,351) [9] disagree with the official old values and are retained only as history. Repair Stations repair and Refuel Stations refuel vehicles from stored supplies; the Drill Rig is reported to pull the Hot Zone toward a fuelled FOB [10]. Gates admit vehicles, doors are infantry-only, hedgehogs block vehicle routes [9]. Official: the CIWS was rebalanced on 2 Oct 2026 [5].

## Pallet delivery and the 0.1.2 reward reduction

Pallets are the logistics unit for moving supplies into a FOB; cargo vehicles carry small amounts and larger loads move on pallets (player-reported) [9]. Update 0.1.2 states: "Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone now awards reduced rewards" [2]. A press summary lists the same change among the cash and XP exploit fixes [7]. The size of the reduction and the zone boundary are not published. The post frames the change as anti-exploit and warns that players abusing repeatable exploits risk a permanent ban [2]. Supply crate sale XP was cut separately in Season 1 [1].

## Build-destroy interaction

Official: "Any rewards for destroying buildables now scale with their build progress - so destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward" [2]. Rocket launchers can take down apartment blocks per the store page [4]. Player-reported: anything built can be destroyed, artillery can level fortifications from outside the zone, and unprotected pallets can be destroyed [8][9]. For diffing: reward scaling is by build progress, with no published curve.

Update 0.2.0 (Season 02, released 15 Oct 2026) is the first official source that states vehicle spawn prices, and it states both the old and new value for most of them [1][2]. The Season 02 patch notes (posted 14 Oct 2026) add four vehicles (Wolf-110, Wolf-110 [M2 Browning], T-72B3 and Flakpanzer Gepard), raise the vendor price of 10 listed existing vehicles (Kodiak [M249], two armed Humvees, two Ural Defenders, the L2A6 and four helicopters; plain and unarmed variants are not listed), move several Driver and Pilot unlock levels and costs, make purchased-vehicle inventories private by default, and fix a list of vehicle bugs [1]. Season 1 (0.1.2) values are kept below as dated history.

The notes use the vehicle names "Ural Defender", "Ural Defender [M249]", "Humvee [Minigun]", "L2A6" and "SPH-2", while the Season 1 changelog used "URAL Covered", "URAL Attack", "Heavy Tank" and "Artillery Tank" [3]. Matching the two name sets is Inferred from identical levels and prices (see the reconciliation table). The notes still publish no crew or seat counts.

Document confidence is Medium: every number below comes from official posts, but the name mapping is inferred, several unlock levels are not stated, and crew sizes are unpublished. The 2026-10-30 snapshot contains no official post after 2026-10-15 [2], so later hotfixes are neither assumed nor excluded.
